  answering `removed` as for one on the box: `text` as the agent would have read it, `words` as
  shown, `keyword`, `draft` for the composer, `files` as a send takes them (`{uri, name?}`), so Edit puts them back and they can
  go again; 404 when the agent took it first (or it isn't waiting anywhere), 502 when the engine
  still holds it, 503 while it can't be read.
- Clients show what's held and whether it's paused from these; the in-flight record of a message
  still on its way stays with the client that sends it, which names those in Stop's `items` (it
  doesn't wait for them), and waits for its hold before it asks the box to resume.
- **Where a client draws a message** (#809), by its id, in one place from the moment it's sent until
  the conversation has it: one `items` lists for the agent's next step (`delivery: "steer"`, `on:
  "engine"`, not `held`) in the conversation, saying it's for the next step (with Send Now, Edit and
  Remove); the rest of `items` in the queue over the composer. Its own message the box hasn't listed
  yet goes where sending it puts it (a send in the conversation, one for after the run in the
  queue); one `items` listed and no longer does was handed to the agent and stays in the conversation
  until its copy comes. Nothing under it while it's on its way.
- **A send whose answer was lost** (its computer restarting, the connection dropped) is asked again
  under its id (`kuvo/sessions/<id>/draft` takes one id once). One an earlier link was partway
  through when it stopped is settled then, not left unknown: answered as sent where it reached its
  conversation (its inbox, its messages, or what waits on the box), else sent now; what was typed
  for the box (`/`, `!`) stays unknown, for you to check.
- A legacy box without `queue` cannot serve this route. Older clients held it until
  it's up to date, never carried by a client.

### A conversation's asks

What a conversation waits on you for (`sessions.asks`), worded by the box as the cards over the
composer show it, so a client draws each card and works nothing out: every permission and question
waiting in the conversation and its subagents, on the engine or the coding agents' bridge, but one
Auto's reviewer took up; and what the box asks you itself for them (`sessions.asks.box`): a command
outside the sandbox, something from the vault. Those wait in the box's long-running process, which
answers these routes: another (`box route`, a machine's kept server) passes the list and an answer
to it over `run/vault.sock`, and with none listening (or one from before, answering `404 {}`)
lists what the engine asks alone. A client never takes the box's own asks' first answer as the
default (Return): only its number or a click answers one.

- `GET kuvo/sessions/<id>/asks` → `{"asks": [ask…]}`, oldest first, those a client answers
  ahead of those answered elsewhere (`other`, below), so the card it can answer shows first. Each has `id`, `kind`,
  `session` (the session asking: a subagent's own) and `title`:
  - `permission`: `{message, command, files, resources, choices}`. `title` as the Mac's card says
    it ("Allow editing src/App.swift and 2 more?", "Allow running this command?"); `message` the
    engine's words, or null; `command` the whole command line the tool call runs (a shell's), or
    null; `files` the changes it would make, `[{file, patch, additions, deletions, status}]`
    (`status` `added`, `deleted`, `modified` or null); `resources` what it covers as the card shows
    them (from the conversation's folder where inside it, folders outside it as people know them,
    `~/notes`); `choices` its answers in order, `[{answer, title, named, placeholder}]`: `once`
    "Allow Once", `always` (its `title`, then `named`, what Always saves, shown as code: "Always
    Allow" `git push`; null where it names nothing, "Always Allow Edits"), `reject` "Don’t Allow",
    `instead` "Tell It What to Do Instead…" with the line it opens (`placeholder`). Each choice
    also has `help`, what it does whole (Always's hover text: "Don’t ask again before running git
    push commands in this project", "… in this conversation" for a coding agent's), and `spoken`,
    the button as a screen reader says it ("Always allow working in Home, notes"); either null
    where the title says it all. `protocol/vectors/always-words.json` holds Always's words. A
    client shows `command` in place of `resources` when it has one.
  - `question`: the agent's questions (a form whose fields are all words or choices, none shown
    only after another answer), `questions: [{key, title, question, options: [{value, label,
    description}], multiple, custom, required}]`, asked one at a time: `multiple` takes several,
    `custom` takes words of your own (one with no choices does), `required` needs an answer.
  - `sandbox`: a command it or a subagent asks to run outside the sandbox ("Sandbox", "Asks"),
    `{message, command, stopped, error, asker, why, choices}`: `title` "Scout wants to run a
    command outside the sandbox"; `message` what stopped it ("The sandbox stopped it from changing
    a file outside Scout’s folder."); `stopped` what the sandbox refused, `[{label, detail}]`
    ("Write", `~/.npm/_cacache/x`); `error`, where it can't say (Linux), the error the command got,
    else null; `asker` and `why`, who asks and in its words. `choices`: `once` "Allow Once",
    `always` "Always Allow" naming the one place it keeps (`named`, `after` "in every chat" for the
    chats') where the box names one, and `reject` "Don’t Allow", each with `help` and `spoken`.
  - `vault`: what it or a subagent asks of the vault ("Vault"), `{need, message, site, note,
    choices}`: `need` `use` ("Scout wants to use GitHub token": `once`, `always` where it may be
    given for good, as its `always` says, and `reject`) or `item` ("Scout needs an OpenAI API
    key": for each item in the vault, `once` "Give" and `always` "Always Give" naming it, with its
    `item`, those for its `site` first, then `reject`). `message` its words or null, `site` the
    site it's for or null. Only the vault's clients (a phone, this Mac's app, the Mac proving
    itself) are offered answers: to another, `choices` is empty and `note` says where to answer it.
    Items are listed only while it's unlocked; `note` says why there are none, else null. A choice with `confirm: true` makes a grant: a client makes sure it's
    you first (Touch ID, the device's password), as a grant made in Settings does, and one that
    can't doesn't offer it.
  - `other`: anything else it waits on you for: a form a card can't take (an MCP server's: one
    filed under no session, `global`, in the conversation's folder, is its own once one of its
    steps, or its subagents', runs a tool of that server, as the Mac's conversation takes it; fields
    a card can't take). `message` says what it asks; `dismiss` says whether it can be put away
    unanswered from here.
  `404 {"message"}` for no such session here, `503 {"message"}` while its place isn't answering.
- `GET kuvo/sessions/<id>/asks/events` (ndjson): the same now, and again as an ask comes, is
  answered, or its run ends (as the long-running process notes them, looked at each second, and
  every 15 s at least); nothing while its place isn't answering, so
  what it said last stands. Through `box route` it answers its first line.
- `POST kuvo/sessions/<id>/asks/<ask>` answers one, to the place and session that asked: a
  permission with `{"answer": "once"|"always"|"reject"}`, or `{"answer": "instead", "message"}`
  (Don't Allow with your words, which the agent reads); a question with `{"answers": {<key>:
  "words" | ["choice"…]}}`, only what was answered (the box adds the form's defaults for the rest),
  or `{"dismiss": true}` for any form; the box's own with one of its choices, `{"answer":
  "once"|"always"|"reject", "item"?}` (`item` as the choice has it), never put away unanswered. The
  sandbox's goes to it as `POST kuvo/sandbox/asks/<id>` would (`reject` is `no`), the vault's as
  `POST kuvo/vault/asks/<id>` would, only from the vault's clients (`403` otherwise, `423` to give an
  item while it's locked). `200 {}`; `404 {"message"}` when it isn't waiting any more;
  `400 {"message"}` for an answer that doesn't fit (a choice it doesn't offer, a required one
  missing, words for `other`); `409` when the session is held or has moved; `503` while its place
  isn't answering, `502` when it refused.

Permission and form replies go over a live client connection to the current owner. They are
excluded from the peer mutation and message queues. A reconnect uses the current pairing and
pending request ID. A cold restart, restored or moved copy, or replacement prompt supplies its
own live state. Bridge handover can preserve the same pending native request when the live turn
transfers and the request has already replayed. Reply requests never wait for the bridge or the
pending request to reappear. Addressed SSH replies also check the current setup trust for the
pairing. A local permission restriction takes effect on the owning Box before a grant is sent,
and the bridge checks current runtime Blocks before resolving a pending approval.

Setup membership grants and revocations are accepted through the primary's setup save path.
Full Access confirmation, starting work from other computers, Settings › Permissions, the
sandbox's allowed paths and the vault's consent are enforced by the Box where the work runs.
Session approval modes and native Always answers remain scoped by their local writer. Local OS
access and vault unlock are separate grants at that computer. A pairing or setup save cannot
supply them. Backup restore still requires fresh consent for local permission grants.

### Tool steps

What a step of the agent's shows when it's opened, which every client draws from the engine's
message alone (a step is `{type: "tool", id, name, state}`; `state` has `status`, `input`, and once
it's done `content` and `metadata`). The engine's own tools, and the coding agents' as their bridge
names them, by the same names (`bash`, in a conversation from before the engine named it, is
`shell`). Sample steps: `protocol/vectors/tool-steps.json`, which only the desktop
client (gpui) tests against for now; the phone is to hold itself to it too.

| Tool | Its target (on its row) | Opened, it shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `shell` (`bash`) | `input.command`, its first line | `input.command` whole, then its `content` text (what it printed): once it's `completed` (nothing printed says so), or one that failed having printed something |
| `edit`, `multiedit`, `patch`, `apply_patch`, `write` | `input.filePath` (or `path`) | each of `metadata.files` (`{file, patch, additions, deletions, status}`) as a diff of its unified `patch`, with `+additions −deletions` on the row |
| `grep` | `input.pattern` | its `content` text (what it found); one that found nothing opens to nothing |
| `glob`, `list`, `ls` | `input.pattern` (or `path`) | its `content` text, as `grep` |
| `websearch` | `input.query` | its `content` text, as `grep` |
| `read`, `webfetch`, `task`, `todowrite`, any other | as its name says | nothing more |

Any step whose `metadata.files` holds a patch opens to it, whatever its name. A step still
`running` (or `streaming`, `pending`) opens to nothing. A long output folds to its first lines.

**A failed step is one short line** (`messages.tool-failures`, #949), whatever agent ran it: each
page of messages a box forwards gives a step that `failed` (`error`) `failure: {line, reason,
error}`. `line` is its row, in the step's own words and nothing else ("Ran 1 command · blocked",
"Read 1 file · not found", "Linear · List issues · timed out"): what it did, counted as a group's
line counts it (or its `title`), and `reason`: `declined` (you said no), `stopped`, `blocked` (a
hook, the sandbox, a permission), `timed out`, `not found`, `exit code N`, else `failed`. `error`
is all it said (its `error`, else what it printed), its wrapping tags (`<tool_use_error>`) and
repeated "Error:" out. Closed, a client draws `line` with a small warning mark and nothing under it
(never the error, a tag or a path); opened, the command and `error` as its output, or `error`
under what the step opens to. A step read live before its page is read again has none: its row as
it was, its error once opened.

**Every other step's words are the box's** (`messages.tool-titles`): each page of messages a box
forwards (`GET api/session/<id>/message…`, the engine's and the coding agents' alike) gives each
step that isn't one of the engine's own (above, and `subagent`, `execute`, `context`, `skill`,
`question`, `todoread`, `codesearch`, `lsp`, `batch`, `invalid`, `plan_enter`, `plan_exit`) two
strings on the step itself: `title`, what it did ("Started a session", "Sent a message to Mira",
"Linear · List issues"), and `doing`, the same while it runs ("Starting a session"). A client draws
them as they are, never the step's `name`, which is an MCP tool's id (`kuvo-browser_start_session`,
`linear_list_issues`) or a bridge's kind (`sleep`, `generate_image`). Kuvo Code's own tools say what
they did in their own words, kept beside each one's definition (which also gives its MCP `title`
in `tools/list`), with the agent named where the call's input has a name (never an address); another
MCP server's are `<server> · <tool>`, the server by its integration's or catalog's name, or its
own made readable, the tool's name made readable without the server's name again; a name of no
server the box knows is made readable whole. The live feed carries none of these: a client reads the
messages again as a step arrives. Samples: `protocol/vectors/message-words.json`.

**How a client groups them** (the desktop app's; a view, so every client does the same): the
steps between two blocks of the agent's words, thinking included and across its messages, are one
group. Anything else that shows (your message, a note, a turn's end, a step's error) ends it, and
so do words. A group of two tool steps or more folds to one line until it's opened: each kind
once, in the order it first came, counted ("Read 4 files, ran 2 commands, searched twice"): files
read or edited counted once each by their target, `shell` as commands, `grep`, `glob`, `list`, `ls`
and `websearch` as searches ("once", "twice", "3 times"), `webfetch` as web pages, `task` and
`subagent` as subagents, `todowrite` as "updated its plan", a step with a `title` by its title
(`×2` when it repeats), and any other as tools; past four kinds, "and N more steps". While a step
is under way, the line says it as that step's does, then the rest. Folded, a step that `failed`
still shows under the line, and so does the last one under way in the conversation's last group
while the conversation waits on you (an ask), with "Waiting for you".

### Mentions

What "@" and "&" suggest as you type in a conversation (`sessions.mentions`), ranked by the box as
the Mac's composer ranked them, so every client shows the same list.

- `GET kuvo/sessions/<id>/mentions?for=files|agents&q=<typed after the mark>[&limit=<n>]` (8
  unless asked, 20 at most) → `{"mentions": [{text, title, detail, kind, session}]}`: `text` goes
  in the message in place of what was typed (and a space), `title` is shown, `detail` beside it
  (or null), `kind` `file`, `folder`, `bot` or `session`.
- `files`: the conversation's folder's files (as `kuvo/folders/tree` lists them) and its project's
  other folders' (each folder itself first, its files after its name). The name itself first, then
  names starting with what's typed, names containing it, then paths containing it; among equals
  the conversation's folder's, then shorter paths. Nothing typed: the folders, then the newest
  files. `text` `@<path>` (from the conversation's folder; another folder's after its name, a
  folder with a trailing `/`), `title` its name, `detail` the folder it's in (null at the top).
- `agents`: who `kuvo/named` lists, but the conversation itself. Case and accents aside: the name
  itself, then names starting with it, a word in a name starting with it, names containing it, then
  projects containing it; past a space only names that go on that way; equals in the list's order.
  Nothing typed: the list's first. `text` `&<name>`, `detail` as the Mac's list says it (a bot's
  job, else "Bot"; a session's project, "Chat" for a chat, else "Session"; then " · on <computer>"
  for one on another), `session` its session, which a client puts in the send's `named`.
- `400 {"message"}` without `for`, `404 {"message"}` for no such session here, `503
  {"message"}` while its place isn't answering. A folder that can't be read suggests nothing.
- In a group chat, "&" asks `GET kuvo/groups/<id>/mentions?q=<typed after the mark>[&limit=<n>]`
  (`groups.mentions`, on the box the chat lives on; 8 unless asked, 20 at most, in all) → the same
  `{"mentions": [...]}`: the chat's own bots first (as its list has them), `detail` "In this chat"
  (then " · on <computer>" for one on another), `session` its conversation or null where that
  computer didn't say; then the guests a message there can name, who `kuvo/named` lists but a
  chat's bot (by conversation, or by name, so each name is offered once), as `agents`
  words them. Each part ranked as `agents` ranks, so a guest never comes before a chat bot; a
  bot that left the chat is a guest. `404 {"message"}` for no such chat here, `503 {"message"}`
  while the coding agents' bridge that runs the chats isn't running or answering. A client
  filters nothing itself, and puts in `text` (the chat reads "&<name>", never a send's `named`).

### A session at a glance

What a session's row and its card show beyond the session itself (`sessions.glance`): a row gains
one mark, its pull request's (else its branch's), only on a session with a branch of its own or a
pull request; its card (hover on a Mac, a long press on a phone) says the state and how long ago,
the branch, the model, effort and account, and the pull request with its checks and size.

- `GET kuvo/sessions/glance?sessions=<id>,<id>…` (at most 200) → `{"sessions": {<id>: {branch?,
  additions?, deletions?, pull?: {number, url, state?, additions?, deletions?, checks?: {passed,
  failed, pending}}, account?: {name, label?}, asked?}}}`. A session the box doesn't have is left
  out (only when every place said it has none: `503 {"message"}` while one isn't answering, rather
  than say it's gone); `400 {"message"}` for none named, `503` with neither the engine nor the coding
  agents' bridge running. `GET kuvo/sessions/glance/events?sessions=…` sends the same now (ndjson),
  and again when it changes: an ask coming or answered and a pull request linked (a moment after, so
  a few at once are one line), and once a minute for the rest; nothing while a place isn't
  answering, so what it said last stands. A
  client follows it for the rows on its screen only, and opens it again as they change; through
  `box route` it answers its first line, and a client asks again a minute later.
- `branch`: the session's own, a worktree's of the box's (`box/worktrees.json`), else its pull
  request's head branch; left out for one in its project's own checkout, whose row stays as it is.
  `additions` and `deletions`, without a pull request: the lines its branch changed since it left
  its base, uncommitted changes too (`kuvo/git/changes/count`'s `branch` scope).
- `pull`: the pull request it made, else, in a worktree, its branch's latest on origin's GitHub
  repository (open, merged or closed) from origin's repository itself (not a fork's branch of the
  same name) and made since the worktree was (not an earlier branch's of the same name). It made it
  when Create Pull Request named it (`kuvo/git/pull-request` with `session`), or when its own `gh pr
  create` (or one of its subagents') printed it, which the box catches as the call ends: a command
  that starts with it (or after `&&`, `;`, `|`), the last pull request it printed, and only on the
  host of the session folder's origin. Kept in `box/pulls.json` (the latest 500), so two sessions in
  one folder never show each other's. `state`: `open`, `draft`, `merged` or `closed`, with
  `additions`, `deletions` and `checks` the pull request's, as GitHub last said; all left out until
  GitHub's been read, or when it can't be (only `number` and `url`). `checks` counts the last commit's check runs and statuses: skipped and neutral ones as
  passed; failed, errors, cancelled, timed out, stale and those needing action as failed; the rest
  pending. Left out for none.
- GitHub is read with GitHub's own `gh` on the box and its sign-in (Kuvo Code keeps no key of
  GitHub's for it): one GraphQL query for every pull request asked for at once, only while a client
  asks, and each only as often as it can change: once a minute while its checks run, every five
  minutes while it's open otherwise (or a worktree's branch has none yet), every half hour once it's
  merged or closed. Kept in `run/glance/github.json` (two hours), which one process at a time
  writes, so a box asks GitHub once however many processes and clients ask it. A box without `gh`,
  or signed out, reads nothing for five minutes, then tries again.
- `account`: the account it runs on, as `kuvo/work` says one ("Work"); none on Custom Auto.
- `asked`: while it waits on you, when the oldest ask still open came (ms), its subagents' too: a
  permission or a question (not one Auto's reviewer took up), or what the box asks you for it (a
  command outside the sandbox, the vault), as the box's long-running process heard it
  (`run/glance/asks.json`). An ask is let go as it's answered, as its run ends or it's deleted, and
  with all of its place's (engine, bridge) once that place is heard again after it couldn't be. An
  ask made while the box couldn't hear it has none, and a client says how long since the session
  last changed instead.
- What a client draws from it (which mark, which lines on the card) is the clients' to decide
  alike; a box without `sessions.glance` gives no marks beyond the worktree's branch, as before.

### Session context

`GET api/session/<id>` and `GET kuvo/agents/api/session/<id>` can include
`data.context: {used, window?}`, in tokens. `used` is the last occupancy reported by the agent
or measured from its latest model request, with cached input included. `window` is the capacity
reported for that model by the agent or its catalog. Session detail can also include
`data.contextWindow` with the capacity in tokens before usage is measured or after a summary. The
box remembers a known capacity across turns and restarts. Usage may be absent before a measurement
or after a summary. Cursor's SDK supplies billing usage and does not expose its context capacity
or measured occupancy. Session `tokens` still describes usage across the conversation.

`kuvo/agents/api/session/<id>` adds `summarizeAt` to it, in tokens, where the box's
"Summarize long conversations at" setting (`kuvo/settings/conversations`) decides when the
conversation is summarized by itself: Claude Code, Codex and Grok, unless the choice is `never`
(Claude Code under a 900k window still summarizes at 400k) or above 85% of `window`, where the
agent's own margin decides. Where it's absent, a client draws no mark. Clients draw used of window
with a mark at `summarizeAt` (the desktop app's Activity, as a strip and on its pinned card).

### Session lists

What each session is, and where every client's lists show it (`sessions.list`): the box decides it
from its engine's and coding agents' sessions, so a client draws its sidebar from facts and works
nothing out. The route requires `sessions.list`. A box that reports `held` shows
its update view. A temporary `503` leaves the list waiting.

- `GET kuvo/sessions/list[?since=<at>]` → `{at, full?, sessions: {<id>: facts}, gone?: [<id>],
  projects: {<folder>: {name?, updated?, asking, working, shown?, total?, more?}}, projectOrder?, startProject?, needsYou: [{session, asks}],
  archivedGroups: [{directory, title, kind, sessions: [id]}], pending?: ["bridge"]}`. `…/events[?since=<at>]` (ndjson) sends that now, then
  a line as anything in it changes; through `box route` (a machine reached over SSH) it answers its
  first line, and a client reads it again as that machine's sessions change and every half minute.
  `503 {"message"}` while the engine can't be read; `405` for anything but `GET`. `pending`: the
  coding agents' bridge runs but couldn't be read yet, so its sessions are as last read (none are
  said gone for it).
- `projectOrder` and `startProject` (`sessions.list.start`) are whole on every line. The box
  orders projects by the latest session, then by project name in sidebar order, then by directory.
  The initial project for a new conversation is the first in that order, or null for Chats.
  An explicit project or Chats pick takes precedence. The starting place stays put while the
  user writes.
- `archivedGroups` (`sessions.archived-groups`) is whole on every line, including deltas.
  Both Settings › Archived Sessions and the desktop archived sidebar draw these groups and
  session ids in the supplied order. The box includes archived project, chat and bot sessions,
  excluding away copies; sessions are newest first (ties by id), grouped by kind and filed project
  or directory, groups in first occurrence order. `title` is Chats for chat groups, otherwise the
  project's name or directory basename. Clients never reconstruct this list from facts.
- The box keeps the list in `run/lists/sessions.json`: its long-running process works it out as its
  engine's and bridge's events come, from each read whole as it's heard (and every five minutes),
  and only once the engine's has been, and again a moment after the box's projects, worktrees,
  bots or moves change, whichever process changed them (a `box route` over SSH too: it watches
  their files). A `box route` reads that file while that process runs, and never writes it then;
  otherwise it reads the engine itself and keeps what it read there.
- `at` says where the list is; `since` resumes from it: only the sessions that changed after it,
  and `gone`, those deleted since. A cursor the box can't resume from (it restarted, or the change
  is older than the day and 2000 deletions it keeps, or its file went) gets the whole list, `full: true`, in place of
  what the client had. `projects` and `needsYou` are whole in every line.
- Facts, each flag left out where it isn't: `kind`, `project` (a `project` session's), `directory`,
  `title?`, `created`, `updated` (ms; latest conversation activity, or creation for an empty
  session; the lists' order), `parent?` (a `subagent`'s session),
  `subagents?` (#950: a session's subagents' sessions, those at work or waiting on you first, then
  the newest), `messages?` (#950, a `subagent`'s: how it takes your messages, `{via: "direct" |
  "parent" | "none", note?}`, its `metadata.kuvo.messages` as the engine routes say; `none` with `note`, why, in words to
  show; the engine's own subagents `direct`),
  `pinned?`, `archived?`, `running?`, `asked?` (since when it's waited on you, ms, as "A session at a
  glance" says it), `away?` (this copy isn't the box's own: moved away, or on its way here, "Moves"),
  `bot?` (`sessions.needsYou`: the bot it is, by its id: whose conversation it is, as `kuvo/bots`
  lists it, else the one it works for, "Work"'s `kuvo.by.bot`, which may live on another
  computer; never on a `subagent`). Since `bots.state`: `thinking?` (`true`: while it's at work,
  its model has been reasoning a while, debounced as "What a bot is doing now" says), `blocked?`
  (`"error"` or `"limit"`: it stopped on one and you haven't read the turn it ended, or it has been
  retrying one a while), `retrying?` (`true`: it's `blocked` by a retry, while it's at work),
  `unread?` (when its turn you haven't read ended, ms: its `time.idle` while
  that's later than `time.viewed`, "What's been read"; an agent's work the box reads for you isn't
  unread while the box judges whether that turn is news to you). The box hears these as they stream
  and reads no session for them.
  A kind a client doesn't know shows nowhere.
- `kind`, in this order: `subagent` (it has a `parentID`); `seat` (`kuvo.seat`, a bot's seat in a
  group chat); `hidden` (`kuvo.engineFor` or `kuvo.reviewPart`: a run its session or review shows);
  `bot` (one of its bots' conversations, as `kuvo/bots` lists them, or anything in its bots folder);
  `chat` (marked a chat naming the folder it's in, or in its chats folder, "Chats"); else
  `project`, filed under the project of its folder as `kuvo/projects`' `worktrees` says, by the
  worktree's Git common directory, or by a worktree record the engine still has. Otherwise it
  uses the project `kuvo.filed` names while it still runs in that folder (as that project is
  filed), then its own folder ("Projects").
- `projects`: every project of the box's list that isn't removed or filed as a worktree, and each one a `project` session
  that isn't archived is filed under (a removed one comes back so), with its list's `name` where
  it has one, and `updated`, its newest such session's. `asking` and `working`
  (`sessions.needsYou`, #711): how many of its sessions listed (not archived, this box's own copy)
  wait on you, and are at work; one that waits isn't counted at work, here or anywhere the box
  counts (a session asking does nothing until it's answered). A client draws its project's badge
  and spinner from these and counts nothing.
- A project's list a page at a time (`sessions.list.pages`, #951): each project says its list's
  first six sessions in the order it shows them (`shown`: pinned, then those at work or waiting on
  you, whenever they last changed, then the newest; ties by id), how many it lists in all
  (`total`: its `project` sessions not archived), and what "Show more" adds next (`more: {cursor,
  count}`, none once all show). `GET kuvo/sessions/page?project=<folder>&cursor=<more's cursor>` →
  `{project, sessions: [<id>], total, more}`: its list as far as that cursor goes, in that order;
  each "Show more" adds twice as many as the one before (10, then 20, then 40…, 5000 in all at
  most). A client keeps the cursor it asked with and asks again with it as the list's line for
  that project changes, so a page follows the list; "Show fewer" is the first six again. `400` for
  no project, or a cursor this box didn't give. A client draws `shown` or its page in that order and
  never sorts, slices or counts a project's sessions itself. Their facts still come on the list's
  lines (the client's search and lookups read them there).
- `needsYou` (`sessions.needsYou`, #711): the sessions waiting on you that the lists show (a
  `project`'s and a `chat`, not archived, this box's own copy), the one that asked last first
  (`asked`, ties by id), each `{session, asks: {kind, summary}}`: what its oldest ask still open
  asks, in the box's words, written to follow the session's or its project's name ("asks to run a
  command", "asks to edit 3 files", "asks to edit App.swift", "has a question for you", "asks to
  run a command outside the sandbox", "asks for something from the vault"; "waits on you" where
  the box heard no more; a file's name or an action's own words are cut at 60 characters). `kind`: `permission`, `question`, `sandbox`, `vault` or `other`; a client
  shows `summary` as it is, whatever the kind. A client draws "Needs you" from it, in its order,
  and works out neither who waits nor what for. A bot's own conversation isn't here: it's its
  bot's (`now` in `kuvo/bots`).
- What a client draws: a `project` session in its project and a `chat` in Chats, unless archived;
  a `subagent` under the session that started it (its `subagents`), while that session or one of
  them is open, or while it's at work or waits on you; any other kind nowhere. Pinned and Chats newest first; projects by their newest session shown,
  those with none last, ties by name (its `name`, else its folder's last part; Finder's order:
  case-insensitive, numbers by value); a project's sessions newest first. Archived is the box's
  `archived`, wherever the session was archived (here, on a phone, by Remove Project). A client
  shows a pin it just made at once, from the session it holds, and an archive (or a session
  brought back) it just made, or the sessions Remove Project's answer names, from a note on its
  copy of the list. A note is kept through lines until one naming that session says the same
  (or lets it go, or a whole line comes), and dropped if the engine refuses the change; one made
  while another of the client's is still on its way is kept even where the list already agrees.
  A move between computers (`away`) is the client's to place, as it sees every computer's list.
- `protocol/vectors/session-lists.json` holds engine sessions and what the box knows
  beside them, the facts the box answers (`box/test/session-lists.test.ts`), and the
  sidebar a client draws from them (KuvoClient's `SessionListsTests`): a client in another language
  checks itself against it.

### Computer display words (`computers.words`)

Each `kuvo/computers` row has `title`, the display title of its `reach` value
(“Connected”, “Connecting”, “Can’t be reached”).
For an unavailable reach (`away` or `connecting`), `detail` gives a short
explanation and `notice: {title, detail}` supplies the named notice shown in Computers;
`settingsNotice: {title, detail}` is the same standing in words about its settings, shown
where its settings would be (a box that sends none: `notice`). Connected computers have neither. `workingTitle`, present whenever
`working` is present, words that count (including zero), such as “1 session at work”.
Clients draw these words; `reach` and `working` remain the values used for behavior.
The same fields are sent in `kuvo/computers/events` snapshots.

### App reach display words (`computers.reach-words`)

Each computer also carries `reachTitles`, a map of display words for the app’s own
reach states: `connecting`, `held` (an update is needed), `away`, `notPaired` and
`unreached`. A client’s direct connection may stand differently from the
answering computer’s connection; it selects the matching supplied title instead of
writing a title itself. The capability is gate-required.

### Box display names (`names.titles`)

Computers include `limitServices: [{id, title}]` alongside the legacy `limits` ids. Clients draw each title unchanged. The box names known services by their plan (ChatGPT, SuperGrok, Copilot, OpenRouter, Z.ai, Ollama, OpenCode Go); unknown service ids have their initial letter capitalized.

Work sessions include `account.title`, the complete short display name including the account label where present ("Claude · Work", "Copilot"). Unknown providers retain their supplied account name. Usage answers include `serviceTitles`, a map from each service id in `services` or `totals` to its spend card title ("OpenCode", "Codex"); unknown ids are capitalized word by word. Clients draw these words unchanged.

### Computers

Your computers as one list (`computers`, #711), from any box, a Mac's or a machine's, with no
client connected: a client's Computers area and its switcher draw it, and ask no Mac for it
(`kuvo/machines` names only what a Mac's app connects to over SSH).

- `GET kuvo/computers` → `{computers: [computer…]}`: the box that answers first (`here: true`),
  then its peers by name ("Peers"). Each:
  - `key` (its box's public key; `""` for the box itself while it has none), `name`, `kind`
    (`mac` or `machine`), `id?` (a machine's name on its Mac);
  - `reach`: `connected` (the box itself; a peer heard from in the last half hour), `connecting`
    (a peer not heard from yet since this box knew of it, or being reached again: Connect, below,
    asked in the last 20 seconds and no word since), `away` (the relay said it isn't
    there, `run/peer-reach.json`, or nothing came from it for half an hour). As this box last heard: one that's itself
    off the relay still says `connected` of a peer heard in the last half hour;
  - `kuvo?`: the installed version of Kuvo on that computer.
  - `version?`, `engine?`, `system?`: the desktop app’s version on a Mac (Kuvo’s on a machine), its engine’s, and its system as
    people know it ("macOS 15.1", "Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS"), as that box said them with its agents
    (`agents.computer`, "Peers"); left out for one that hasn't said;
  - `features?` (`computers.facts`): what its box answers, as its `kuvo/info` says (this box's
    own) or as it said with its agents: as advertised. The box supplies the row’s compatibility projection ("The update gate"). Left out for one that hasn't
    said, and one whose list is longer than peers keep
    (300 names, "Peers"): it can't be said what's missing then, and a client doesn't call it older;
  - `via`: `here` for the box that answers, or `relay` for a peer;
  - `address?` and `relay?` (`computers.reach`, #742): where a client of your own reaches that
    computer's box itself: its address on the relay (base64url, as its setup's peers document
    names it; the box's own from its relay secret) and the relay's URL, the one this box reaches
    it through. With the box's key (`key`) that's all a paired device needs to open a session
    there ("Sessions"), so Kuvo Code's desktop app connects to each of your computers directly
    and no box relays for another. Left out while this box has no relay;
  - `working?` and `atWork?` (`computers.facts`): how many of its sessions are at work
    (conversations, not their subagents, never one that waits on you), and which, newest first,
    each `{id, title?}` (its session's id on that computer, and its title): its own from its session
    list (the first 100), a peer's as it last said (the first 20; a peer tells which as they change,
    at most once a minute). `0` and `[]` for one that's away (nothing there can be seen at work
    now); both left out for one that never said: a client says nothing of what's at
    work there, never "nothing";
  - `limits`: the services whose plan limits it reads (`claude`, `codex`…), as the answering
    box's limits rows say (`rows[].boxes`); `[]` while its coding agents' bridge doesn't run.
    `limitServices` (`names.titles`) carries the same services as `[{id, title}]`; clients draw
    `title` unchanged ("ChatGPT", "SuperGrok", "Claude"). Unknown ids have their initial letter
    capitalized. `limits` remains for older clients;
  - `actions` (`computers.manage`): what can be done with it from this box now, in the order to
    offer them, `{id, label, confirm?, why?}`, as accounts' are ("Signing in"): `label` the
    button's words, `confirm` `{title, message, label}` where a client asks first (its question,
    what it comes to, its button), all the box's; `why`, it can't be done now, in words a client
    shows beside it, its button not taken (asked anyway, it's refused with those words). `rename`
    changes the accepted name of a managed setup computer. `connect` retries an away peer, and
    `remove` asks the primary to unlink a member. In a setup, `remove` carries `removal: {choices,
    last?, handOver?}`, the removals the box allows: `choices` of `unlink` (`POST …/unlink`) and
    `wipe` (`POST …/unlink-and-wipe`); `last: true` where it's the only computer of its setup, so
    it can only be wiped (`choices: ["wipe"]`); `handOver`, on the main computer of more, the
    box's words for who takes its role first. A client offers exactly those, and no removal where
    `removal` is missing (a 0.7 Mac's record outside a setup). `update` (`computers.update`, below: Update
    Now, with its `confirm` while something may be at work there) on a machine this box keeps up to
    date. `update-here` (`computers.update.here`: Update Now, `POST kuvo/update {now: true}` of this
    box, with its `confirm` while sessions are at work) on this box's own row while a release Kuvo
    Code here offered waits. `add` (`computers.update.here`), "Set Up Over SSH…", on an older machine
    (by its version, or heard from and saying none) that this box could add but didn't set up over
    SSH, so it can't bring it up. A client draws the ids it has a control for.
  - `update?` (`computers.update`): `{state, title, detail, long?, action?}` on another computer whose Kuvo
    is older than this box's and that follows its peers ("Updates", Your computers follow each
    other): "Kuvo on <name> updates in a moment" (`waiting`, nothing to press), a Mac or a machine
    alike, and once this box has seen it behind for a day (since its link started), "Kuvo on <name>
    hasn’t updated yet" (`long: true`); on a machine whose Kuvo this box brings up to its own (Keeping them up to date, below): `waiting` for nothing to be at work there
    (`long: true` once that's been over a day), `updating`, or `failed` (tried again by itself
    later); `title` and `detail` the box's words, which a client shows as they are. Left out where
    there's nothing to bring up, and on every other box. Clients use `update.action` for the
    update control and confirmation. Its `id` selects the Box update route or opens Add a
    Machine for `add`, using the supplied `address` when present. The feature gate continues
    to use each Box's announced features. On this box's own row
    (`computers.update.here`): how its own update to a release Kuvo Code here offered stands,
    "Kuvo on <name> updates once your sessions there finish." / "… updates as soon as nothing’s at
    work there." (`waiting`), "Kuvo on <name> updates in a moment." (`waiting`), "Updating Kuvo on
    <name>…" (`updating`), "… tries its update again in a while." (`waiting`: it failed once, put
    back or not), "Kuvo on <name> couldn’t be updated to <version> after 2 tries." (`failed`: a
    version newer than the box failed here twice in a row, `offerFailed.tries`, whether an offer
    waits or not: it isn't taken by itself again until a newer one comes); `update-here` (Update
    Now, which takes the release offered here, else the newer one held in `updates/release`, else
    GitHub's newest; asked first where it restarts the engine) only with that last one, or (`long: true`) a release that restarts the engine that has
    waited a day for nothing to be at work: nothing to press while it takes the release by itself. Left out while none waits, or while it can't update (blocked, its engine
    stopped on purpose, an update on trial). On an older machine this box could add but didn't set
    up over SSH (`add`, above): "Kuvo on <name> needs an update. Set it up over SSH from <this box>
    to update it." (`waiting`).
  - `appCheck?`: on this Mac's own row, the Kuvo version this Mac runs while it's newer than the
    desktop app that last registered with `kuvo/box/app` ("Updates", This Mac's app follows): that
    app looks for its own update, once for each version. Left out on every other row and box.
  `405` for anything but `GET`.
- **Managing them** (`computers.manage`, #735), from any box, with no client or Mac's app open. A
  machine's record (its name, that it's one of your computers) is in the signed peers document of
  the computer that set it up ("Your setup"). The primary writes the setup’s accepted membership and names.
  Outside a setup, a legacy machine can use the one Mac that set it up as its writer. A Mac's box reaches only its own machines, never another Mac,
  so on a Mac that's a member of another Mac's setup nothing is offered, and asked it says to do it
  from the main computer (a known gap until a member Mac can hand it on). A box that isn't the writer hands what you do to it by mail,
  as a Work Queue item's change goes to the computer that keeps it ("The Work Queue", Done where
  it's kept: `{workQueue: {act: {id, area: "computers", method, item: <key>, body?, at}}}`, answered
  `{acted}`), once the writer's agents name `computers.manage`, and answers with what it said; the
  change reaches every computer with the writer's peers document. Two boxes renaming at once are
  done in turn there: neither change is lost, and of two names for one machine the later is kept.
  Each is the same done twice, so one the writer took and was cut short by a restart is done again
  when it's asked again (never answered as in doubt, as a Work Queue item's change is).
  - `PATCH kuvo/computers/<key> {"name"}`: renamed (1 to 100 characters, spaces and control
    characters folded): `200 {name}`. The writer keeps it apart from what its app says of its
    machines (`peerNames` in link.json), so the app saying them again keeps it (one missing from
    its list for a moment too), until the app names it otherwise (renamed there) or it's removed; a machine lists itself by the name its writer's
    record gives it.
  - `DELETE kuvo/computers/<key>`: removed, as a Mac's app removes one: off the writer's peers
    document, named among those you removed (`left`, which the machine hears and lets that Mac go),
    and off that Mac's list of machines (`machines.json`); its app listing it again
    (`kuvo/link/peers`), or setting it up as it connects (`kuvo/link/setup?key=`), doesn't bring it
    back (`removedHere` in link.json). Adding it again over SSH creates a new membership with a
    fresh box key, signing key and relay address. If saving the
    machines list fails, the removal still revokes access and the request reports the incomplete
    change. It keeps running there, as a box of its own, with its sessions.
    Device pairings belong to the setup and continue to reach its remaining members.
  - **Unlink and wipe** (`computers.removal`, #904). `POST kuvo/computers/<key>/unlink`
    leaves the sessions and bots on that computer in a new standalone setup.
    `POST kuvo/computers/<key>/unlink-and-wipe` also schedules their deletion with Kuvo Code.
    Both take an optional client-generated `operation` (16 random bytes in base64url) and return
    the accepted membership receipt plus `removal: {operation, state, accessRemoved}`. The
    same operation or the original receipt in `save` returns the same current removal result. A legacy standby-backed receipt can still be pending (202). The primary commits the unlink without contacting the target and
    publishes the updated roster and device grants. If the target is the main and other members remain, the box arranges an eligible replacement before committing. Unlinking the only computer wipes it, leaving no setup. On layout 21 and later,
    an accepted removal of the last computer in a standalone layout can include
    `offer: "reinstall-local"` while the wipe is pending. The app-owned Mac layout offers
    reinstall through installer status once its last-computer wipe has completed. An ordinary
    disconnect gives no such receipt.
    `GET kuvo/computers` and its events include `wipePending: [{key, name, operation}]` while a
    wipe remains unconfirmed. A returning target challenges the current primary and verifies
    its signed instruction for the operation, setup, epoch, and target before acting. This
    exchange does not restore peer access. An unlink acknowledgement follows verification that
    the target's Kuvo engine and agent sign-ins and integration keys have been cleared.
    A wipe target runs the preparation hook and verifies
    any configured pre-wipe backup before stopping Kuvo Code and again before deleting its folder. A removed
    member with automatic Relay backups enabled requires a verified removal export in place
    of the automatic wipe backup. Its daily point is preserved, and Relay continues to deny
    access to the revoked member. A plain wipe in this case returns `review` with
    `removal.nextAction: "choose-export"`. Submit `prepare.export` with the **same** operation
    on `unlink-and-wipe` from the local desktop on the main Box. The result and
    `wipePending` entry say why the wipe is held. If a move-only plan was already accepted,
    `nextAction: "revise-export"` uses a new operation plus `supersedes`. Include the desired
    move destination in the replacement plan to preserve that choice. Unsupported layouts can
    report `review` with `nextAction: "cancel-wipe"`, which keeps the data and completes unlink.
    A member with the canonical app-owned layout deletes that app's validated Application
    Support directory and does not get a last-setup reinstall offer. The source reports
    completion after deletion. Layout 12 keeps a completion receipt outside the wiped folder.
    Relay retries and the SSH Add probe can deliver the operation-bound acknowledgment. A
    confirmed lost disk can close a pending wipe with `resolve: "lost"` and the existing
    operation. This records the loss and permits a fresh enrollment while retaining both old
    key revocations. The removal continues to report `lost` after a fresh enrollment.
  - **Prepare removal** (`computers.wipe-preparation`, `computers.removal-operations`, #905). Before unlink or wipe, the local
    desktop can ask `POST kuvo/computers/<key>/removal-plan` with optional `projects` (absolute
    paths on that computer). The source returns its current inventory in `plan`, including
    move destinations, active moves, export-only items, child sessions and categories that
    stay behind. `complete: false` means the listed `unresolved` work or stores could not be
    verified. An unreachable source
    returns 503. Only explicitly selected project folders appear in the plan.
    To save data first, send `prepare: {moveTo?, export?: {destination, recoveryKey, projects?}}`
    with the wipe's `operation`. Accepted membership keeps the operation and a hash of
    its choices through primary changes. The recovery key and paths live in private
    preparation journals on the boxes doing the work. After a primary change, re-send the
    original choices if the source hasn't received them yet. The desktop generates and keeps a 32-byte base64url recovery
    key before sending an export choice. A disk destination is an existing folder outside Kuvo
    on the source, or select a current backup computer with the existing SSH destination shape.
    In layout 12, revocation commits before preparation. The removed source can transfer the
    accepted inventory to the selected destination over removal-only mail. The destination
    can confirm that operation over the same channel when ordinary peer reachability is stale.
    Each move has its
    own accepted change identity and a destination receipt. Sessions with attached child
    sessions can be exported. If both choices are made, the archive captures the remaining
    source work after the moves. The source binds readiness to the version of that work and
    the selected projects. A SQLite checkpoint or close leaves this version unchanged when
    the committed data is unchanged. Changes invalidate readiness, including changes detected after the
    primary sent its grant. The source verifies the archive again and checks the generation
    after stopping Kuvo before deleting its folder.
    Session attachment names are opaque, and Work Queue attachment records select their
    payloads. A missing listed file or a size mismatch holds a requested export in review. The source
    checks the selected attachment bytes against the bytes written to the archive before
    publishing it. Removal-only progress for a ready export includes `inventoryVersion: 1`.
    A main Box that understands this field requires it for a new export grant and asks for
    another verification rather than resending a saved grant without it. A receipt already
    in flight can still settle that operation.
    An accepted preparation failure reports `review`, an error, and unresolved IDs when known.
    Retry after correcting the problem with `retryPreparation: true` and the original operation.
    Before deletion is authorized, `resolve: "cancel"` keeps the source work and finishes unlinking.
    A replacement `operation`, `supersedes` naming the prior operation and a new `prepare`
    replace the plan while access stays revoked. Completed moves retain their ownership
    decisions. The `export: {source, id, at}` reference, destination and key open through the
    existing restore route with the same replacement approval rules.
  - `POST kuvo/computers/<key>/connect`: this box's own, for a peer that's `away`: its link tells
    that computer its agents now, asking for theirs (`run/reach-again.json`, sent by the process
    that holds the relay connection, as `box route` leaves it), so its answer marks it back
    (`noteHeard`), and it's listed `connecting` for 20 seconds meanwhile. `202 {}`; `503` while this
    box is off the relay itself.
  - **While the old app is attached** (the Mac app before 0.8, which keeps its own list of machines
    and writes all of it back, `machines.json` and `kuvo/link/peers`, so a removal there wouldn't
    hold): the box that writes a machine's record takes no removal, from a client of its own or
    handed from another box: `409 {"message": "Quit the old Kuvo Code app on <Mac> first: it keeps
    its own list of machines, and would add <machine> back."}`, and its `remove` says so meanwhile
    (`why`, those words). It tells its peers so with its agents (`computer.oldApp: true`, "Peers"),
    so theirs say it too, within a minute (not while that Mac is away: it's away then). Renaming
    goes on: the old app keeps a name it didn't change. The box counts the app attached while it
    follows `kuvo/link/status/events` (which only that app does), and for a minute after it says
    its link's config (`kuvo/link/config`, the first thing it does as it attaches, again too).
    Once a Mac's box has moved out of the old app's folder (its move's record says it's done,
    "Moving this Mac's box"), the old app opened again is out of date and in charge of nothing:
    every `kuvo/link/…` route it asks is answered `410 {"message": "Kuvo Code 1.0 has replaced this
    app on <Mac>. Quit it and move it to the Trash: everything it did is in Kuvo Code now."}`, it
    never counts as attached, and nothing this box does itself (adding machines, keeping them up
    to date, Update Now, removals) waits on it.
  - The writer checks what's handed to it as the asking box does: a machine shared with another
    setup is renamed and removed only from that Mac itself (`409`).
  - Your phones are given a machine by the name you gave it (`kuvo/hosts`, from the box while the
    old app isn't open).
  - Refused in words a client shows as they are: `400 {"message"}` for a name that isn't one, `404`
    for a key that isn't one of the computers this box lists, `409` for what isn't offered there
    (with why: a Mac, the box itself, not the writer's machine, a writer
    that needs a newer Kuvo Code, already connected or being reached), `503` where the writer can't
    be asked now (it isn't answering, this box is off the relay, or no answer came in time, so
    whether it was done can't be told), and `405` for another method.
- `GET kuvo/computers/events` (ndjson): the same now, and a line as it changes (a peer's word, one
  going away or coming back, this box's sessions starting or stopping work, and every 15 seconds
  for the rest); through `box route` a client asks again instead.
- **Adding one** (`computers.add`, #636): a box adds a computer over SSH itself, for whichever
  client asks, with no app: a client sends an address, draws the box's steps and words, and
  answers what it asks. (Before, a Mac's app did all of it: `kuvo/machines`, which stays the old
  app's.) SSH is used to set a computer up, set it up again and uninstall it, never after: the
  computer's own keeper runs it, and boxes talk through the relay ("Peers").
  - **Who adds**: the primary, with a relay and keys for its link and its release files. A legacy
    Mac outside a setup can still enroll computers. Members forward adds to the current primary.
    A Mac while the old app is attached to its box answers `409` (that app keeps its own list).
    The rest return `503 {message}`, a list of machines
    that can't be told among them: read as `kuvo/machines` reads it ("Machines": there and won't
    read, or not there while `phone-link.json` keeps machines), so no computer is added over a
    list that's only missing (#753). `GET kuvo/computers/add` says the same as `can: false` with
    `why`.
  - `GET kuvo/computers/add` → `{can, why?, hosts, tries}`: `hosts`, the `Host`s of the box's
    computer's `~/.ssh/config` and the files it includes (names only, never a pattern), 50 at
    most, those not an address of a computer it set up; `tries`, those under way first, then the
    last few that are over. `GET kuvo/computers/add/events` (ndjson) follows it.
  - `POST kuvo/computers/add {"destination", "replace"?}` → `202 {try}`. A destination is what `ssh` takes: a
    Host's name, a host's name or `user@host`; one with `:`, `/`, white space or a leading `-`
    (a port, a path, an IPv6 address, an option) is `400 {message}` and never reaches `ssh`. One
    being added or set up at that address already is answered as it is; one being stopped is
    waited for, and the new try runs after it; `409 {message}` while that computer is being
    uninstalled. On a machine the kept server runs the attempt for local, SSH and relay clients.
    If an installation matches a saved computer fingerprint, Add updates that computer's
    position and membership history. The probe hashes the operating system or hardware UUID on
    the enrolled computer with the setup ID as a salt. The raw ID stays on that computer.
    When automatic evidence is missing, `replace` explicitly selects the most recent membership
    of the same computer by its key. A name or SSH address alone does not establish identity.
  - **A try**: `{id, kind, destination, name, state, title, steps, question?, failure?, computer?,
    known?}`. `kind` is `add`, `setup` or `uninstall`; `state` is `working`, `asking`, `stopping`,
    `failed` or `done`; `steps` are `[{id, title, state, detail?, sent?, total?}]`, each
    `waiting`, `now`, `done` or `failed`, with `sent` of `total` bytes while it copies (and
    `detail` saying the same in words, "41 of 98 MB"). Adding
    and setting up again have `checking`, `files`, `engine`, `starting`, `seeding`, `joining`; uninstalling
    `checking`, `removing`, `forgetting`. `failure` is `{title, message, again}` (`again`: trying
    again could go otherwise); `computer` `{key, name}` once it's one of yours (`known`: it was
    here already, at another address, which is kept as one of its addresses: told by its
    `machine-id` and, where its card says it, its box's key, so a copy of another machine's disk is
    a computer of its own). Every word is the
    box's. Kept in `run/adding.json`: a box that started again says a try was cut short, and
    never takes it up again by itself.
  - **What it asks** (`state: "asking"`, `question: {id, title, message, at, facts: [{label, value,
    code?}], answers: [{id, label, kind}]}`, `kind` `primary`, `plain` or `danger`), answered with
    `POST kuvo/computers/add/<id>/answer {"answer": <an answer's id>, "at"}` → `200 {try}` (`409`
    when it asks nothing now, or not that). `at` is the ask's number, which a client sends back:
    an answer that names another ask (a late one, for a fingerprint shown before), or none, isn't taken:
    - `hostKey`: the host's key isn't known. The box reads it as `ssh` reaches the host (your
      config's port and jump host), offering no key and no agent to a host not trusted yet, and
      shows its fingerprint (`SHA256:…`). `trust` keeps it in the box's own
      `~/.kuvo-code/ssh/known_hosts`; your `~/.ssh/known_hosts` is read, never written.
    - `hostKeyChanged`: the key differs from one the box kept. `trust` puts the new one in its
      place: the old key's line goes, with every other key kept under that host's name. A key that differs from one in your own known hosts is never asked about: the try
      fails, saying to remove it with `ssh-keygen -R`.
    - `recoverAccount`: an earlier attempt left the SSH account marked in use and no remote
      command holds its write lock. `recover` checks the lock and the mark again, then gives the
      account to this attempt. Commands from the earlier attempt can no longer write there.
    `cancel`, on each, stops the try.
  - `DELETE kuvo/computers/add/<id>` stops one under way (at its next step: what it runs there
    now ends first, and its start is never cut short; it says `stopping` meanwhile, then leaves
    the list), or forgets one that's over: `200 {}`, `404`. One stopped, or failed, after it
    started on a computer that had nothing of Kuvo Code and before it's one of yours, is taken
    off there again (stopped, its start after a restart removed, the keys and sign-ins copied
    there deleted), and a failure's words say so; where that couldn't be done the try fails,
    saying it may still run there.
  - Adding, updating, setting up again and uninstalling over SSH all reserve the account before
    probing it, through their last change. The account's home holds the reservation and the
    OS file lock used by each remote write. Only the reservation's owner can roll back a failed
    addition. If SSH drops during a write and the box cannot confirm that it ended, the attempt
    stops and leaves the reservation for recovery. A failed release is reported with the result.
  - **What it does**, in order: connects with the keys and agent of the box's computer (never a
    password; refused, it tries once through an agent of its own that offers the first few SSH keys
    in the vault, "Vault"); takes an atomic reservation on the SSH account, then probes the
    computer (its system and kind, what the engine needs,
    its `machine-id` where it has one, what Kuvo Code it has); refuses a Mac with an earlier Kuvo
    Code's data its installer would move (`app-07`, `app-box`: updated to Kuvo there first),
    unless that Mac has a box of its own (`box/kind` says `mac`; the probe doesn't look at the
    data then) or a machine's, judged from the probe by the rule the installer judges one by
    (`machineBoxIn`), where its installer leaves that data as it is; puts its own release's files there, each checked by its
    SHA-256 before it's put in place, unless they're there already or the computer has a newer
    Kuvo Code, which is left as it is. For a Mac, it supplies the signed Kuvo Helper from its
    files or its verified release archive. It supplies the engine, its own binary where the two are the same
    kind, else the pinned package fetched and checked on the box's computer (the computer added
    downloads no code); then, in one script, the computer's settings made its own (one with none starts
    with the box's, below), how its keeper starts it (`run/launch.env`: the session's PATH, shell and
    language and its name; no password or key), and its `machine-id` made once. On Linux it adds
    the `@reboot` line and runs `kuvo-start start`. On Darwin it installs and starts Kuvo Helper’s
    launch agent. The keeper starts the engine with a port and passwords that never leave it; then `kuvo-link.js setup` there with this box's keys and documents, its answer
    written as the box's own record of it (its peers document, `machines.json`, and
    `phone-link.json` for `kuvo/hosts`).
  - **What a new computer starts with** (`seeding`), once as it is added. A fresh SSH
    installation can take the source's model choice and simple local integration definitions
    that use only the selected key files. Settings with inline secrets stay on the source.
    Selected keys go with the private input to `box adopt`. Selected stable engine sign-ins
    go to `kuvo-link.js box seed` on standard input as `{credentials: [{integrationID, label, value}]}`
    and are stored unless the destination already has a sign-in for that account. The command
    answers with the count, and records a completed copy in `run/seeded.json`. A restarted
    copy skips credentials already written. A computer with an existing installation, and
    every computer set up again, keeps its sign-ins and keys. The source values stay out of
    commands, logs, and saved attempt or forwarding receipts.
  - `POST kuvo/computers/<key>/setup` → `202 {try}`: the same at the address it was added under
    (Set Up Again), which brings an older Kuvo Code there up to this box's. `POST
    kuvo/computers/<key>/uninstall` → `202 {try}`: over SSH the computer lets this box go
    (`leave`) and, unless another Mac that set it up still uses it, runs its own `kuvo-link.js
    uninstall` and deletes the sign-ins and keys it keeps, and the folder of Kuvo Code's app
    there (`~/.kuvo-code/desktop`: the key that app is known by among your devices, and its list
    of your computers; #753); then the box removes it as `DELETE kuvo/computers/<key>` does,
    which takes that app off your devices on every computer. (On a Mac the app keeps its key in
    its Keychain, which SSH doesn't reach: there, being taken off your devices is what keeps it
    out. Where another Mac still uses the computer, nothing is deleted there, and its app is
    taken off this setup's devices all the same. The app's folder goes even where no Kuvo Code
    that runs is found there.) The rest of its folder stays. Asked while that computer is being set up, the
    try under way is stopped first and waited for, so nothing starts it again behind the removal
    (#603). Both are offered in `actions` (`setup`, `uninstall` with its `confirm`; `why` while
    one is under way) on machines the box has an SSH address for, and are `404` for any other.
    A computer that can't be reached isn't uninstalled later: the try fails, saying so.
- **Keeping them up to date** (`computers.update`): every computer follows the newest signed
  release its peers hold by itself, at once ("Updates", Your computers follow each other); this is
  the retry. The box that set a machine up over SSH brings its Kuvo up to its own once it's older,
  with no client open, when the machine doesn't follow its peers (a box from before that, whose mail
  says no `kuvo`), or still hasn't an hour after this box first saw it behind (`behind` in
  `run/keep-up.json`). A machine from before `kuvo/box/update` takes no release from a client over
  the relay, and a beta isn't GitHub's latest release, so this is how such a one is brought up.
  Every 15 minutes (`run/keep-up.json` keeps what
  it found of each, by key), for each machine it set up (`kind: "machine"`, not
  `away`) whose version, as it said it with its agents, is older than this box's (or that says
  none: then `bin/box-version` there tells; until a look says otherwise, one heard from that says
  none counts as older, being from before boxes said it), it brings it up whatever is at work
  there, as nothing there is cut short: where its version isn't said, it looks over SSH first,
  changing nothing (`bin/box-version`, and what's at work there, noted). Then it runs Set Up Again's steps
  (all but copying keys and sign-ins) as a try of kind `update` ("Updating Kuvo on <name>…"), which
  leave its running engine alone and its coding agents' bridge to make way at a quiet moment ("A
  new version while it works"). Begun by the box itself, a try that would ask you something (a
  host key, another setup's box) fails instead. One that fails rests an hour, then a day after each
  next failure, and one you stopped isn't begun again by itself for a day; a machine that can't be
  reached over SSH is no failure, and is looked at again next round. What went wrong goes to the
  box's log, in ssh's own words; a client gets plain ones. Found as new as this box, a machine
  isn't reached again for it for a day. Where a round can't run at all (`canAdd` refuses: no link
  yet, files missing, the old app attached before a move; or its own version can't be read), the
  box logs why once each time that changes, and says it on each older machine (below).
  - Reaching it: at the address it was added under first; where that doesn't answer (a home
    network's address while you're away), each other address in turn: those you added it under
    (`otherAddresses`, reached as themselves), then those it tells its Macs (`computer.addresses`,
    "Peers"), reached as the first is (its user, port and keys, as `ssh -G` reads your config) and
    checked against the host key known for the first (`HostKeyAlias`: your config's own, else its
    host, as `[host]:port` off port 22), never asked about. Not reached at any: "Couldn’t reach
    <name>. Make sure it’s on and connected, then Try Again.", whatever another address said (what
    each said goes to the log).
  - `update` says what's true now (`title`) and, where there's one, the next step (`detail`):
    "Kuvo on <name> updates in a moment", "Couldn’t reach <name>" and
    "Couldn’t update Kuvo on <name>" (`failed`: why in words, then "Kuvo also tries again by itself
    later."), "Couldn’t check <name>" (reached, but what's at work there couldn't be told),
    "Updating Kuvo on <name>…" (`updating`), and, where this box can't bring it up, "Kuvo on <name>
    needs an update" with why: what keeps a Mac's box that isn't another's member from it now
    (`canAdd`'s words, nothing to press), or set it up over SSH from here once (`add`). A Linux box
    and a member of another Mac's setup say nothing (they never bring machines up): a client draws
    what the box that lists your computers says instead, as it does wherever the box it shows offers
    nothing to press and that one does. Mostly there's nothing to press: it's brought up by itself.
    "Try Again" (`update`, no `confirm`: nothing at work there stops) comes only once it failed twice
    (`failed.tries`; one you began yourself that fails, at once), or this box couldn't reach it over
    SSH for three days (`unreachedSince`) while it doesn't follow its peers; before that, "… tries its
    update again in a while" and "Kuvo on <name> updates once <this box> can reach it" (`waiting`).
  - `POST kuvo/computers/<key>/update` → `202 {try}`: Update Now, the same try begun now (one that
    rested is tried at once), with nobody's work waited for: a client asks first where the action
    has a `confirm`. One as new already ends with each step "It’s up to date already". `404` for a
    computer this box didn't set up over SSH; `409` while something else is done with it (Set Up
    Again, Uninstall), and as `…/setup` answers otherwise.
- A box says what it knows, never more: SSH is only how a computer was set up, so
  no box says a machine is reached "through SSH", and a computer no peer of this box names isn't
  listed.

### What waits on you

How many things wait on you in each area, across the box (`waiting`, #711), for a client's badges
(the Mac's rail, a phone's tabs): counted by the box from its session list, so every client says
the same number and counts nothing.

- `GET kuvo/waiting` → `{sessions, bots, queue}`: `sessions`, every session that waits on you, each
  once, for a client's one badge of them: those "Needs you" lists (`needsYou` in
  `kuvo/sessions/list`) and, since #718, the bots' own conversations that wait, which the lists file
  under their bots (not archived, this box's own copy), so the number is what a client's rows of
  waiting sessions show and a client adds nothing to it; `bots`, the bots that live here with a session waiting on you
  (`now.asking`, below; a session here working for a bot on another computer is that computer's
  to count); `queue`, the Work Queue's items here that need you (#729), each once: open (not in a
  status the view says is `closed`) and not deleted, and either in the status Needs you
  (`needs-you`: someone said it waits on you) or with a session linked to it (not archived, this
  box's own copy) that asks now, whatever its status still says (its agent waits on you before it
  could say so). One rule, the box's; a client counts nothing. So the badge can be more than the
  Needs you status's count (`counts.statuses`): an item in another status whose session asks is in
  the badge, under its own status in a list (a view says which items' sessions ask: none yet). While the engine can't be read, `sessions` and `bots` are zero
  and `queue` counts only the items in Needs you. `405` for anything but `GET`.
- `GET kuvo/waiting/events` (ndjson): the same now, and a line each time it changes (an ask comes
  or is answered, a bot or an item changes, an item's status among them); through `box route` it answers its first line, and a
  client asks again as that box's session list changes.
- Each box counts its own: a client that shows several computers adds theirs up (a view). The three
  are counts of three areas, never added to each other: a bot's helper that asks is in `sessions`
  (as its own session) and makes its bot one of `bots`.
- **What counts as waiting** (one rule, the box's: `asked` in the session list's facts, from which
  `needsYou`, `now.asking`, the projects' `asking` and these counts all come): a permission or a
  question the session or one of its subagents asks, a command the sandbox stopped, what it asks of
  the vault, and, since #718, the cards the box keeps for it: what its agent asks while it browses
  (`kuvo/asks`: a sign-in, a code, a step of yours; while that browser runs), what it asks before it
  does it (`kuvo/work/asks`: a project to make or clone, a limit reset to use), and a goal its bot
  put to you (`kuvo/work/goals`, while it's proposed, in the bot's own conversation). In `needsYou`
  these say `kind: "other"` with the box's words ("asks you to sign in to github.com", "asks for a
  code from …", "asks you to do a step in its browser", "asks to make a project", "asks to clone a
  project", "asks to use a limit reset", "proposes a goal"). The box looks at those cards every two
  seconds, and at once for one kept in its own process. No client keeps a rule of its own for any
  of them.
- **What a bot is doing now** (`bots.now`, #711): each bot in `GET kuvo/bots` and
  `kuvo/bots/events` has `now` `{working, asking, finished?}`: how many of its sessions (its own
  conversation, and those working for it: `bot` in the session list's facts; not archived, this
  box's own copy) are at work (its own turn runs, or its turn is over while a command or subagent it left goes on: Background work, the same fact the session list's `running` says), and wait on you (never both); and, with neither, `finished`, when
  the newest of them last changed (ms; left out for a bot with no session listed). Its events say
  it again as its sessions start, ask, are answered and finish. Facts only: a client words them
  ("1 at work, 1 waiting on you", "Finished 3h ago") alike, a view. A bot made or changed
  (`POST`, `PATCH`) answers without `now`.
- **The one state a bot is in** (`bots.state`): `now` also has `state` (always), `since`, and
  `thinking?`, `blocked?` and `blockedBy?`: `{working, asking, finished?, state, since, thinking?,
  blocked?, blockedBy?}`. `thinking`: how many of those at work are thinking (they count in
  `working` too); `blocked`: how many are blocked, and `blockedBy` (`"error"` or `"limit"`) what
  blocked the newest of them; each left out when none. `state` is the first of these that holds:
  1. `needsYou`: one of its sessions waits on you (`asking` > 0);
  2. `blocked`: one is blocked: its run stopped on an error or a limit (`session.execution.failed`;
     a limit when its `error.type` is `provider.quota` or `provider.rate-limit`, or a coding agent's
     `limit`) until it runs again, you've read the turn it ended, or you've seen the bot since that
     turn ended (Seen, below); or it has been retrying for 10 seconds with no step begun since
     (`session.retry.scheduled`, until `session.step.started` or the run ends), whether or not
     you've seen the bot;
  3. `thinking`: every one at work is thinking: its model has been reasoning for 2 seconds on end
     (`session.reasoning.started`, until `session.reasoning.ended`, `session.text.started`,
     `session.tool.input.started`, `session.tool.called` or the run's end), and it stays thinking
     for 1.5 seconds after (reasoning again meanwhile, it never stopped), so a face doesn't flicker;
  4. `working`: one is at work;
  5. `done`: one, neither at work, waiting nor blocked, has a turn you haven't read (`unread` in
     the session list) that ended after you last saw the bot (Seen, below), on any client;
  6. `asleep`: its wake-ups are paused, or its next one (`wakes`) is more than 12 hours away;
  7. `idle`.
  `since` (ms): when it came to be in that state, as this box saw it (a box just started says when
  it started, for the state each bot was in then); for `done`, when the newest turn you haven't
  read (and that ended after you last saw the bot) ended. The box
  says it again as the state changes, a moment after the list settles (a run's end and the reads
  that follow it are one change), and as a bot's next wake-up comes within 12 hours with nothing
  else changing. The rule is the box's (`box/src/link/lists/rule.ts`, held to
  `protocol/vectors/bot-states.json`); no client works it out. **Offline is the client's own**: a
  box can't say it can't be reached, so a client draws a bot offline while the bot's computer's
  `reach` is `away` ("Computers"), or while it can't reach its own box, keeping the counts for the
  words under its name. Under the name of a bot that's `blocked`, a client says what blocked it:
  "Hit a usage limit" (`blockedBy` `"limit"`) or "Stopped on an error" (`"error"`), in place of the
  counts' words. A client may hold a state on screen a little longer as it draws it (Done's
  celebration), never decide one.
- **Seen** (`bots.state`): `POST kuvo/bots/<id>/seen` (`{}`), as a client shows you a bot (its
  conversation opened, its row looked at). The box keeps when you last saw each of its bots (its
  own clock, ms; across its restarts; one that no longer lives here is let go as it next keeps
  one), never past the end of a turn of its work it's still judging (READ_RULE: you couldn't have
  seen that one yet, so if it's news to you, it counts). What it does:
  - The bot is no longer `done` for a turn that ended by then, nor `blocked` by a hard stop that
    did, on every client (each hears the bot's line in `kuvo/bots/events`). A turn that ends later
    makes it `done` (or a later stop `blocked`) again; a retry under way blocks it all the same.
  - Its own conversation is read up to where its last turn ended, as a client reads the
    conversation it shows (`POST api/session/<id>/view`, the coding agents' through their bridge;
    each hears `session.viewed`).
  What it doesn't: read the sessions working for it. What the box left unread there as news to you
  (READ_RULE: a turn that failed, one answering what you wrote in it) keeps its new mark on every
  client until you open that session; only the bot stops saying `done` for it.
  Answers `200 {}`; `404 {"message"}` for a bot that doesn't live here (ask the box it lives on),
  `502 {"message"}` where its conversation couldn't be read just now (the bot is seen all the same:
  ask again), `503` while the engine can't be read (seen all the same), `500 {"message"}` where the
  box couldn't keep it, `405` for anything but `POST`.

### A session's actions

Pin, Rename, Archive and Delete, as a session's menu offers them (`sessions.actions`, #668): the
box does each on its engine or its coding agents' bridge, whichever keeps the session (every coding
