  the conversation (the Mac's sidebar has them under it).
  - `POST …/kuvo/btw/<session>` with `{"question", "thread"?}` (at most 4,000 characters) →
    `{data: question}`, `state` `answering`; it's answered in a moment. `thread` asks it as a
    follow-up in that thread (`404` when there's no such thread); without it, it starts one. A
    question: `{id, session, thread?, question, state: "answering" | "answered" | "failed",
    answer?, error?, asked, answered?}`; `thread` is the id of the question that started its
    thread (its own for the first; one from before threads has none: a thread of its own).
  - `GET …/kuvo/btw/<session>` → `{data: [question]}`, oldest first; `GET …/kuvo/btw` → `{data:
    [{session, count, threads, latest}]}`, every conversation that has some (`threads`: how
    many side threads its `count` questions are in).
  - Side threads (`btw.threads.events`), each a side chat, grouped by the box so no client groups
    them: `GET …/kuvo/btw/<session>/threads` → `{"threads": [{id, title, asked, latest, answering,
    questions}]}`, the one with the latest activity first. `id` is the thread's (its first
    question's), `title` that question as asked, `asked` when it was, `latest` when anything in it
    last happened (a question asked or answered), `answering` while one in it is still being
    answered, `questions` the questions in it, oldest first. A conversation with none has `[]`.
    `GET …/kuvo/btw/<session>/threads/events` (ndjson) sends the same now, then a line each time
    anything in that conversation's side questions changes (asked, answered, failed, taken away),
    until its client closes it; it passes through the box's link as it comes
    (`kuvo/agents/api/kuvo/btw/<session>/threads/events`).
  - `DELETE …/kuvo/btw/<session>/<id>` takes one away, `DELETE …/kuvo/btw/<session>/threads/<thread>`
    a side thread, all of it, and `DELETE …/kuvo/btw/<session>` all of them.
  - Events: `kuvo.btw.updated` `{sessionID, question}` as one is asked and answered;
    `kuvo.btw.removed` `{sessionID, id?}` (a thread's, one for each of its questions).
- **Handoffs** (`handoff`): a conversation carried on in a fresh one.
  Its model writes a handoff note from inside it, and a new conversation in the same folder, on
  the same model, effort, agent and permissions, titled "<title> (continued)", starts on that note
  (a note whose text starts with `[Handoff] `: show its `description`, "Carried on from “…”"), and
  on `next` when given. The two are linked in their metadata (`kuvo.handoffFrom`,
  `kuvo.handoffTo`; the rest of it kept): show the link in each.
  - `POST …/kuvo/handoff/<session>` with `{"next"?}` → `{data: handoff}`, `state` `writing`: the
    note takes a while. A handoff: `{from, state: "writing" | "done" | "failed", to?, title?,
    error?, started?}`, `started` when it was asked for (ms since 1970): which handoff it is, so an
    end told before the answer to its start isn't taken for an earlier one's. `409` for a subagent's, one with no model yet, one being handed off, or one whose
    agent is working (wait for its turn to end); one whose agent starts while the note is written
    fails, and makes no new conversation.
  - `GET …/kuvo/handoff/<session>` → `{data: handoff}`, its latest while the box runs.
  - Event `kuvo.handoff` `{sessionID, handoff}` as it starts and ends: open `to` once it's `done`.
- **Branches** (`branch`, "Branch from here"): a new conversation with another one's words before
  a message of yours, made by its place (the engine's own fork, or the bridge's), and marked as
  branched from it in its metadata (`kuvo.branchedFrom`; where its source came from or was handed
  off to isn't carried over, and it starts unpinned and not archived; if the mark can't be written,
  it's answered without it). Show a conversation marked `kuvo.branchedFrom` or `kuvo.handoffFrom`,
  or `kuvo.startedBy` (one an agent started with its start_session tool, on a Mac or a machine;
  it opens nowhere by itself, and the mark isn't carried over to a branch either; older ones also
  carry `kuvo.beside`, which nothing reads),
  under that one when it's in the same list, newest first, and rank it in a list of the latest by
  its newest branch; a subagent's session (one with a `parentID`) is never shown so: it shows in
  the conversation it works for. A box from before branches answers `404` "Not available for this
  agent.": fork with the engine's own route, and mark it so yourself.
  - `POST …/kuvo/branch/<session>` with `{"before"}`, the message's id → `{data: session}`, the new
    conversation, marked. `400` with no `before`, `404` for a message not in it, `409` for a
    subagent's.
- **Reviews** (`reviews`; scopes `reviews.scopes`): what `scope` names in the conversation's folder, read by a
  model with none of the conversation's context: on the engine, its own model afresh, or `model`
  when given; with the coding agents, its own agent (another one you're signed in to when it
  can't), `model` left out. A scope:
  - `{"kind": "uncommitted"}`, the default: the changes not committed yet (the folder's own, in
    its git: tracked files' diffs, against nothing before the first commit, and new files whole;
    a big new file is named with its size, and links and files that aren't text are left out);
  - `{"kind": "branch", "base"?}`: the branch's changes since it left `base` (when left out,
    main or master, yours or origin's, whichever is newer, or origin's HEAD), with those not
    committed yet;
  - `{"kind": "commits", "from", "to"?}`: what the commits after `from`, up to `to` (HEAD when
    left out), changed, git's `from..to`; `from` as `<commit>^` starts with that commit, the
    first one too;
  - `{"kind": "folder", "path"}` and `{"kind": "project"}`: the files themselves, of a folder in
    the project (a path inside it, never `..` or absolute: `400`) or all of it, numbered line by
    line: those git keeps or would (all but hidden ones and `node_modules` out of a repository),
    but for links, lock files, `.env` files, big files and ones that aren't text;
  - `{"kind": "described", "words"}` (bridge 0.9.101, when `choices` says `describes`): the files
    `words` describe ("the auth module and its tests", "the files I changed today"), which the
    conversation's model picks from the project's files, told what git says was worked on lately
    and today's date; then read as a folder's are. A client sends only `words` (500 characters at
    most); the box finds the files, keeps them for half an hour for the same conversation and
    words (so a review asked for after `measure` reads the same ones), and a review's `scope` has
    them as `paths` once found. Words that fit no file are `422` with what to do.

  One too big to read at once is read in parts, one after another (at most 30; more is left out,
  and its summary says how many files), each by a fresh model.
  - `POST …/kuvo/reviews/<session>` with `{"model"?: {providerID, id}, "focus"?, "scope"?}` →
    `{data: review}`, `state` `reviewing`; `409` while one is under way, `400` for a scope that
    makes no sense. `focus` is what to look at especially, as the user wrote it, or `security`, `performance` or `accessibility`, which the box spells out
    for the reviewer. A review: `{id, session, state: "reviewing" | "done" | "failed", model?,
    scope?, focus?, progress?: {read, of}, stopped?: {read, of}, summary?, findings: [finding],
    error?, fix?, started, ended?}`, its findings bugs first; `scope` is left out for the changes
    not committed yet, `progress` is there while one read in parts is under way (`read` of `of`
    parts), its findings so far in `findings`, and `stopped` says where Stop ended one. A finding: `{id, title, explanation, severity: "bug" | "risk" | "nit",
    locations: [{file, line?, endLine?}]}`: what's wrong in a line, why and how to fix it (`""`
    when the title says it all), and every place it's in, none when it's about the change as a
    whole (a missing test). `fix` is what to send the agent, as your message, to fix them all.
    `parts` (`reviews.parts`, bridge 0.9.102) are what it reads, each part by a reviewer of its
    own: `[{n, of, files, state: "waiting" | "reading" | "done" | "failed" | "stopped", found,
    session?, now?}]`, `files` the part's first 200, `found` what it found. On the engine each
    part reads in a session of its own, `session`: under the conversation (`parentID`), marked
    `kuvo.reviewPart: {review, part, of}` and kept out of lists like the box's other runs, its
    agent `plan` with rules that let it read the project and nothing more. Its folder is the box's
    own (`reviewers` beside its reviews, a git repository with one empty commit), reading the
    project from outside it, so no "Always allow" saved for the project reaches it (a box that
    can't make that folder so, without git, fails the part, saying why, rather than read it
    elsewhere); `kuvo.messages` says it takes none. A client opens it as it
    opens a subagent's, to watch it read and to look at it after; it goes when the review is put
    away or another takes its place. `now` is what it's doing as it reads ("Reading src/a.ts",
    "Looking for “token”", "Thinking", "Writing what it found"), told as it changes (not kept),
    gone once it's done. Stop stops the part reading (`stopped`); those after it stay `waiting`.
    A review's only part stopped from its own session ends the review as its Stop does. Parts'
    sessions no kept review records (made as the box stopped) are deleted once the box's engine
    is there again, and one left reading is stopped.
    With the coding agents a part has no `session`. A box from before `parts` leaves it out.
  - `POST …/kuvo/reviews/<session>/measure` with `{"scope"?}` → `{data: {files, parts, leftOut,
    commits?, found?}}`: how much a review of it would read, to show before asking for a big one
    (`commits` for a branch or a range of them, `found` the first 10 files found for described
    words that it reads); `422` with what's wrong when it can't be read (not a repository, no such
    commit or folder, words that fit no file, or only files it can't read), `503` when the model
    couldn't be asked. Described words still being found are waited for, not asked again, by a
    review or another `measure` meanwhile.
  - `GET …/kuvo/reviews/<session>/choices` → `{data: {repository, branch?: {name, base, commits},
    commits: [{id, short, title, time}], folders: [{path, files}], describes?: true}}`: what "What to review"
    offers in the conversation's folder: the branch it's on with its base and how many commits
    of its own (left out on the base itself), its 30 latest commits (`time` in ms), and its
    folders by path, with how many files each has at any depth (500 at most, shallowest first).
    Out of a repository, `repository` is `false` and only the folders come. `describes` says it
    reads what you describe (`described`; a box from before leaves it out).
  - `POST …/kuvo/reviews/<session>/stop` → `{data: review}`: one under way ends where it is,
    `done`, keeping what it found so far (its summary says how far it got); `409` once it's over.
  - `POST …/kuvo/reviews/<session>/fix` with `{"findings"?: [id]}` → `{data: {text}}`: what to send
    an agent, as your message, to fix them all or those it names, wherever you send it (this
    conversation, a new one, another); `404` when the review found nothing, or none of them is
    in it any more.
  - `GET …/kuvo/reviews/<session>` → `{data: review}`, its latest; `GET …/kuvo/reviews` → every
    conversation's; `DELETE …/kuvo/reviews/<session>` puts it away (one under way is let go: its answer isn't kept).
  - Event `kuvo.review.updated` `{sessionID, review}`, `review` null once it's put away.

The same bridge also gives voice input the words to listen for in a conversation (a speech model
is prompted with them), for the engine's sessions and the coding agents' alike:
`GET …/kuvo/voice/words/<session>` → `{data: {words: [string]}}`, at most 100, most useful first
(ask when listening starts). They're the project's own names: its folder's (and its repository's),
the names said in the conversation's newest messages, its packages', the files changed lately (each
with and without its extension), then its other folders and files. Never anything of `.env`
files, nor long hex or random-looking strings. `404` for a conversation that isn't there, `409`
for one with no folder.

### What a typed message means

Kuvo has no typed keywords or commands: what's written in a composer goes to the agent as a
message, as written, one starting with "/" or "!" too (Claude Code's own "/" commands, typed in its
conversation, are its to read). A client sends it through the conversation's box:

- `POST kuvo/sessions/<session>/draft` (feature `typed.draft`; `…/submit` and `…/submissions`
  through another computer, `typed.submission-recovery`) with `{id, text, message, quotedText?,
  submission?}`, once per `id` whatever becomes of the request. The box checks the conversation's
  model first, as `kuvo/sessions/models` says it (one it can't say about now goes on), then sends
  `message` (the send route's fields below, `words` aside) as the message `text`, or `quotedText`
  with what the composer replies to. `200 {answer, message?, acceptedAt?}`: `answer` is `{send:
  {text, quoted: true}}` with `message` its id once sent; `{restore: {text}, error, action?}` where
  the model can't run (`action` as `kuvo/sessions/models` says it) or the send was refused, for the
  client to put the text back and say why; `{ambiguous: true, error}` where the box can't tell
  whether it went. `400` without `id`, `text` and `message`; `404`/`503` `{message, restore}`.
- `kuvo/sessions/<session>/typed` (feature `typed`) stays for 0.7.x clients: `POST {text, id?}`
  answers the same `answer` (the client then sends the message itself), and `GET` answers
  `{"keywords": [], "commands": []}`: nothing is offered after "/".

### A message's parts

See “Messages in a session” for same-ID send and restart settlement.

Coding-agent history can return a `file://` address for an attachment that was sent inline
or returned by a tool. The bytes live on the conversation's box and can be read with
`kuvo/file`. A client's message pages keep the same message IDs, order and cursors.

A client sends what was written and what goes with it as fields, and the conversation's box writes
the text the agent reads (feature `messages.send`, which the update gate requires); every message
the box sends keeps its parts, which clients draw it by. No client writes or reads the blocks.

- `POST kuvo/sessions/<session>/send` `{id, words, files?, delivery?, widget?, comments?,
  named?, notes?}`: `words` as written (the composer's text, quotes and all), `files` as the engine
  takes them (`file://` on the box's own disk, or `data:` inline, which the box keeps as
  `attachedIn` does), `widget` the title of the
  widget it answers (`""` for none), `comments` `[{file, line, side: "new"|"old", snippet, text}]`,
  `named` the sessions picked from the "&" list (of two agents with one name, these), `notes`
  `{included?, paths?, unsent?}` (files the client sent with their contents, by path, or couldn't
  send). `{id, text, files?, delivery?}` sends one sent before again as the agent
  read it (Retry; another agent's letter put back; one from before whose parts couldn't be read),
  `words` then only how it's shown; its files are kept as a message's are (a picture for a model that
  only reads words goes as a path, in the note it has). A session picked in `named` that this box
  doesn't list, after a moment's wait for its list, is refused (`409`), never dropped. It goes to the
  engine or the coding agents' bridge, wherever the session is, once per `id` (`sentOnce`), and
  answers as they do; `400` nothing to send, `404` no such session, `409` moving or an agent not
  listed, `503` not running. `queue/add` takes the same fields, `{text, again: true, words?}` for one
  sent again as the agent read it, and `{text, kept: true, words?, metadata?}` for one a DELETE gave
  back (Undo) with the parts it had; `text` alone is an older client's own envelope.
- **What the agent reads,** in this order (the words Kuvo Code wrote before, byte for byte): the
  words (trimmed; the widget's block after them: a line `<from-widget>`, a heading, its title on one
  line, `</from-widget>`), for a bot's goal asked for (`kuvo/work/goals/ask`) its block
  (`<sent-with>`, a heading and how to plan it, `/goal`, `</sent-with>`), who the "&" names are
  (`<named-agents>`, from everyone the box lists then, `- &<name> (<session>): <what it is>`), the
  comments (`<review-comments>`, a heading, then for each a blank line, `[<file>:<line>]` or
  `[<file>:<line> (removed)]`, `> <the line>`, what was said), the files' note (`<attached-files>`,
  the client's `notes` then what the box keeps, each list under its heading), and from a phone
  (a request that isn't a Kuvo Code app's, nor the desktop app's over the link: `clients.kind`,
  "Sessions") `<from-phone>`. An `&` in a title is written
  `＆`; words ending like the named, comments' or files' block get a space after its tag, so they
  stay words.
- **Parts:** kept in the engine message's (and inbox item's) `metadata.kuvo.parts`: `{words,
  keyword?, widget?, comments?, paths?, agents?: [{name, session}], phone?: true, mail?: {name,
  session}, command?: true}` (`paths`: files its note names that it doesn't carry; `mail`: another agent wrote it,
  `"[Message from <name> · <session>] (…)"`, and `words` is what they wrote; `keyword`, a bot's
  `/goal`, or the keyword an older message was sent with; `command`: an older message ran a command,
  `keyword` (`/review`), with `words` as its arguments). Those sent here and
  `queue/add`'s with fields keep them, as do a started session's task and a bot's /goal; a letter
  between agents, a prompt passed on the way before (`api/session/<id>/prompt`) and anything else
  the box sends keep them where there's more to them than the text. The box's own notes keep none
  (`kuvo.note`), nor does a plain message, which a client asks about once.
- **Messages from before** keep no parts: `POST kuvo/messages/parts {texts}` (at most 500) answers
  `{parts}`, one for each, read from the text as the apps read it before (every block, an older
  keyword's `<sent-with>` among them, a /goal
  sent as `[Goal] …`, a file listed with ` (on the user's Mac: …)`, the named block's earlier
  heading). A client asks once for each message (KuvoClient's `MessageParts.read`), before it shows
  the page, and shows one its box couldn't read as written.
- **An older command shows as typed** (`messages.commands`): Kuvo no longer runs the engine's
  commands, but messages that ran one before keep the parts `{words, keyword: "/<name>", command:
  true}`, so a client draws "/review this branch", never the prompt the command made: a coding
  agent's with the message, the engine's kept by the box by message id in `run/commands.json`.
  `kuvo/messages/parts` takes `{texts, ids}` (an id for each text; `session`, which older clients
  send, is no longer needed) and answers those by id; the queue's items and `removed` say them too.
- Both directions: `vectors/message-parts.json` (written from the apps' Swift before this), which
  the box (`test/message-parts.test.ts`) and KuvoClient (`MessagePartsTests`) are held to.
- One waiting on the box (`waiting` in a queue) says the keyword it was sent with (`keyword`: a
  bot's /goal, or an older message's), for its row to show in front of its words.
- A group chat's message still carries the widget it answers as its own block (`WidgetAnswer`).

- **Quotes and picture names in `words`**, written the same by every client (KuvoClient's
  `Quoting` and `ImageReferences`; the desktop app's `kuvo_box::quoting` and
  `kuvo_box::image_names`), so a reply written on one shows the same on another. A quote is
  Markdown ahead of the words: each quoted line as `> line` (`>` alone for a blank line), a blank
  line, then the answer to it; several quotes one after another, each with its answer, and words
  after an answered last quote follow a line of `---`. A client draws the `> ` lines that start
  the words, or follow a blank line, as the quote (not inside a code block). A picture attached is
  named where you're writing as `[Image N]`, N counting the message's pictures in the order they're
  attached from 1; taking one off takes its name out and moves the later ones down a number. The
  box passes both on as written.
- **Files a client attaches**: to its own computer's box, by `file://` path; to another
  computer's, with their bytes (`data:`, as a phone sends them), which its box keeps, since no path
  on the client's computer means anything there. A picture the client keeps only a while (one
  pasted) goes with its bytes to its own box too, so the message never points at a file that goes.
  One the client can't read, or too large to send (over 50 MB, or 100 MB in all), isn't left out:
  the send doesn't go, and the client says which file and why.

### Features

`kuvo/info`'s `features` names the routes the box has, so a client checks a name, never a version
(`app`, `bridge`), before it shows what needs a route. A route it names can still refuse for now,
with a message to show: `503` while the engine or the coding agents' bridge is down (or, on a legacy Mac install, its app for its keys), and on a
machine `409` for `config`, `config.apply`, `keys`, `mcp.catalog` and `integrations` until a Mac has made its
settings its own. A name comes with what it names and never changes meaning; one the client
doesn't know, it ignores. Both boxes are held to their lists by
the route scenario `vectors/routes/features.json`, which `scripts/route-shapes.sh` writes from the
box's lists (`FEATURES` in `box/src/shared/features.ts`, `MAC_FEATURES` and
`MACHINE_FEATURES` in `shared/routes/mac.ts`). A Mac's list is its box's (`macFeatures`, from #191
step 2; the app gave it before): every box's but a machine's own, and the Mac's own, the same
with its app closed. An app-only compatibility callback can answer `503 {"message"}`.
A note of when a name came in names the bridge's version up to 0.9.211; after that, the bridge's
version is a hash, and a name is its own mark.

A client checks the advertised capability or box-authored compatibility before
drawing a feature that depends on it. Each route registration names its
feature. The expected capability list can be smaller than the set of features
the box advertises. A request still obeys the box's authorization and format
checks.

One row a name, in order, so branches that each add one merge cleanly.

Here "a Mac" is the box the app runs (`KUVO_BOX=mac`), and "a machine" any box in `~/.kuvo-code`,
on Linux or on a Mac.

The engine's own routes (`api/…`), sockets and `kuvo/info` itself are always there.

### Sockets

A request with `h.upgrade = "websocket"` opens a WebSocket on the host's engine; today only a
terminal's (`api/pty/<id>/connect`). Its body is empty. The host answers `res` with `s: 101`
once the engine's socket is open, or another status and `end: true` if it won't open. Then
each `data` message for that `id`, either way, is one message on the socket: text, or binary
if `h.type = "binary"`. Text from the engine too long for one message goes in several;
binary that long doesn't go. The phone closes it with `cancel` (or `data` with `end: true`);
when the engine closes it, the host sends `data` with `end: true`.

A box's own server (`serve`) passes a terminal's socket too (feature `pty.socket`): a WebSocket
upgrade of `GET api/pty/<id>/connect`, with `serve`'s `Authorization: Basic
<base64(opencode:password)>` and `x-opencode-directory` where it has one, checked as the browser's
live view's upgrade is (401 for a wrong password, 400 for a route version it doesn't know); 502 if
the engine's socket won't open. Each message then passes as it came, either way: text as text,
binary as binary (the engine's note, a zero byte then JSON such as `{"cursor":n}`, among them).
Either side's close goes to the other with its code and reason; an engine cut off cuts the
client off too.

## Pairing

A host shows a link, as a QR code:

```
kuvo-link://pair?v=1&relay=<relay URL>&host=<address>&key=<static key>&token=<16 bytes>&name=<name>
```

The phone opens a session with `pair` set to the token. The host checks it (and on a Mac
asks you to confirm), then keeps the phone's static key. A token works for 10 minutes and
once.

Kuvo Code's desktop app pairs without a link: it asks the box on its own computer (`POST
kuvo/devices/pair`, "Paired phones"), which requests the grant from the primary. Its key and relay secret are its own, made on its computer and never
given to a box; what it then knows of each computer (`key`, `address`, `relay`: `kuvo/computers`)
is what a pairing link holds.

On a machine the bridge keeps its state in `~/.kuvo-code/run/link.json` (mode 600):

```json
{"relay": "wss://…", "secret": "…", "key": "<static private key>", "sign": "<signing key's seed>", "mac": "<the last Mac's static key>",
 "macs": ["<each Mac that set it up>"], "macSigns": {"<Mac>": "<its signing key>"}, "macSeen": {"<Mac>": <when it came, here, moved on by time off since>}, "macNames": {"<Mac>": "<its name>"},
 "docs": {"<origin> <kind>": {"d": "…", "s": "…"}}, "own": {"<kind>": {"n", "h", "b"}}, "views": {"<origin>": {"n", "h"}},
 "phones": [{"key": "…", "name": "…", "added": 1760000000, "from": "mac", "mac": "<the Mac that listed it>", "address": "…", "pairing": "…", "kind": "desktop"}],
 "removed": [{"key": "…", "pairing": "…"}]}
```

`phones` is what its documents say ("Paired phones"): those its Macs list (`"from": "mac"`),
and those paired with the machine itself (`"pair"`); `kind` is there only on Kuvo Code's desktop app (`"desktop"`). `address` is the phone's on the relay, where its notifications go: the Mac passes on
what it knows, and the bridge notes it each time the phone comes in. The machine's keys stay when no phones are left, so pairing again gives the same
address. The bridge reads the file every 30 seconds: a phone taken off loses its sessions,
and with no phones and no pairing waiting the bridge stops. The bridge notes when a phone last
used the machine (`run/link.seen`).

### This Mac's box

The active Mac box lives in `~/.kuvo-code`. Kuvo Helper supervises it
independently of GPUI, and provides native Keychain and permission services.
The keeper and Helper start `serve --resident` on supported releases. The
GPUI client reads `run/serve.json` and connects to the private loopback
server. See [resident launch and rollback](../docs/architecture/one-client-process.md).

The following app-folder launch and keeper contracts apply to installed
0.7 clients and their import or rollback paths.

A legacy Mac runs the same box a machine does: its keeper ("The keeper", below) starts `kuvo-link.js serve` (bridge 0.9.33 and
later) beside its engine, with the engine's Bun and `KUVO_HOME` in the app's own folder
(`~/Library/Application Support/run.kuvo.code/box`), never `~/.kuvo-code`, and
`KUVO_ENGINE_CONFIG`, the app's engine's settings folder (its `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`), where it keeps
the skills a Mac has always kept ("Skills"). It answers the box's
routes over HTTP on `127.0.0.1`, as the agents bridge answers the app: it says `{"url"}` on its
first line once it listens, takes only Basic `opencode:<OPENCODE_PASSWORD>`, checks a path as
the relay does (403 for one that isn't what it seems), sends a stream as it comes (a line at a
time for `application/x-ndjson`), and goes when its stdin closes. A route that holds a request
before its answer's head (an ask waiting for you, a sandbox tool, a vault wait) sends an interim
`102 Processing` every 20 seconds to an HTTP/1.1 client, which clients ignore but which keeps
their wait for the head alive (URLSession's request timeout). It never reaches a phone: the app
forwards a phone's request to the box with URLSession, which takes it in and gives on only the
answer. It finds the engine and the
coding agents' bridge as on a machine, by `run/engine.json` and `run/bridge.json`, which the keeper
writes (only you can read them) as they start and removes as they stop.

#### The keeper

For the legacy app-folder install, this Mac's box keeps running whether or not the app is open, as a machine's does with its Mac
closed: its keeper is Kuvo Code's own executable run with `--box`, which launchd starts from the
launch agent in the app (`Contents/Library/LaunchAgents/<bundle id>.box.plist`, registered with
`SMAppService` the first time the app opens; never once this Mac's box lives in its home of its
own, with `movesOwnBox` on, where its helper starts it: "Moving this Mac's box"), at each login and
again if it stops by itself. It has no window. It runs the engine, the box and the coding agents' bridge, starts each again when it
stops (at once, up to three times in five minutes), and tries each again when it couldn't start or
keeps stopping (after 15 s, 30 s, 1, 2 and 5 minutes, then every 10 minutes for good, as a machine's
keeper waits, starting over once it ran for ten minutes; not when another try can't help: a program
that isn't there). Once among those waits, it isn't started again at once until it has run for ten
minutes. Past those waits, a try that took too long while macOS was asking you something waits an hour
instead, and goes as soon as that question is seen to be answered: it closed after staying open once
the try had ended, or a server it held came up. It records each in the box's
`run` folder,
as a machine's keeper does, so a client finds them there:

- `run/keeper.json`: `{"pid", "version", "build", "url", "password", "started"}` (milliseconds).
  `run/keeper.lock` is held while it runs: one at a time.
- `run/engine.json` and `run/bridge.json`, as on a machine; `run/engine-stopped` (its reason) when
  the engine stopped and isn't started again until asked, or until its next try, and beside it
  `run/engine-output`, what the engine wrote last (when it wrote anything), which the app shows under
  the reason, and while it waits for that try, `run/engine.retry` (when, in seconds since 1970, as on
  a machine); `run/agents-stopped` (`{"why", "retrying"}`) while the bridge is down, not while it's
  starting or stopped on purpose; `run/.system-asking` while macOS asks you something.
- `run/serve.json`: `{"pid", "port", "password"}`, where the box answers.
- `bin/kuvo-start`: as a machine's (`kuvo-start restart`), here calling the keeper
  (`--box-control`).

It answers on `127.0.0.1` at `url`, to `Authorization: Bearer <password>`: `GET status` (`pid`,
`version`, `build`, `started`, `engine {state: starting | downloading | ready | failed, progress?,
reason?}`, `busy`, `updating`, `awake`, and `box`/`agents` `{failure}` when either stopped for
good), and `POST` `restart-engine`, `restart-agents`, `restart-box`, `stop` (Stop Background Work:
it stops everything and itself, and launchd leaves it stopped until the app opens or you log in
again), `update` (an app of another version opened: it goes the first moment nothing is under way
on the engine or with the coding agents, however long what runs takes, since a running session is
never stopped for an update; launchd starts the installed app's; it answers `{updating}`, false
when the app at its place is still its own version, as when the app asking is another copy), and
`app {tools?, host?}`
(below). It also makes way by itself once another version is installed in its place.

While a session works on the engine or with the coding agents, the keeper keeps the Mac from
sleeping on its own (Settings › General's Keep this Mac awake, the app's own setting, read as it
changes), whether or not the app is open; `awake` says whether it does now, with the setting as it
is then.

The app is a client: it reads those records (again as the `run` folder changes) and connects to
the engine, the box and the bridge as they say, starting the keeper with launchd when there's none.
While macOS doesn't let the keeper run (switched off in Login Items & Extensions), the app runs the
same three itself, and they stop when it quits. A newer app finding an older keeper asks it to
make way (`update`) and follows it meanwhile, saying the update waits for what's running (when
the keeper answers that it makes way); it
downloads no engine of its own then, so the one the older keeper runs stays, and connects to the
new keeper's once its records appear. The app keeps the Mac awake itself only while it runs the box
itself; following the keeper, `kuvo/mac`'s `awakeNow` is the keeper's `awake`.

The engine and the agents reach Kuvo Code's own tools through the keeper's own MCP server,
whose address doesn't change as the app opens and quits: the open app says where its tools answer
(`app {tools: {url, token}}`, again whenever a new keeper starts), and each call goes there as it
is. With the app closed, the tools are listed as the app last listed them (`run/tools-list.json`),
and the keeper answers them through this Mac's box, as a machine's `kuvo-browser.js` does: the
agents' tools (`POST kuvo/agent-tools`), wake-ups (kuvo-wake), `set_job` (`PATCH kuvo/bots/<id>`),
the vault (`POST kuvo/vault/tools`), and show_file, show_widget and mark_final. Only the browser's
tools and show_in_panel need the app: a call answers `isError`, saying Kuvo Code must be open. A
browser call with the app closed opens it in the background (#211: the keeper opens the app it runs
from, once for every call waiting, 30 seconds, five minutes' rest after one that failed, never while
an update installs). A Mac's box in a home of its own has no keeper's tools: its own
`kuvo-browser.js` sends the browser's tools to the app, and the box opens it ("This Mac's app").

Its group chats run in its coding agents' bridge, as a machine's do, with folders in the app's
own: the chats in `groups` (`KUVO_GROUPS`), its bots' in `bots` (`KUVO_BOTS`), what it lets go
of in `box/trash` (`KUVO_TRASH`; the bridge says `kuvo.group.trashed {id, path}` and the app moves
it to the Finder's Trash), and who can be named with `&` in `box/run/agents.json`
(`KUVO_AGENTS_FILE`, as a machine's `run/agents.json`, which the box writes: "Peers"). `KUVO_BOX=mac` says
it's a Mac's: its bots are the Mac's own (`machine` left out), made with the words the app puts in its
`bin`, with no time zone of their own while no zone is picked (they go by the Mac's clock as it
changes; "Your time zone"). Its bots remember its
chats under `kuvo.groups` (`KUVO_GROUPS_MEMORY_KEY`). The box passes a client's `kuvo/groups…`
on to that bridge, as a machine's does (bridge 0.9.65; the app did before), saying "Group chats on
this Mac are starting" or "aren't answering" when it can't; from 0.9.202, while the bridge is down,
what `kuvo/groups…`, `kuvo/artifacts…` and `kuvo/agents/…` answer with their 503 is "This Mac's coding
agents aren't running." with why (`run/agents-stopped`), and that Restart on the Mac starts them unless
they're being tried again. The box carries its group chats' mail (`seat`, "Peers")
on its relay connection, as a machine's bridge does, and tells the bridge who your machines and
their bots are (bridge 0.9.63).

Its engine settings (`kuvo/config`, `kuvo/config/apply`, `kuvo/mcp/catalog`) are where the app's
engine has always read them, `opencode/config/opencode/opencode.json` in the app's folder: the
app gives the box the engine's settings folder (`KUVO_ENGINE_CONFIG`, the engine's
`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`), so nothing moves. They're its own from the start (never `409`). Its keys
(`kuvo/keys`, and those Settings › Integrations adds with, `kuvo/integrations`) stay in the Mac's
Keychain, under the service they've always had: the box asks the app for them ("Host interface")
and names them where the app writes them for the engine to read (`KUVO_KEYS`, in the app's
temporary folder), never in its own folder. What integrations' servers keep (a sign-in) is in the
app's `integrations` folder (`KUVO_INTEGRATIONS`), as the engine runs them with it. The app puts the popular servers in its
`bin/mcp-catalog.json` as it starts it, and those that use a Mac's own apps are listed and added
there.

#### A home of its own

Every box can run in a home of its own, laid out as a machine's (#333), a Mac's too: its kind is
what it records in `box/kind`, a word on a line (`mac` or `machine`; none, or another word, is a
machine). The app's box in its own folder is a Mac's whatever's recorded there, as its keeper says
(`KUVO_BOX=mac`), and is the only box that reaches beside its home, for what its app keeps there.
Every other box names every place from its home (`kuvo-link.js`, `bin/kuvo-start` and
`bin/kuvo-launch` read `box/kind`), whichever of its processes asks. A Mac's box in a home of its
own keeps:

- its engine's settings and skills in `config` (`config/opencode/opencode.json`, its own from the
  start, as in the app's folder; never `box/opencode.json`), its engine's data in `data/opencode`,
  what integrations' servers keep in `integrations`;
- its chats in `chats`, every file sent with a message in `attachments`, its bots in `bots`, their
  wake-ups in `wakes`, and the rest of the box's own as a machine keeps them (`box/`, `run/`,
  `artifacts`, `trash`, `search`, `apps`, `browser`, `updates`, `t`); the coding agents' bridge
  keeps `agents` and `groups` there, as on a machine;
- the list of your machines in `machines.json` and the app's record of their bridges in
  `phone-link.json`, which the app writes beside it;
- its engine's settings as its own: its engine's start (`kuvo-launch`) reads nothing before them and
  writes nothing over them, whatever a machine's start left in that home (`box/opencode.json`);
- its keys in the Mac's Keychain, through its host ("Host interface"), as in the app's folder, from
  every process of its own (`serve`, a client's `box route`) whatever its environment says. What
  the engine reads them from, the box writes itself, where a machine keeps its keys
  (`box/keys/<variable>`, each `0600`; its settings name them
  `{file:~/.kuvo-code/box/keys/<variable>}`): each once its host kept or removed it (one its host
  still keeps stays), under one lock across its processes (`run/.key-files.lock`); and, while
  `serve` runs, as it starts and twice a day after (a minute later while its host can't list them),
  each as its host has it then;
- Keep This Mac Awake as its own setting (`keepsAwake` in `box/work.json`, on unless you turn it
  off; `kuvo/work/settings`, "Work"): while a session works on its engine or with its coding agents,
  `serve` holds the Mac from falling asleep by itself (`caffeinate -i`, tied to it), looking every
  ten seconds; it lets go once none does, or the setting's off, and keeps the hold as it was while it
  can't tell (its engine recorded but not answering). It says so in `run/work-awake.json` (`{"by":
  <its pid>, "hold": <caffeinate's pid> | null}`), which every process's `awakeNow` reads. While
  that `serve` runs, its `kuvo-start` holds nothing for it and lets go of a hold it had; until then
  it holds the Mac awake on power as a machine's does.

Only the move below records `box/kind` (`mac`), or a new Mac's box made there from the start
(`rehome --new`). The keeper runs the move and the app makes a new Mac's box only with its
`movesOwnBox` on (off: #333, until what the app does for a box there is built), so this Mac's box
runs in the app's folder as above.

#### Moving this Mac's box

`box.rehome`. The box moves itself out of the app's folder into `~/.kuvo-code`, laid out as above,
with `kuvo-link.js rehome` (#333 pieces 2a and 2b), run by the engine's Bun (it opens the engine's
database with `bun:sqlite`). The box decides and does each step; the keeper only
stops the old box first and starts what's there after, and a client only shows it. Only on a Mac:
on Linux every command but `--status`, `--ready` and `--resume` refuses, saying there's nothing to
move (`--settled` works anywhere). Everything it keeps is in `~/.kuvo-code/updates/rehome`, made
first and never moved (an update's tidying of `updates` leaves it): its state (`state.json`, one
change at a time, synced), its journal (`journal.json`, synced before what it
says is done, and `journal.acts`, each act on a line, synced before it's done; a journal that's
there but can't be read is a move under way that nothing finishes by guessing), its lock (`lock`, the holder's pid: a second `rehome` waits for it, saying so
on stderr; one whose holder is gone is taken over), its staging folder, and the kept copies.

`kuvo-link.js rehome <root> …`, with `KUVO_HOME` the app's own box's folder (`<app folder>/box`)
and `root` the home's name in the home folder (`.kuvo-code`, or a test's), as `here` takes them.
Each prints one JSON line, `{result, message?, status}` (`--ready` always as below, with why where
it's not), and exits with what the keeper starts
then: 0 (`done`, `back`, `nothing`), what's there; 1 (`refused`, `failed`: it never began, or went
back, or something unforeseen went wrong before a move began), the box where it was; 3
(`stuck`: it stopped past the point it goes back from, or its journal can't be read, with why in
`state.json`'s `failed`; `--resume` carries it on), nothing; 4 (`waits`: another move holds the
lock), nothing; 2, a command it doesn't know. It goes by whether each process runs, never a pid
alone (it drops `KUVO_BOX`). A copy of the app (its box's folder not in `run.kuvo.code`) is
refused anything but `--status` on the real `~/.kuvo-code`.

- **`rehome <root> --release <folder> [--keeps-awake off]`**: the move, with the old box stopped
  (its engine, coding agents' bridge and `serve`; the keeper may hold its lock). `status` is as
  `kuvo/box/rehome` says it. `--release` is a folder with the box's own files in `bin/`
  (`kuvo-start` and `kuvo-link.js` at least, as files), copied into `~/.kuvo-code/bin` (links
  followed), with what the app put in its box's `bin` that the release doesn't bring (its catalog
  of servers, its bots' words); `--keeps-awake off`, Keep This Mac Awake off in the app,
  which the box's own setting says then (`keepsAwake: false` in `box/work.json`). Its steps:
  1. **Plan.** What moves where, journaled. It's refused, in words, while the old box hasn't
     started since the app updated (its `run/served.json`, which `serve` writes in the app's
     folder each time it starts, names another app version, from `KUVO_APP_VERSION`, or another
     link version), while something runs in it, without the box's files, while a box is in
     `~/.kuvo-code` (one with a card or a link.json that its Mac didn't remove, `here`'s `runs`
     not `gone`: both keep running as they are), when the app's folder and `~/.kuvo-code` aren't
     on one APFS disk, without room for the engine's database and its journal, × 1.1, plus
     200 MB, for a copy of the app (a demo's, a test's: its folder isn't `run.kuvo.code`) moving
     into the real `~/.kuvo-code`, when it isn't run by Bun, and while an engine database
     (`opencode*.db`) is of a schema the rewrite wasn't tried with: its migrations, counted and
     the last (`SELECT count(*), max(id) FROM migration`), must be one it knows (`59
     20261030054400_job`, the pinned engine 2.2.6's); one never used (no tables) is no refusal. A
     refusal counts as a try.
  2. **Install.** What's in `~/.kuvo-code` that isn't a box (one its Mac removed, or what was
     left) is set aside into `trash/earlier-box-<date>`, nothing deleted; never the desktop app's own
     folder (`desktop`), which isn't the box's.
  3. **Clone.** Each folder cloned (`cp -c`, for up to six hours: APFS clones, links as links,
     sockets left out) into
     staging: the box's own folder's entries (not `bin`, nor in `run` its processes' records:
     `keeper.*`, `serve.json`, `served.json`, `host.json`, `engine.json`, `bridge.json`, pids,
     locks, `socket.key`, the app's notes on its engine), the engine's `opencode/data`, `config`,
     `state`, `cache` and `workspace` to the same names, `engine`, `integrations`, `bots`,
     `wakes`, `groups`, `Chats` (to `chats`), `agents`, `phone-link.json`, the app's
     `Attachments` (into `attachments`), and the box's files. The app's folder isn't changed.
  4. **Rewrite.** In staging, by one path map (each placement's old folder to its new one, the
     longest first; a move back's the same map turned around). A path is rewritten where it's a
     path, whole: a value equal to an old folder or starting with it and `/`, a `file://` URL to
     one (kept as it was written, plainly or with `%20`; where both read the same, as in
     `~/.kuvo-code`, encoded), or an engine setting's `{file:…}`. Never a path among other words.
     - **The engine's database**, in one transaction (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, its foreign keys checked
       before it's kept, its log checkpointed after): `project.worktree`, `session_v2.directory`,
       `worktree.directory`, `project_directory.directory` and `permission.resource`; every path
       in the JSON of `project.sandboxes`, `session_v2.revert`, `summary_diffs`, `permission`,
       `metadata` and `workspace.binding`; and only the files sent (`files[*].source.uri` and
       `uri`) in `session_message.data` and `session_inbox.payload`. A project outside git, whose
       ID is its folder's (`sha1("directory:" + path)`), gets its new folder's, with every column
       naming it (`session_v2.project_id`, `permission`, `worktree`, `project_directory`,
       `event_sequence.aggregate_id`, `event.aggregate_id`) and its `shell/<id>` folder. Each
       worktree's snapshots (`snapshot/<project>/<sha1(path)>`) are renamed for its new path, and
       each snapshot's `config` (its worktree), `opencode.gitconfig` and `objects/info/alternates`
       rewritten.
     - **The box's own files**: every `.json`, `.jsonl` and `.ndjson` of the box's and its bridge's
       (keys too, as lists kept by folder are), the one-path `wakes/<session>/directory` and
       `bots/<bot>/directory`, a bot's `workspace/.opencode/opencode.json`, the engine's
       `config/opencode/opencode.json` and `updates/rollback/restore.sh`; an artifact's ID with its
       path (`art_` and its hash), and what's kept by a path's hash renamed: the bridge's
       `snapshots/<sha1(top)[:20]>`, `box/branch-backups/<sha1(top)[:20]>`, and usage's place in a
       log (`agents/usage/*-files/<sha256(log)[:32]>.json`). Never what's yours or an agent's own
       (chats' and bots' folders, sent files, the agents' settings folders, the trash, the vault),
       nor what the box makes anew as it starts (`run/fence`, the engine's plugins).
     - **Sent files merged beside one of the same name** (`<name> 2`, as placing does it): what
       names them names the new name.
     - **The coding agents' own, in the bridge's folder**: Kuvo Code's own Console sign-in's and
       an added Claude Code account's history of each folder (`projects/<slug>`, its slug as Claude Code makes it: each character but a
       letter or digit a `-`, one over 200 cut there with `-` and its 32-bit string hash in base
       36), an added Grok account's sessions (`sessions/<URL-encoded path>`), and Cursor's records
       of its agents' folders (`agents.ndjson`'s `cwd`). Codex needs nothing; Antigravity keeps
       its conversations by their IDs (whether it keeps anything else by a folder isn't known).
  5. **Check.** It goes back, saying why, if any of the box's own files still names the old place
     as a path, whole, if the database still does where it rewrites (a path column, a path whole
     in its JSON, a file sent), if the engine's database holds other counts of sessions or
     projects than its copy did before the rewrite, or if the engine (the version the box's keeper
     names, else the newest) started on a copy of the staged database (no schedules, jobs,
     accounts, keys or queued messages; nothing busy or suspended; settings, home and cache of its
     own; no network, through a proxy that's nowhere; at a port of its own, stopped as its stdin
     closes) doesn't list every session (page by page, and the archived), or has one of the newest 25 in
     another folder than the database says, or a moved one's folder isn't staged though it was
     there. Where the old place is still named but isn't the box's to change (people's and
     agents' words in the database and in files that moved, a diff's text, a command in a kept
     rule, a command's saved output), it's
     noted in `state.json`'s `leftovers` for support, never a failure.
  6. **Place.** Each staged folder renamed into place, merged entry by entry where one's there
     (a name in both keeps both: the one there keeps its name, the other is `<name> 2`); then
     `box/kind` (`mac`), last.
  7. **Fix.** What outside the box names its folders, each change journaled first, so going back
     puts it back: every worktree link between what was placed and a repository anywhere,
     repaired from the repository (`git worktree repair <worktree>` in its common folder; a link
     relative to where its end was, `worktree.useRelativePaths`, read from there), with what git
     writes outside what was placed, all of it before any repair, (the repository's `worktrees/<name>/gitdir`, or a
     worktree's `.git` outside the box) journaled as it was (`{act: "wrote", path, was}`; the old
     place is still there, so nothing prunes the link before); your own Claude Code's history of
     each folder that moved (`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `~/.claude`, `projects/<slug>`) and your
     own Grok's sessions (`$GROK_HOME` or `~/.grok`, `sessions/<URL-encoded path>`; one too long
     for a name stays) renamed, with Grok's index for searching them
     (`sessions/session_search.sqlite`, a cache naming each session's folder, which Grok makes anew
     when it's missing) set aside as `<name>.before-kuvo-move` and deleted once the old place is
     cleared (an added Grok account's, in the bridge's folder, is dropped from the staged copy);
     and each added Claude Code account's sign-in, the Keychain item
     named by its folder (`Claude Code-credentials-<sha256(NFC folder)[0:8]>`), copied under its
     new folder's name with `/usr/bin/security` as Claude Code writes it (`-U`, the value in hex),
     which the item trusts, so nothing's asked, written on its stdin (never a command line), read
     back to check (`{act: "keychain", service, account, aside?}`: going back deletes the copy; no
     secret is journaled: one there already under the new name with another value, an earlier
     box's, is kept aside as `<service>.before-kuvo-move` and put back from there going back, and
     deleted once the old place is cleared). A moved worktree's own `.git` is pointed at its record's
     new place before any repair (relative where it was), so no git links it back to the copy.
     The originals are deleted once the old place is cleared. Kuvo Code's own Anthropic Console
     sign-in (`agents/claude/console`) goes the same way as an added account's.
  8. **Clear.** Should something have started in the old box meanwhile, or anything changed, or
     been made, in what it clears since it cloned (the engine's `opencode` folder aside, which only
     the engine writes, and in `run` its processes' records: a file the app kept as you sent it,
     say, or its list of machines), it goes back first: nothing is left only in the kept copy. So the app writes nothing
     there during a move. From here it only goes forward. The originals, the app's `box` and `opencode`
     folders whole and each other, are renamed into `updates/rehome/kept/<date>/`, so nothing in
     the app's folder says a box ran there (`here`). Kept 30 days (`keptUntil`), then deleted (only ever what's in the move's own `kept`, where it
     really is, `..` and links followed, whatever `state.json` names; nothing where `kept` itself
     isn't a folder of its own), by
     `serve` as it starts and by `--ready`.
  9. **Done.** `state.json` says `done`, with what the app's executable still owes (`owed`:
     `keychain`, the Keychain's originals deleted, and `agent`, its own launch agent
     unregistered), then the journal, last.

  A failure before step 8 goes back: each act journaled is undone, last first (only where it was
  done), and staging is deleted, so the app's folder and `~/.kuvo-code` are exactly as before, but
  for the move's own `state.json` saying so.
- **`--resume`**: a move (or move back) that stopped part way, finished: back before step 8,
  forward from it. Going back is done again from the start if it's cut short itself. While one is
  unfinished, `here` says `{verdict: "moving", use: "wait"}`: a keeper and app that know it start
  no box (an app from before #333 piece 5 doesn't know `wait`, and never runs a move). Gone back, `failed`; finished, `done` or `back`; nothing to finish, `nothing`, making nothing.
- **`--back`**: Move Back, with the box in `~/.kuvo-code` stopped: the same steps the other way, on
  the data as it is now (what was made since goes back too), into the app's folder it came from
  (`state.json`'s `from`). What the move merged goes back where it came from; each other entry of
  `~/.kuvo-code` to where the move took it from (`updates` an entry at a time, never the move's
  own folder; never the desktop app's `desktop`, which stays), any other into the app's `box`, without `box/kind` or the key files written from the
  Keychain (`box/keys`, `box/bot-keys`, which go as it clears, never kept), nor a box the move set
  aside in `trash` (it stays); folders made again as they were in the move's kept copy.
  Where the app made a file again meanwhile, the box's keeps the name and the app's is kept beside
  it (`<name> 2`). Then `~/.kuvo-code`'s originals and its `bin` are kept as above, and
  `state.json` says `back`, owing `keychain` (the items put back) and `agent` (registered again).
  Refused while that box runs (its keeper, `box.pid`, aside: it's what runs it), or while the app's folder has a box of its own again; a refusal
  answers Move Back (`asked` cleared, `failed` says why). One that fails leaves the box moved
  (`done`, with `failed`). Moved back, it moves again only on Move Now, until a move's done.
- **`--ready [--release <folder>]`**: whether the keeper should run it now, asked with the box
  running (its running isn't a refusal here: the keeper stops it first): `{ready, how:
  "move"|"back"|"resume"|null, why?, status}`. One unfinished first (`resume`); then Move Back
  asked (`back`, unless it would be refused: then that answers it); then not while a move would
  be refused; then Move Now asked (`move`, whatever runs: the app asked you before stopping it).
  Otherwise not after three tries (it waits for Move Now), nor before the next (an hour after one
  fails), nor while something works on the box (a conversation on its engine or with its coding
  agents, or one that can't be told) or a browser waits on you. Only waiting for a quiet moment
  does it note it waits (`waiting`, `waitingSince`), and three days of that (waiting, or failing
  meanwhile) is `overdue`.
- **`--status`**: `kuvo/box/rehome`'s answer. **`--settled keychain|agent`**: one of `owed`, done
  (`{settled, status}`).
- **`--new --release <folder> [--keeps-awake off]`**: a new Mac's box, made in `~/.kuvo-code` from
  the start, with nothing to move (the app, as it first opens): refused, saying why and changing
  nothing (not even making `~/.kuvo-code`), where a box of the app's own ran in its folder or its
  engine kept your sessions (`here`'s, with `KUVO_ENGINE_DATA`: that one moves instead), where a box
  is in `~/.kuvo-code` (as a move is, and also one with no card yet that says it's a machine's in
  `box/kind` or has keys of its own in `box/keys`), for a copy of the app into the real `~/.kuvo-code`, without
  the release's files, or before the engine is in the app's folder. Under the move's lock: what's
  there that isn't a box set aside into `trash/earlier-box-<date>` (as the move's install step
  does; never the desktop app's `desktop`), the release's `bin` put in place whole, the app's `engine` cloned beside it (copied where
  the disk can't clone; the app's stays), Keep This Mac Awake off where it's off in the app, then
  `box/kind` (`mac`), last, saying it's being made meanwhile (`updates/rehome/new`, written before
  anything's set aside): one cut short is made again from the start, what it left set aside in the
  trash like the rest, nothing deleted (but its own scratch copies, `bin.new` and `engine.new`).
  The mark counts only where no move has been (no
  `state.json` state, no journal) and no box of anyone's has been there since (a machine's kind,
  keys of its own, a card); a move's install step sets it aside, journaled, so a box moved there
  later is never taken for a making cut short. All of it holds the move's lock to the end; one that
  fails part way (not cut short) takes its mark away again. `done` (exit 0); made already,
  `nothing`. The box's installer ("Installing this computer's box") makes it the same way with
  the engine it took itself rather than the app's folder's, and what it staged
  (`updates/install`) is never set aside. No `state.json`: nothing moved, so there's nothing to move back. **`--new --check`**,
  changing nothing: `{ready, made, why?}`, `made` once its kind says so with no move under way (a
  move writes it before it's done: never `made` then), `ready` where it would be made now (the
  release aside).
- **`--failed <why>`**: a try the keeper gave up on before the move began (the Keychain's copies, the
  release), counted as a refusal is (`tries`, `nextTry` an hour on, `failed`), so `--ready` waits
  for the next: `{noted, status}`, `noted` false once a move's under way or done.
- A release (`--release`, to move or make one) must bring the helper,
  `bin/Kuvo Helper.app/Contents/MacOS/Kuvo Helper`: without it nothing would start the box in
  its home, so it's refused, saying so.

**What the keeper does** (#333 piece 5, with the app's `movesOwnBox` on; off, nothing here happens
and the keeper is as "The keeper" says). Everything above it asks of the box with this app's own
`kuvo-link.js`, by the engine's Bun (the box's, once the app's moved with it):

- **As it starts**, holding a lock of its own in the app's caches (`keeper-move.lock`: a second
  keeper goes), before it writes anything in the app's folder (its records there would say a box of
  the app's ran there again): `--status`. A move under way (`moving`, `clearing`, or a
  journal not `done`) is finished first (`--resume`); one that's `done` is finished off (below), and
  the keeper retires without starting anything (so does one that finds a new Mac's box there, its
  helper's launch agent left as it is); otherwise copies of the app's Keychain items a try
  left (their journal `copying` or `copied`) are taken away by the helper (`keys uncopy`), and the
  box starts in the app's folder as always. While a move holds on (`stuck`, `waits`, or what's owed
  can't be done yet), it starts nothing, and looks again every ten minutes.
- **Running**, at its first look and every ten minutes after, and at once when `state.json`
  changes (Move Now asked), unless an update waits for it or something's under way: `--ready`. Ready
  (`move` or `resume`), it makes the box's release (the files `scripts/box-release.sh` writes now,
  which the app wrote itself then, with the helper the app carries) and asks `--ready --release` with it, the box still running; still ready, it stops
  the engine, the bridge and `serve` (holding `run/box.lock`, so the
  app starts none meanwhile, and answering every control but `status` `503` with a `message`,
  Stop Background Work too, its `status` saying `moving: true`, and `movingWhy` while the move holds
  on, stuck part way say, as the box said it; the app's window says it's moving, with why, in its
  starting text, not as a failure), copies the app's Keychain items for the helper
  (`KeychainMove`; an earlier try's copies taken away first, items an earlier box left cleared once
  with `keys clear`) and has the helper read them back (`keys check`), then runs `--release`, with
  `--keeps-awake off` where it's off in the app. What it gives up on before `--release` (the release
  not made, the copies) it says with `--failed`, so the box's tries count it.
- **Moved** (`done`), and whenever it finds the box moved: the helper's launch agent put in place
  and loaded (`helper install --load --app <its bundle ID>`, run with `KUVO_HOME` the box's home;
  one loaded already is started if it isn't running, `helper start`, as one that found the box
  moving went), so the box runs from its home at once; the Keychain's originals deleted
  (`deleteOriginals`), then `--settled keychain`; `--settled agent`, then its own launch agent
  unregistered, and it exits as Stop Background Work does. Each only once the one before is done
  (the box said it's settled), else tried again. Where the Keychain won't
  change (locked), it stays registered and running nothing, looking again every ten minutes; the box
  runs meanwhile, from the helper's copies.
- **Not moved** (`refused`, `failed`, a copy the helper couldn't read; moved back, `back`): the
  helper takes the copies away, and the box starts in the app's folder again (the bridge too).
- **Stopped** meanwhile (SIGTERM, as you log out): it starts nothing again as it goes; the next
  keeper finishes what the move left, as above.
- **The app**, with `movesOwnBox` on, asks `here` before it starts a box (the keeper too, with either
  flag on). While `here` says `moving` it starts nothing and says so in its starting text (why it
  holds on, from `--status`'s `failed`, which a move under way has only once it's stuck), asking
  `here` again, less often as it goes on (5 seconds, up to a minute); a copy that attaches in place
  but doesn't move boxes says so once, as a failure. On a new Mac it asks `--new --check`, makes the box with `--new` where it's `ready`,
  and has its helper load; where the box says it's `made`, it registers no keeper of its own
  (`BackgroundWork`). Finding this Mac's box in its home stopped, it starts it through its helper
  (`helper start`, else `helper install --load`), never by running its `kuvo-start` (where the box
  can't say whether it's a Mac's, nothing).
- **What piece 8 adds** (drafts first): the move's own view (waiting, moving, done, didn't finish,
  Move Now…), Settings' "This Mac's box" (starts at login, where it is, Move Back, Uninstall…),
  permissions for the helper, the `two` state, and the phone drawing `moving` (and the Mac away
  for the move itself as moving, not offline).

A Mac's box in a home of its own starts its bridge as a machine's (`KUVO_AGENTS_REMOTE`), but the
coding agents' default accounts stay yours, in your home (`~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, `~/.grok`), as
the app's box keeps them: only on a machine are they in the bridge's folder (`<agent>/home`).

`kuvo/box/rehome`: `GET` answers `{state, way, step, tries, nextTry, waitingSince, overdue,
failed, movedAt, keptUntil, owed, asked, from, to, progress?, dropped?, steps?, signIns?}`. `state`: null before anything, `waiting`,
`moving` or `clearing` (under way, at `step`, or a journal that can't be read: `plan`, `install`, `keys`, `clone`, `upgrade`, `database`, `rewrite`, `check`,
`place`, `fix`, `clear`, `done`; `keys`, `upgrade` and `database` only in a move the box runs whole itself), `done`, `failed` (gone back; `failed` (cleared as a move begins: while one's under way, why it's stuck) says `{at, step,
message}`), or `back`; `way`, `move` or `back`; `nextTry`, `waitingSince`, `movedAt` and
`keptUntil` in ms; `owed`, what's still to be settled (`keychain`, `agent`; and after a move the box ran itself, `start` and `passwords`); `asked`, `now` or `back`, until it's acted on. With `box.rehome.run`: `progress`, while a
move the box runs itself is under way, `{step, title, index, of}`: the step, what's happening in
words a client shows as they are (the box's own: a client keeps none of its own for a step),
which step it is (from 1) and of how many, else null; and `dropped`, what that move didn't carry
of what an earlier Kuvo Code kept, each in words a client shows once (none: `[]`); and `steps`,
every step of a move the box runs itself, in order, each `{step, title}` in the same words, so a
client lists them ahead of where the move is (`progress.index` counts into it, from 1; where it
stopped is `failed.step`). With `box.rehome.signIns`: `signIns`, how bringing an earlier Kuvo
Code's saved sign-ins over stands ("Saved sign-ins", below): `{state: "asking"}` while it runs
(macOS may be asking you about them), else how it last went, `{state: "done", at, added, kept}`
(how many came into the vault, and how many stayed in the Keychain) or `{state: "failed", at,
message}` (words to show as they are; said only while `passwords` is still owed), else null. The app's box in its folder
answers for the `~/.kuvo-code` it moves to (the real app's folder alone, `run.kuvo.code`; a copy,
only for the home `KUVO_MACHINE_ROOT` names, else nothing: it never reads or asks the real one's); a box in a home of its own, for its own. `POST
{now: true}` asks for Move Now and `{back: true}` (once it's moved) for Move Back, answering the
same: only from Kuvo Code itself (the app, or `box route`; 403 from a phone), 409 with why when it
can't (a machine, nothing to move back, or a move the box ran itself, whose earlier Kuvo Code's
folder was never changed). With `box.rehome.signIns`, `POST {signIns: true}` brings an earlier
Kuvo Code's saved sign-ins over now (`rehome <root> --sign-ins`, started in a process of its own;
"Saved sign-ins", below): only from Kuvo on this same Mac, over the box's own server
(`x-kuvo-from: app`; 403 from anything else, a phone included: macOS asks about them on the Mac),
and only a Mac's own box in a home of its own. `202` with the status (`signIns: {state:
"asking"}`) once it's started; `200` with it where one runs already (none is started beside it);
409 with why where none are owed. A client asks only when you act on it, having said that macOS
may ask about each.

**The whole move, run by the box** (`box.rehome.run`, #713). Kuvo Code 0.5 to 0.7.2 and
0.8.0-beta.1 had no box and no keeper, and the app that takes their place (the desktop app) runs
neither: so the box moves an earlier Kuvo Code's sessions and settings itself, doing what the
keeper did around the move above. Nothing runs on such a Mac until it succeeds, so every refusal
says what to do, and trying again is yours: no wait between tries, no cap (tries are counted).

`kuvo-link.js rehome <root> --run --app <bundle> --release <folder> --engine <folder>`, with
`KUVO_HOME` the box's home (as the installer runs it; `install --move`, below, starts it in a
session of its own and follows it). `--app` is the app that carries the release: its ID names the
earlier Kuvo Code's folder (`~/Library/Application Support/<ID>`), and it brings `kuvo-keys`
(`Contents/MacOS/kuvo-keys`); `--release` and `--engine`, what the installer unpacked and fetched
(`updates/install`). One JSON line, `{result, message?, status, started?}`, and the same exits as
above. Only on a Mac.

- **The earlier Kuvo Code's folder is never changed.** Everything is cloned into staging and
  worked on there; nothing in it is renamed, written, or opened for writing, and its engine's
  database isn't opened at all (reading one that keeps a log beside it can rewrite the log's
  index): what the move needs to know of it, it reads from a clone. So nothing is cleared and
  no copy is kept: there's no `keptUntil`, and no Move Back.
- **What it moves**: an earlier Kuvo Code's data with no box of its own (`app-07`), or a keeper
  build's box (`app-box`: `box` in the app's folder). A machine's box already in `~/.kuvo-code`
  with an earlier Kuvo Code's data beside it (`two`) isn't put together yet: refused, saying so,
  before anything is stopped, with nothing noted in that box's home.
- **First**: an earlier try is finished (one stopped before `clear` goes back, and this one
  starts afresh; one at `clear` or later is carried on). A keeper build's keeper is asked to stop
  (`POST stop` on its control, `run/keeper.json`, only ever at `127.0.0.1`), waited for 30
  seconds, then stopped by its pid; all of it only while `ps` says that pid is a keeper (`--box`
  in its command line): a record left by one that's gone names nothing to stop. Then everything
  else of the earlier Kuvo Code's still running, whatever started it and whether or not it left a
  record, found by what each runs (`lsof`, once, never by a name: a program in its own `engine`
  or `box` folder, its engine's, its bridge's and its server's, never one of yours in a worktree
  or chat there; or in an app with its bundle ID and another program's name than the one moving
  it, so no copy of this app is), but the move and what started it, once what refuses it
  whatever runs was checked: its keeper's launch agent (`<ID>.box`) let go
  of, each asked to stop (`SIGTERM`), then made to after 15 seconds; one still running refuses
  the move. A program that isn't Kuvo's with a file in its folder open to write in refuses it
  too, named as you know it (its app's name, else its command's: "Xcode is still using your
  earlier Kuvo Code's files. Quit it, then try again.", a program that isn't an app by its
  command, in quotes)). What it found and stopped
  goes to the move's log (`run.log`) alone, never on screen.
- **Refused**, changing nothing, each in words to show: a copy of the app into the real
  `~/.kuvo-code` (or Kuvo Code itself into another); the release not whole (each file as its
  `box.json` says, with its helper) or its engine not fetched ("Check that this Mac is online");
  Kuvo Code itself without `kuvo-keys`; something of the old keeper's still running, or something
  running in `~/.kuvo-code`; two disks, or one that isn't APFS; no room (the database and its log
  × 1.1, plus 200 MB); a program that has the earlier Kuvo Code's database open to write in (`lsof` on
  `opencode*.db` and its `-wal` and `-shm`, by how each has it open: "Quit Kuvo Code wherever
  it's open", which programs in the move's log alone; one that only reads it, a backup or
  Spotlight, holds nothing back); and a database
  of a schema nobody tried (the pinned engine's, or one it brings up to date: `50
  20261010180456_project_time_archived`, engine 2.0.32's).
- **Its steps**, journaled as the move's above, with three more:
  - `plan`, `install` as above; what moves is as above too, and besides it the app's list of bots
    (`bots.json`, beside the bots' folder, where the box takes a job kept only there as it
    starts), the files an imported engine's settings name (`opencode-files`), and the engine
    from what the installer fetched, never the earlier Kuvo Code's (which stays where it is).
  - **`keys`**: `kuvo-keys copy --home <home> --helper <the release's Kuvo Helper.app>`, run by
    this very process (it holds the move's lock, which `kuvo-keys` checks), then `Kuvo Helper
    keys check`. Items an earlier box left (`leftovers`) or copies an earlier try left
    (`journal`) are taken away by the helper once (`keys clear`, `keys uncopy`) and the copy
    made again. A Keychain that won't stops the move here, before the long part, in words by
    `kuvo-keys`'s `reason`: `locked` (only when it is) "Your Keychain is locked…"; `not-allowed`
    (macOS kept an item from `kuvo-keys`, or you didn't allow it) "Kuvo needs your OK…"; anything
    else, "Kuvo couldn't take this Mac's keys along…". What it said (`error`, the item, and
    `status`, the OSStatus) goes to the move's log alone, never on screen. A `kuvo-keys` signed
    differently from the Kuvo Code that made the items (an Apple Development build after a
    Developer ID one: the items' list names that one's certificate) lets macOS ask you, once per
    item it reads (here and in `passwords`), whether it may use it: only where reading it without
    asking was refused, searching only the item's own keychain while it's unlocked, and what you
    allowed must then hold without asking (Always Allow: what comes after, deleting the originals
    and later runs, never asks), or it's `not-allowed`. Nothing else it does asks, and a locked
    Keychain is never asked to be unlocked. Up to thirty minutes for those answers. A move that goes back takes the copies away (`keys uncopy`).
    Skipped, said nowhere, where the app brings no `kuvo-keys` and isn't Kuvo Code itself (a
    copy has no keys of Kuvo Code's own).
  - `clone`, then what it holds is counted (below).
  - **`upgrade`**: what the earlier Kuvo Code kept in its own files and preferences, brought
    into the box's own files in the staged copy ("What the move carries", below). What it
    doesn't carry is said (`dropped`).
  - **`database`**: an engine database of an earlier schema brought up to date by the engine
    itself: the release's engine started once on the staged data with nothing else of yours
    (as the check's is: settings, home, state and cache of its own, nowhere to reach) and
    stopped as soon as it answers. It must then be of the pinned schema, and hold no fewer
    sessions, projects, messages, rules, worktrees or waiting messages than before, or the move
    goes back. (It acts on nothing it finds: a run that was cut short is marked suspended, as
    at any start.) What the engine's own update lets go of is said (`dropped`): the rows of a
    table that isn't there after (`session_pending`, messages waiting on a session in 2.0.32).
  - `rewrite`, `check` as above; and the counts taken after the clone hold: sessions, projects,
    messages, the engine's worktrees and the box's records of them, bots, wake-ups (a
    conversation's, a bot's), vault items, accounts added to coding agents, group chats; none
    may be fewer (`state.json`'s `counts` keeps both, for support).
  - `place`, `fix` as above.
  - `clear`: nothing is cleared. First, should anything have been written in what it cloned
    since the clone began (by its time of last change, `mtime`: a file written, added or taken
    away; a change of attributes alone, or SQLite's shared-memory index `*.db-shm`, which any
    program that only reads a database rewrites, loses nothing and is never counted), or a
    program have its database open to write in, it goes back. Then, by itself and with its
    progress still said, it stops what of the earlier Kuvo Code's runs again (as **First**
    does), refuses where a program that isn't Kuvo's has what changed open (named, as there),
    and runs again from the start, three times in all; then "Something kept changing your
    sessions while Kuvo copied them, so nothing was moved. Quit the earlier Kuvo Code wherever
    it's open, then try again." One try is counted, however many rounds. What changed goes to `run.log` alone. From here it only goes forward.
  A failure that's the person's to act on is said as it is (`failed.message`); any other, in
  one sentence ("Kuvo couldn't move your sessions this time, and left everything as it was.
  Try again."), with what went wrong in `updates/rehome/run.log`.
- **Done**, then what it owes that needs no one's answer is settled: `start` (`helper start`, by
  the link just put in place: `started` in the answer; in a home that isn't the real one nothing
  outside the folder is written, and nothing's owed); `keychain` (`kuvo-keys delete-originals`,
  which never asks); `agent` (a keeper build's launch agent, `<ID>.box`, let go of with
  `launchctl bootout`). What the installer staged (`updates/install`) goes once the box has
  started. Where one of these couldn't be settled yet, the answer's `message` says so in a
  sentence (why is in `run.log`). **A move that's done is never run again**, for what it owes or
  anything else: `install --status` says `new` for its start where its helper isn't in place,
  and null otherwise (`install --move` does nothing); the box settles `start`, `keychain` and
  `agent` itself as it starts (`rehome <root> --settle`, in a process of its own; `start`
  because it runs, and only then what the installer staged goes; `passwords` where the earlier
  Kuvo Code's preferences say it had them in a vault already), so opening or updating Kuvo never
  waits on the Keychain. The saved sign-ins
  are never the move's: macOS may ask you about each, so they come over only when you ask.
- **Saved sign-ins** (`passwords`): owed only where there may be some. Where the earlier Kuvo
  Code had brought them into a vault itself (`passwords.movedToVault` in its preferences, read
  without the Keychain, at the move or as the box starts), or your login keychain, found unlocked
  a moment before (the move's own `keys` step, or `delete-originals` just done), lists none
  (`security find-internet-password -c KUVO <login.keychain-db>`: that keychain alone, by what's
  listed, no password read, so macOS asks nothing), `passwords` is settled; else the move says
  in `dropped` that they stay in your Keychain for now, and it's owed until you bring them over (`POST kuvo/box/rehome {signIns: true}`, above, which runs
  `kuvo-link.js rehome <root> --sign-ins` with `KUVO_HOME` the box's home). That holds the move's
  lock while it runs (which `kuvo-keys` checks), and nothing waits for it: `install --status`
  takes a lock held by `--sign-ins` or `--settle` (by the holder's command line) for no move at
  all, and its progress for none. A try that doesn't finish, for whatever reason, says so in
  `signIns`. It finds `kuvo-keys` in the app the move took its data with,
  else in Kuvo's desktop app as it last opened with this box (`run/app.json`'s `desktop`).
  `kuvo-keys passwords` says the sign-ins an earlier Kuvo
  Code kept before the vault down its standard output, a pipe this process reads, macOS asking
  you about each where it would (up to thirty minutes); each goes
  from memory to the box's own server on this Mac (`run/serve.json`; `POST kuvo/vault/items`, a sign-in of its site, to sign in with only,
  named for its site, then its account, then numbered). One whose site and account the vault
  has is left as it is; one under four characters, which the vault keeps none of, is said
  (`dropped`); a site the earlier Kuvo Code let agents sign in to alone, with that account,
  stays so (`POST kuvo/vault/grants`, everyone, `own`: asked again at a later run where the
  sign-in is there without it). Each password is checked against the vault's
  (`POST kuvo/vault/items/<id>/same`, which shows nothing and notes nothing in its activity)
  before `kuvo-keys delete-originals --password <site> --account <account>` removes its
  Keychain original (the verified password arrives on stdin). One the vault keeps differently
  (it had another password for that site and account) or refuses (`400`: a site it can't keep),
  those the Keychain has more than one of for a site and account and one not valid UTF-8 (said
  with U+FFFD in its place; neither is given to the vault), and one `delete-originals` finds
  changed (`copy-missing`) keep their originals, are counted in `dropped`, and the rest go on. Done, `passwords` is
  settled and `signIns` says `done`; otherwise it stays owed and `signIns` says `failed`, in words
  by why: your Keychain locked; macOS didn't let `kuvo-keys` read them (you clicked Deny); its
  question went unanswered; Kuvo's app not found on this Mac; anything else, "Try again". Why
