  itself goes to `run.log` alone (it may name a site or an account). A try cut short adds nothing
  twice. Never written to a file, by either.
- **What the move carries** (the `upgrade` step; each reads the app's folder and its
  preferences, `~/Library/Preferences/<ID>.plist`, asked of the system for Kuvo Code itself, and
  writes only in staging; each leaves what a box already had as it is; preferences that are
  there and can't be read stop the move, which goes back, never taken for none):
  - that you've had the first run (`run/welcomed.json`, "Your setup"): always, since anyone with
    an earlier Kuvo Code's sessions has;
  - your projects (`projectFolders`, `projectSettings`: order, names, extra folders, Run
    commands) → `box/projects.json`; never a bot's folder or a machine's (`ssh://…`); one kept
    only for its settings stays removed;
  - worktrees' records (`worktrees`, those whose folder is still there) and removed ones
    (`removedWorktrees`) → `box/worktrees.json` (`worktrees`, `handedOver`);
  - your machines (`machines`) → `machines.json`, by `destination`; with none, an empty list
    where there's no list yet (no list beside `phone-link.json`'s machines would read as one
    that can't be told, "Machines");
  - Settings › Git (`git.branchPrefix`, `git.commitInstructions`, `git.pullRequestInstructions`)
    → the engine's settings, where they have none, once (`box/git.json`'s `moved`);
  - integrations' keys named in the engine's settings (and each bot's) where the app wrote them
    (its temporary folder) or as a version before named them (`{env:KUVO_KEY_…}`) → named where
    the box writes them (`{file:~/.kuvo-code/box/keys/KUVO_KEY_…}`);
  - the engine's plugin, which the app wrote beside the engine's settings at each start
    (`config/opencode/plugins/kuvo-code.js`): the release's, in its place;
  - Keep This Mac Awake, off (`keepsAwake`) → `box/work.json`; Ask First as new sessions' start
    (`toolApproval: askFirst`) → `box/approval.json`'s `last`; what the app added to the
    engine's settings once (`engine.defaultsAdded`, `engine.searchMovedToExa`) →
    `box/defaults-added`;
  - "Let my devices connect" as this Mac's link had it set (`phoneLink`), and a relay of your
    own (`phoneLink.relay`) → `run/mac-link.json`; never set, nothing is written, and the box
    starts with its own (on);
  - this Mac's bots: `bot.json` (0.6 wrote none), `session`, `directory` and `via` in each
    one's folder, where missing;
  - personalities (`personalities.json`, `personalities-removed.json`) → met with
    `bots/personalities.json` by the library's own rule;
  - this Mac's group chats (`groups.json`, `groups/<id>.json`) → `groups/<id>/messages.json`
    then `groups/<id>/group.json`, as "This Mac's own group chats" says, with what a bot was
    still to forget (`groupMemoryWaiting`) in `groups/pending-memory.json`; a chat that moved
    between computers as the app last quit (`movesUnderWay`) is `held`;
  - letters (`agent-letters.json`, `agent-messages.json`, `agent-letters-seen.json`) →
    `run/outbox/sending`, `run/letters-seen.json`, for machines whose boxes talk to others
    (`phone-link.json` says `peers`), as the app's own hand-over went;
  - the usage panel's settings (its layout, total spend, notifications, Codex's fallback model)
    → `agents/usage/settings.json`, by the box's own import.
  The browser's history and settings are taken by the box as it first starts ("The browser's
  data"), from the earlier Kuvo Code's folder, which is still there.
- **Said, not carried** (`dropped`, each only where it applies): messages typed and not sent;
  websites signed in to in the app's browser; changes to a machine's bot not yet sent there
  (`botEditsWaiting`: held edits are sealed with the link's secret); a project's terminal app;
  a move left at `switched`; sign-outs and clean-ups still owed to machines that were away
  (`machineSignOuts`, `machines.waiting`); what the app kept for its machines' projects and
  worktrees (`ssh://…` entries: names, folders, Run commands, which project a worktree's
  sessions belong to); an API key pasted into the usage panel (its own Keychain items: said where the panel had
  OpenRouter or Z.ai connected); starred
  models; a list the app set aside as unreadable (a file, or its machines'); usage keys or a proxy set
  up by hand (`Usage/*.json`); a group chat that couldn't be read; a machine's bot's seat in a
  group chat (it takes one again where it lives); and messages for machines that were away. Where
  new sessions ran everything without asking (`toolApproval` unset or `approveAll`), they start
  with Auto now, unsaid. The rest of the app's preferences are its window's own.

#### Installing this computer's box

An app that carries the box's release ("Updates": `boxes.json` and the pack, in a folder) carries
`kuvo-install` beside them, a POSIX shell script `scripts/box-release.sh` writes there from
`box/src/install`. It's how a computer with no box gets one, and how the app learns what a
computer holds before it starts or attaches to anything. The app runs it and draws its lines; it
decides nothing itself.

`sh <folder>/kuvo-install status|new|move|update [--now] [--app <bundle>] [--root <name>]`

- `--app`: the app's bundle (a full path), on a Mac: its bundle ID names the folder an earlier
  Kuvo Code kept its data in (`~/Library/Application Support/<ID>`, `S` below). Linux has none.
- `--root`: the box's home in your home folder (default `.kuvo-code`, `K` below; a demo copy
  names its own). On Linux it's always `.kuvo-code`: the keeper names no other.
- Kuvo Code itself (`run.kuvo.code`) goes with the real `~/.kuvo-code` only (your account's own,
  whatever `HOME` says and however the folder is written: through a link, or on a Mac's disk in
  other letters' case; where the account's home can't be told, it's refused), and a copy of the app never with it; on a Mac the app must be named.
  The script checks this first, from the bundle's ID, before it writes anything: either mismatch,
  or no app, is `{"result": "refused", "message"}` (exit 1) with nothing made, not even the
  folder. (The link checks it again.) Linux has no bundle to tell a copy by.
- It prints JSON lines: `{"step": "checking" | "engine", "title"}` while it works (the pack being checked
  and unpacked, "Getting ready"; the engine being fetched, "Downloading the engine": `title` is
  words an app shows as they are), then one answer, last. Exit 0; 1 refused or failed,
  with `message` in words to show as they are; 4 when another move holds the lock (`result`
  `"waits"`). Exit 2 when it isn't asked as above: a usage line on standard error and no JSON
  line (an app's mistake, never a user's). What the shell's part refuses or fails itself (the
  refusals above, a damaged copy, an engine that can't be had) is `{"result", "message"}` alone,
  with no `verdict` or `status`: nothing has judged the computer yet.
- Every `KUVO_*` variable it was started with is dropped (but a test's, `KUVO_TEST_*`).

**The shell's part**, since a new computer has nothing to run JavaScript with:

1. `boxes.json`'s manifest is read (its version, its engine, this system's engine URL and npm
   integrity, the pack's SHA-256). Its signature isn't checked again here: on a Mac the app's own
   signature seals the folder; elsewhere it's as trusted as the app that carries it.
2. The pack (`box-<version>.tar.gz`, beside it) is checked against that SHA-256 and unpacked into
   `K/updates/install/release`: beside it first (`release.new.<pid>`, this run's own), renamed
   whole, marked with the pack's sum (`.whole`), so the same release isn't unpacked twice and one
   cut short is never used. Two runs at once each unpack and fetch their own, and the first in
   place stays; what a run that's gone left is removed by the next.
3. The engine: `K/updates/install/engine/<version>/opencode` if it was fetched before; else, for
   `status`, the box's own as it is (`K/engine/<version>/opencode`, or whichever version it has:
   a computer with a box is told how it stands offline too, with nothing fetched); else it's
   fetched from the manifest's URL (`https` only, by `curl` or `wget`; a `file:` URL is a test's,
   taken only outside the real home with `KUVO_TEST_INSTALL_FILE_ENGINE` set), checked against the integrity
   (SHA-512), run once (`--version`), and only then put there. A copy of the box's own of that
   version is taken for `new`. Where it can't be had and the box has an engine, the box's own
   answers: a box already made needs no other, and a new one says the engine couldn't be
   downloaded.
4. `kuvo-link.js install --<verb> --root <name> --release <folder> --engine <folder> [--app
   <bundle>]` from that release, on that engine, with `KUVO_HOME` the box's home.

**`update [--now]`** (`computers.update.here`): the box that's there brought up to the release
the app carries, by that release's own update (`kuvo-link.js update --installer --from <folder>
[--now]`, on the box's own engine as `status` runs: the update fetches a new engine itself). It's
how an app brings this computer's box up when that box is from before it took an offered release
as soon as nothing's at work (it lacks `computers.update.here`). Refused with no box there. Without
`--now` it waits, in that process, until nothing is at work there (as "Updates" counts it, looked
at every 15 seconds), saying so: `{"step": "waiting", "title", "confirm": {title, message,
label}}` (the words for an app's chip, and what Update Now asks first), and checks again as it
updates, waiting again where work began meanwhile; it ends quietly once the app that ran it is
gone (the box takes the offered release itself then). With `--now`, an update the box is making
already is waited for first. With `--now` it doesn't
wait. Then `{"step": "updating", "title"}`, and last the update's answer (`{"result": "updated" |
"current" | "blocked" | "busy" | "off" | "failed", "message"?}`, exit 0 for `updated` and
`current`, else 1). A try that failed before anything changed in a way that passes (a download
that broke off, the engine not stopped) is made once more 15 seconds on; only a second failure is
said. Updated, the running bridge goes for the keeper to start the new one.

It writes only in `K/updates/install`, which goes once a box is made from it. Beside a box
that's there already (`ours`, `machine`, `two`, nothing to run), the engine it fetched goes once
that box has the same engine itself, and the installer runs on the box's own from then on; the
unpacked release (a few megabytes) stays, one at a time, so it isn't unpacked at each ask.

**`status`** → `{"verdict", "verb", "status", "message"?, "offer"?}`: what this computer holds, from its folders alone;
`verb` is what to run next (`"new"`, `"move"` or null), and `status` is how a move stands
(`kuvo/box/rehome`'s answer), for its step to be drawn (and every step ahead of it, `status.steps`).
`message`, for `two` alone: words an app shows as they are before it goes on, since the earlier
Kuvo Code's sessions stay where they are, unseen. It leaves installed and earlier Kuvo Code
data alone during ordinary inspection. It stages in `K/updates/install`, as above. The
two refusals above (no app named on a Mac; a copy and the real one mixed) say nothing of what's
there.

A fresh install makes the local box the primary of a new setup. A client with no local box
and an empty saved computer list offers to add a computer. An offline saved computer still
counts as part of the setup.

The last computer's wipe keeps a private receipt beside the erased data root. For a Mac Box
in the app's folder, the root is its own Application Support directory, including the Box's
configured data kept alongside it. The Box refuses app-owned layouts with data roots outside
that directory. The receipt binds the accepted operation to the directory identity and
records stopping, detaching, and erasing it. The installer waits for an active wipe and
resumes an authorized interrupted wipe. After erasure, `status` returns
`offer: "reinstall-local"`, `verb: null` and `wipeReceipt: {setup, operation}`. Choose `new`
to reinstall and create a fresh setup. A successful start clears the receipt.

| `verdict` | What's here | `verb` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `waits` | another process holds the move's lock for a move (never what a move that's done left to finish, `rehome --settle` or `--sign-ins`: nothing waits for those) | null |
| `stuck` | a move stopped at `clear` or later, or its journal can't be read | `move` |
| `moving` | a move stopped before `clear` | `move` |
| `ours` | a Mac's own box in `K` (`box/kind` says `mac`) | never `move`: a move that's done is never run again, whatever it still owes (`status.owed`: the box settles what asks nothing as it runs, and saved sign-ins come over when you ask); `new` while its helper isn't in place (its launch agent's file missing, or launchd not having it: a making cut short after the box was made, a start launchd refused, Login Items off for it); else null: the app attaches |
| `back` | it was moved back | null: it moves again when you ask |
| `two` | a machine's box in `K`, and an earlier Kuvo Code's data in `S` | null: both stay (putting them together isn't built yet) |
| `machine` | a machine's box in `K`, nothing in `S` | null: the app attaches to it in place |
| `app-box` | a box of the app's own ran in `S/box` (a keeper build's) | `move` |
| `app-07` | an earlier Kuvo Code's data in `S`, no box of its own there (0.5 to 0.7, 0.8.0-beta.1) | `move` |
| `fresh` | none of these | `new` |

- A machine's box is one with a card or a link, keys of its own or `box/kind` `machine`, that the
  computer that set it up hasn't removed (`here`'s rule); on Linux its start script alone
  (`bin/kuvo-start`) is enough; but under the installer's mark (`updates/install/making`) only
  one that runs is a box.
- Data in `S` is anything there but what's nobody's: the engine's download (`engine`), caches
  (`opencode/cache`, `Caches`, `cache`, `tmp`, logs), a folder early builds of the desktop app kept there (`desktop`; it keeps to
  `~/.kuvo-code/desktop` now, which the move, a new box and a move back all leave as it is), and
  a `box` folder holding only `run` and `bin`. Broad on purpose: a Mac with data taken for a new
  one would get a box beside what it has.

**`new`** → `{"result", "verdict", "started"?, "setAside"?, "message"?, "status"}`. `result` is
`done`, `nothing`, `refused`, `failed`, or `waits` (another move holds the lock: exit 4, never
`refused`). `setAside` is the folder what was in `K` before went to, whole
(`K/trash/earlier-box-<date>`), when anything was there:

- **On a Mac**, only for `fresh`: the release's files checked against its `box.json`, then the
  box made as `rehome --new` makes it ("Moving this Mac's box") from the installer's release and
  engine (that version's alone), then its helper started by the link just put in place (`helper
  start --app <the bundle's ID>`, the whole start: "This Mac's box: its helper"). `done`,
  `started` true. For `ours`, only the helper: `nothing`, `started` true. A helper that couldn't
  be started is `failed` with `started` false and why, the box made all the same: `status` then
  says `ours` with `new` to run again. Any other verdict: `refused`, saying why (`waits`:
  `waits`, exit 4). In a home that isn't the real one (a demo copy's), it's made but nothing outside the folder
  is written: `started` false, said.
- **On Linux**, only for `fresh`, under the move's lock: a machine's box, as a computer that's
  added gets it ("Computers", Adding one). What's in `K` that isn't a box (one the computer that
  set it up removed or turned off, with the sessions it left; what a making cut short left) is
  set aside whole in `trash/earlier-box-<date>`, nothing deleted, as a Mac's new box does (but
  the installer's own, the move's records, and the desktop app's own folder, `desktop`). Then the
  engine and the release's files put in place by name with their modes (the keeper's mark and
  the version last), `updates/installed.json`, then the one start script that adding runs there
  (its settings its own, `run/launch.env`, its `@reboot` line, its id, `kuvo-start start`). No
  helper, no `box/kind`. Refused while anything still runs from `K/run` (a keeper that's ending),
  as on a Mac. One that couldn't be started is `failed`, and `fresh` with `new` still, whatever
  its start left (keys and a link too): under the installer's mark, what doesn't run isn't a
  box, and is set aside as it's made again. It has no relay until a Mac sets it up or
  `kuvo-link.js pair <relay>`.
- One cut short at any point is made again by running it again; `fresh` holds until a box is
  whole.

**`move`** → the lines `{"step", "title", "index", "of"}` as each step is reached (the box's own
words for it, `kuvo/box/rehome`'s `progress`), then `{"result", "verdict", "started"?,
"message"?, "status"}`: an earlier Kuvo Code's sessions and settings moved by the box itself
("Moving this Mac's box", The whole move). Only on a Mac, and only where `status` says `move`
(`app-07`, `app-box`, a move stopped part way, or one that's done and still owes something):
`fresh`, `machine`, `two` and `back` are `refused`, saying why; `ours` with nothing owed is
`nothing`; `waits`, exit 4. It starts `kuvo-link.js rehome <root> --run …` in a session of its
own, its answer kept in a file of this installer's own (`updates/rehome/run.<its pid>.out`)
until it's read and what it says besides in `updates/rehome/run.log`, and follows it: an app that quits meanwhile doesn't stop the move, and
at its next open `status` says `waits` (with `status.progress` to draw) while it's still at
work, or what it came to. `progress` is there the whole time a move the box runs itself is at
work: `plan` while what still runs is stopped and the refusals are checked, each step of its
journal, then `{step: "done", title: "Starting Kuvo on this Mac", index: of, of}` while Kuvo is
started and what's owed is settled (`updates/rehome/run.phase`, believed only while a process
holds the move's lock). `status.dropped` says what wasn't carried.

#### This Mac's app

GPUI registers its desktop and version with `kuvo/box/app` through local HTTP.
The browser belongs to the box on either platform. The app-owned browser tools
and callback contracts below describe the installed Swift client.

`box.app` (#333 piece 3). A Mac's box in a home of its own (`box/kind` says `mac`; not the app's box
in its folder, whose keeper does this) is where its app registers, and its agents browse in the
app's panel through it, with no Chromium of its own. A machine's box answers `409` to both routes
(after a phone's `403` where one asks what only Kuvo Code may).

- **`kuvo/box/app`**: `POST` from Kuvo Code itself (`403` from a phone), `{tools: {url, token}, bundle,
  host?}` as the app opens: where its panel's tools answer (MCP over HTTP, on `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` or
  `[::1]` only, to `Authorization: Bearer <token>`), and where it's installed (a whole path to its
  `.app`). `{tools: null}` as it quits, its place kept (the app says so over the box's server as it
  goes, waiting a second at most; one that doesn't, a crash, is found gone when its tools stop
  answering). `{updating: true}` as it quits to install an update, so the box doesn't open it while
  Sparkle does. `bundle` left out keeps the one before. `GET` and each `POST` answer `{bundle, open,
  updating, opening, failed}`: where it's installed (null before it ever said), whether its tools
  answer now, whether an update installs (said in the last two minutes), whether an opening is under
  way, and the last opening that failed, within its rest (`{at, message}`, `at` in ms), and `desktop`
  (below). Kept in `run/app.json` (`{bundle, desktop, tools, host, at}`, `0600`).
- **Kuvo's desktop app** (#781): `POST kuvo/box/app` `{desktop, version?}`, only from the app itself over
  this box's server (`x-kuvo-from: app`; `403` otherwise, `box route` too, which anything on the
  Mac can run), a whole path to its `.app`: the desktop app says where it is as it opens, once its
  nearest box answers `kuvo/box/at-work` ("In the menu bar"), so Kuvo Helper's **Open Kuvo** opens that very
  copy, never an older one with the same bundle ID; and its version (`1.2.3` or `1.2.3-beta.4`,
  else ignored), by which this Mac's row in `kuvo/computers` says `appCheck` ("Updates", This Mac's
  app follows). Kept apart from `bundle`: the desktop app has no
  browser for agents yet, so it's never what a browser call opens. Answered as above, with
  `desktop` (null before it ever said; left out by a box from before).
- **The app's own host** (`box.app.host`, #333 piece 6b). The box's host is its helper, which holds
  its keys but can't answer what only the open app can: a phone's ask of the Mac's own routes
  (`link/route`, "This Mac's box: the relay") and what the panel's browser is signed in to
  (`sites/signed-in`). So the app also says where its own host interface answers: `host: {url,
  password}`, `url` `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, taken only from the app itself (`x-kuvo-from: app` over
  the box's server; `403` from `box route`, which anything you run could use to have your phones'
  asks sent elsewhere; `400` for anything else). It's kept while the app's open; a registration
  without `host` has none (a host an earlier app left isn't kept for it), and it goes with `{tools:
  null}` and `{updating: true}`; never in what `GET` answers. The box sends those two calls there, proving it's the app first (`hello`, "Host
  interface") for each one, as the box outlives the app and a port it left after a crash could be
  anyone's by the next; with no app there, a phone's ask is `503` ("isn't answering"). The app answers
  only those there (`hello`, `sites/signed-in`, `link/route`; `404` for its keys, which are the
  helper's).
- **The browser's tools.** The box's tool server (`kuvo-browser.js mcp`, as its engine and coding
  agents run it) sends each `browser_*` call to the app's tools as it came (`tools/call`, with the
  session's `_meta`, `x-kuvo-session` naming the conversation, and an `mcp-session-id` of its own;
  a call stopped is told to the app as `notifications/cancelled`), and gives back what the app
  answers. Nothing there, or something there that doesn't answer as the app's tools do (a `401`, not
  JSON-RPC), is the app gone: the call has it opened again. Its other tools are the box's, as on a
  machine. On a Mac the app's tools' port is refused to agents' commands in the sandbox, as the box's
  own servers are.
- **Opening the app**, when a browser call comes with no app registered:
  `POST kuvo/box/app/open` (from Kuvo Code's own processes; `{gone: <token>}` says the app
  registered with that token didn't answer, so it's taken for closed). The box decides:
  - one opening at a time, across all its processes (`run/app-opening.json`, `{at, by}`): a call
    while one's under way waits for it, and hears how it ended; one whose process is gone (a call
    stopped is told to stop once, and sees its opening through; one cut off anyway), or that ran
    past its time, is taken over;
  - the app is opened where it last registered, by what runs as the app (its host interface's
    `app/open`, below), and waited for: 30 seconds from the opening's start, for it to register;
  - while an update of the app installs (`{updating: true}` in the last two minutes,
    `run/app-updating`), it isn't opened: calls wait for Sparkle to open it;
  - after one that failed (`run/app-open-failed.json`), none for five minutes: calls are told what
    it said. The app registering forgets it, and the update's note.
  It answers `200` with the app's state once the app's registered, else `503 {"message"}`, what the
  agent's told (Kuvo Code's own words, as the keeper said them): it isn't where it was installed
  any more; it couldn't be opened (and why); it wasn't ready within 30 seconds; it never registered
  here (nothing to open). A call stopped while it waits stops waiting; the one that asked for the
  opening sees it through, for the others.

#### The app attached to this Mac's own box

Historical 0.7 attachment contract (#333 piece 6b). Once this Mac's box has moved into a home of its
own, the app attaches to it in place, as to any box already on this Mac (`here` answers `attach`,
its `box.kind` `mac`), and does for it, through its routes, what it did for its box in its folder:

- **Reached over its server**, where `run/serve.json` says it answers (its helper keeps it up), as
  its own app (`x-kuvo-from: app`), so what the app follows there streams; while there's none, its
  CLI (`box route`), a request at a time, as a machine's is read.
- **Its link**: told what's wanted (`kuvo/link/config`), followed (`kuvo/link/status/events`,
  `kuvo/link/phones/events`), told your machines (`kuvo/link/peers`, which it signs; and each
  machine set up for your phones with what `kuvo/link/setup` gives), and phones paired from Settings
  › Phone (`kuvo/phones/pair`), as the app's own box was. The app reads none of this Mac's keys and
  makes none: its key is the one the box says.
- **Registered** (`kuvo/box/app`, above): its browser's tools, its place, and its own host.
- **Offered the release it carries** (`kuvo/box/update {from}`, "Updates"), once each time it opens,
  where the box has `box.update`; one that isn't newer the box refuses (`409`), as it should.

A machine's box attached in place (one a Mac set up on this one) keeps its own link: the app tells
it nothing of it, pairs no phone there and reads or makes no key of this Mac's for it (its
`kuvo/link/*` answer `403` all the same). It asks for the box's server to be kept each time it
connects (`kuvo/box/serve {needed: true}`, "Kept for clients"; left asked for as it quits, for the
next time it opens), and once the box says it takes Kuvo Code
there (`box.serve.mac`), reaches it over that server as Kuvo Code on its computer (`x-kuvo-from:
mac`, taken as `box route` is), so what it follows streams; else, and while there's no server, its
CLI.

#### This Mac's box: its keys, for its app

`box.appKeys` is the retained native identity contract (#333 piece 6a). Once this Mac's box has moved
into a home of its own, its keys are its helper's copies in your Keychain ("This Mac's box: its
helper"), which the app can't read, and must never make anew: a key made by the app would be
another Mac to every phone, machine and peer. So the app reads none of them, and asks the box for
what it did with them. Its route answers only Kuvo Code on this Mac (`x-kuvo-from: app` over the
box's own server, to the password in `run/serve.json`), `403` to anyone else (a phone, or `box
route`), and `409` on any other box. That password is in a file only you can read, which the sandbox
keeps agents' commands from, as it keeps them from `run/host.json`, whose host interface gives the
same keys (`link/identity`): what runs as you outside the sandbox can reach either, as it could the
app's keeper's before the move.

- **`POST kuvo/box/proof`**: this Mac's proof for one of your machines' vaults ("Vault"), signed with
  the Mac's signing key: `{machine}` for its vault's key (`kuvo-vault-key\0<machine>\0<at>\0<nonce>`),
  or `{machine, method, path, hash}` for one request (`kuvo-vault-request\0<machine>\0<at>\0<nonce>
  \0<METHOD>\0<path>\0<hash>`, `hash` the body's SHA-256 in hex). It answers `{mac, at, nonce,
  proof}`, as the app made them before: `mac` the Mac's public link key, `at` now (ms), a nonce of
  its own. Its keys come from its link once it's on, else from its host (`link/identity`), never made
  here; `503 {"message"}` while the Keychain can't give them. `400` for anything else asked.
- **The app's other uses**, through the routes every client has: the vault's values it fills or
  shows (`kuvo/vault/items/<id>/values`, noted `shown` in the vault's activity, as Kuvo Code on this
  Mac), whether a password you signed in with is the saved one (`kuvo/vault/items/<id>/same`, which
  neither gives nor notes it), and the integrations' keys a new machine starts with (`kuvo/keys`).
- **What the app still writes there**, as it wrote them beside the box in its folder: your machines'
  list (`machines.json`) and their bridges (`phone-link.json`), in the box's home; the box reads both
  ("Machines").
- **Its integrations' catalog** is the release's `bin/integrations-mac.json` (every integration,
  those that use the Mac's own apps too, their keys named in `box/keys`), read instead of
  `bin/integrations.json` there, where the app wrote the box's catalog into its folder before.

#### Host interface

What only the app can do for this Mac's box, the box asks the app for (bridge 0.9.46): the keeper
answers it, as Kuvo Code's own executable (so the Keychain trusts it as it trusts the app), and asks
the open app for what only it can answer (what the panel's browser is signed in to, the Mac's own
routes for a phone: `app {host: {url, password}}`), answering `503 {"message"}` while it's closed. Its keys,
which the app keeps in the Keychain, and (bridge 0.9.50) what its browser is signed in to, and moving what it lets go of to the Finder's Trash. The app listens on `127.0.0.1` and, each time it
starts listening, writes where and with what password to the box's `run/host.json` (`{"url",
"password"}`, made `0600` and moved into place; bridge 0.9.60). It takes it away before each start,
when it stops, when it can't start, and as it quits; one a crash left behind stays until the next
start. The box reads it again for each call, so a host interface the app started again (it does,
whenever it fails, and with Try Again in Settings) is reached at its new address without the box
starting again, and every client's streams stay open. Before it sends anything else there, the box
makes sure it's the app, not whatever took a left-behind file's port: `hello {"nonce"}` (a random
nonce, asked without the password) → `{"proof"}`, the HMAC-SHA256 with the password, in hex, of
`kuvo-host-hello\0<nonce>\0<host>:<port>`: where the box reached it, which the app answers with its
own (`127.0.0.1:<port>`), so a proof relayed from the app at another port (by another user's
process on this Mac, which can't read the file) is wrong there. Without that proof, its keys can't be reached (`503 {"message"}`); with it, nothing is asked
again until the file changes or the app stops answering there. The box is started with `KUVO_KEYS_ON_HOST=1`: without the file, its
keys can't be reached (`503 {"message"}`), never kept in files of its own. Before 0.9.60 the app
passed `KUVO_HOST_URL` and `KUVO_HOST_PASSWORD` in the box's environment, which the box still uses
while there's no file, taking the password out of its environment as it starts so nothing it runs
has it. Each other call is a `POST` with `Authorization: Bearer <password>` and `content-type:
application/json`:

- `keys/names {"prefix"?, "suffix"?}` → `{"names"}`, the keys kept whose names begin and end so;
- `keys/get {"name"}` → `{"value"}`, or `404` for none;
- `keys/set {"name", "value"}` → `{}`;
- `keys/delete {"name"}` → `{}`, for one there wasn't too;
- `sites/signed-in {}` → `{"sites": {"<integration>": <bool>}}`, whether the panel's browser is
  signed in to the sites the agent uses there (X, LinkedIn, Reddit), as their cookies say: only
  those it can tell. The app reads the cookies again only once they've changed (or after 30
  seconds);
- `vault/get {"id"}` → `{"values"}` (`404` for none), `vault/set {"id", "values"}` → `{}`,
  `vault/delete {"id"}` → `{}`: the vault's values, by item, in the Keychain ("Vault", bridge
  0.9.100);
- `permissions {}` → `{}`: Kuvo Helper only ("This Mac's box: its helper", What macOS allows):
  what macOS allows it, looked at again and noted in `run/permissions.json` before it answers;
  the app's keeper answers `404`;
- `trash {"path"}` → `{}`: a folder the box put in its trash (`box/trash`, a deleted bot's), to the
  Finder's Trash (bridge 0.9.52); one anywhere else stays where it is;
- `app/open {"bundle"}` → `{}`: Kuvo Code at `bundle` opened in the background, as the box asks for
  its agents' browser ("This Mac's app"): no window, out of the Dock, not taking focus; one running
  from there already is left as it is. The keeper opens only the app it runs from, whose bundle ID
  is its own and whose signature meets its own designated requirement (`403` for anything else),
  answering `410` when there's nothing there and `502 {"message"}` when macOS didn't open it. The open app answers `{}` (it's open). A host that doesn't know it answers `404`;
- for its link (bridge 0.9.61, "The relay, on this Mac's box"):
  - `link/identity {}` → `{"key", "secret", "sign"}` (each 32 bytes, base64url): this Mac's link
    key, relay secret and signing key, from the Keychain, never asking you to unlock it; `503` while
    the link isn't wanted or the Keychain won't give them (read again a minute later while it was
    locked);
  - `link/route {"method", "path", "headers", "body", "phone"}` (`body` base64, `phone` the asking
    phone's key, base64url) → that request's answer as the app gives it: its status, its
    `content-type` and `cache-control`, `x-kuvo-answer: 1` (the app's own answer, whatever its
    status), and its body as it comes, chunked (a followed route streams). One cut off partway
    (the engine went) ends without its last chunk, so the box tells the phone it was cut off. The
    box closing the request (the phone went) stops what it asked, before any answer too. Before bridge 0.9.63, mail the box didn't take itself went to the app (`link/mailed`, 0.9.61 and 0.9.62).

Names are `KUVO_KEY_*` only (`^KUVO_KEY_[A-Z0-9_]+$`): the box never asks for another, and the app
answers no other. The app keeps the files the engine reads (`KUVO_KEYS`) in step as it
changes them. Anything else it answers is an error the box's route answers `503 {"message"}`
with. Without these, as on a machine, the box keeps its keys in files only you can read.

#### This Mac's box: its helper

`box.helper`, #333 piece 4, behind the app's `movesOwnBox` (off): nothing uses it until the move
does. Once this Mac's box lives in a home of its own (`~/.kuvo-code`, `box/kind` says `mac`), it
runs under **Kuvo Helper**, a small signed program of Kuvo Code's own with no box logic. It's
Swift, for macOS only (a box on Linux needs none), in a package of its own (`mac/helper`), and
built on its own by `scripts/build-helper.sh <folder>`, with no app built or needed: `Kuvo
Helper.app`, signed with the hardened runtime and its own entitlements, so it can be notarized as
it is (and `kuvo-keys`, below, ad hoc only: signed with a real identity only when asked, `KUVO_SIGNED_KEYS=1`,
which nothing does yet). The box's release brings it into `bin/Kuvo Helper.app`, and it runs from there. Its bundle
ID is the app's with `.box` after it (`run.kuvo.code.box`); an update keeps that, its signer and
its place, which is what macOS keeps your permissions and its Keychain items by. (Until #713 it
was named Kuvo Code Box, in no release.)

A Darwin machine box uses the same signed Helper and launch agent with `keep-machine --home <box>`.
Helper starts its keeper and the box continues to use its machine credentials. An existing machine
starts a permission watcher under the signed Helper while the existing launch job still runs
worker restarts and ordinary engine updates. After the watcher sees the Files grant, Kuvo waits
for quiet, holds incoming messages, keeps pending inbox messages, and saves the launch job before
switching it. It rechecks the grant with the Helper that will run the workers. New installs and
migrations both verify that the engine and bridge answer before completing the switch. If
migration fails or is interrupted, Kuvo restores the previous job and holds messages until both
services answer. A failed adoption backs off so ordinary engine updates can proceed.

- **Started** by the launch agent `run.kuvo.code.machine` (one per computer): `kuvo-link.js helper install [--load] [--app <bundle ID>]` writes
  `~/Library/LaunchAgents/run.kuvo.code.machine.plist` (`ProgramArguments`: the helper, `keep
  --home <box>`; `RunAtLoad`; `KeepAlive {SuccessfulExit: false}`; `AbandonProcessGroup`;
  `AssociatedBundleIdentifiers: [<the app's ID>]`, by default `run.kuvo.code`), and with `--load`
  lets go of whatever had the label, waits (ten seconds at most) until launchd has, and bootstraps
  it (`gui/<uid>`), three more times a second apart while launchd refuses. It prints `{written, loaded,
  message}`, exiting 0 once done, 1 when refused (not a Mac, not a Mac's own box in a home of its
  own, not the real `~/.kuvo-code`, or no helper in `bin`) or launchd didn't start it, 2 for what it
  doesn't know. `helper status` says `{helper, agent, loaded, running, handOver}` (`loaded` and
  `running` null where launchd couldn't be asked; `handOver` the record below, or null). `helper start [--if-missing] [--app <bundle ID>]` is the whole start through the helper: its
  launch agent put in place and loaded where it isn't there (as `install --load`), loaded where it's
  there but not loaded, and started where it isn't running (`launchctl kickstart`, leaving one
  running as it is); with `--if-missing`, one in place is left as it is, loaded or not (switched
  off in Login Items, it stays off: `left: true`). It says `{started, mac, left?, disabled?, opened?,
  message}` (`disabled` where launchd won't because it's switched off in Login Items, which
  `message` then says plainly, and `opened` where it opened the helper itself then, below), `mac`
  whether it's a Mac's own box in a home of its own (only then does its helper start it, and
  nothing else may), `message` why not where it didn't; exit 0 once it has (or left it), 1 when
  refused as `install` is or launchd didn't. As `uninstall` does, it touches launchd only for the real `~/.kuvo-code`, or a test's
  stand-ins (`KUVO_TEST_UNINSTALL_TOOLS`). `uninstall` takes it away.
- **With Login Items off for it** (`box.permissions`), launchd won't load or start it, and `helper
  start` opens it itself: `open -g -j -n <bin/Kuvo Helper.app> --args keep --home <box>`, through
  Launch Services, so it's its own program to macOS as launchd's would be (never the child of
  whatever asked, which would make that what macOS asks about). It answers `{started: true, mac,
  disabled: true, opened: true, message}`, exit 0: macOS was asked to open it and took that, which
  is all `started` with `opened` says (whether the helper then keeps the box is in its own records:
  `run/helper-trouble`, `run/permissions.json`). Opened so, it runs the box until you log out, and
  isn't started at login until it's switched on again, which `message` says. One running already
  keeps the box (its lock); the one opened goes at once. Where macOS doesn't open it: `{started:
  false, disabled: true, message}`, exit 1. `--if-missing` never opens one. No client opens the
  helper. (Before `box.permissions`, `helper start` answered `{started: false, disabled: true}`
  and nothing ran until you switched it on.)
- **Runs**: only your account's `~/.kuvo-code` (from its home folder as the system has it, not
  `$HOME`; `--home` may name only that), kept only from the bundle installed there
  (`bin/Kuvo Helper.app`), the box and its `bin` yours alone to change: a copy of the helper
  elsewhere, or a folder of anyone's making, would otherwise be handed the vault's secrets and serve
  your keys (the tests' own build takes the box it's given). One per box (`run/helper.lock`; a
  second goes at once, exit 0). What it won't run, it says on stderr and exits 0. It checks first that
  its bundle on disk is the very one it was started from (its code directory's hash, as the app
  checks itself); changed, it starts nothing, writes why in `run/helper-trouble`, and exits 0 so
  launchd doesn't start it again. Nor does it start anything (the same note, exit 0) while a move
  of the box is under way (`updates/rehome/journal.json` not `done`), while its keys are being moved
  (the Keychain journal below `copying` or `returning`), or are copied for a move that hasn't
  finished (`copied` or `settling` without `state.json` saying the move's `done`): the old box may
  run then, with the same keys. Nor when its keeper (`bin/kuvo-start`, `K="$HOME/<name>"`) names
  another folder than its box's: its children get `HOME` the folder around its box. Then it starts
  its host interface (below), `kuvo-start serve`, and `kuvo-start keep` in a session of its own,
  each its own child, so macOS takes it for the
  responsible process of everything the box runs (the engine, the bridge, every agent's command):
  folders, Screen Recording and the rest are asked for Kuvo Helper. Nothing sets a Mac's own box up
  over SSH, so its keeper notes how its engine starts itself, once, as it starts and before each
  start of the engine (`run/launch.env`, as a machine's start notes it: the `PATH`, `SHELL`, `LANG`
  and `LC_*` the helper gives it, and `OPENCODE_CLIENT=desktop`); one noted already stays as it is.
  Either child that ends is
  started again: a second after one that ran ten minutes or more, else after a wait that grows each
  time in a row (2 s, 5 s, 15 s… up to ten minutes). Every ten seconds it notes macOS asking you something (`run/.system-asking`), as the
  keeper did, and every minute what macOS allows it (below). SIGTERM (launchd, logging out) closes `serve`'s stdin, sends the keeper SIGTERM (the
  engine, link and bridge are detached and go on, for the next keeper to take over), takes its
  `host.json` away and exits 0; what hasn't ended three seconds on gets SIGTERM, a second after
  that SIGKILL. The box turned off (`run/off`, `kuvo-start off`) with its keeper
  gone, it does the same.
- **What macOS allows** (`box.permissions`). Everything the box runs is asked about, and allowed,
  as Kuvo Helper, and the helper checks Screen Recording, Accessibility and Full Disk Access without prompting.
  It checks as it starts, every minute (and within ten seconds of the note going), and whenever
  the box asks it to (its host's `permissions {}` → `{}`, answered once it has noted it; a helper
  from before that answers `404`), each time in a process of its own that never asked before
  (`Kuvo Helper permissions`, its own child, which says `{"screenRecording", "accessibility", "fullDiskAccess"}` and
  exits), one at a time: macOS answers Screen Recording once for each process, so a running helper
  asking itself would never see a change you make. Where that process can't say (within five
  seconds), the note reports unknown. Old observations expire. It writes `run/permissions.json` after each check: `{"v": 1, "pid": <its own>, "started": <when its process started, in
  seconds>, "observedAt": <milliseconds since epoch>, "screenRecording": bool, "accessibility": bool, "fullDiskAccess": bool or null}`, `0600`, taken away as it goes. A failed check writes just the process identity and observation time. The box says it:
  - `GET kuvo/box/permissions` → `{applies, name, known, screenRecording, accessibility, bundle, list}`,
    the helper asked to look again first (above), so what you just switched on in System Settings
    is said at once; where it can't be asked, or hasn't answered within two seconds, the note as it
    is. Settings › This Mac reads it the same way.
    `applies`: whether this box runs under Kuvo Helper (a Mac’s own box in a home of its own or
    a Darwin machine using Helper, which reports only Files and refreshes its note every five seconds);
    `name`: what System Settings lists it as (`"Kuvo Helper"`), null where it doesn't apply;
    `known`: whether the helper runs now and has said (a note whose `pid` isn't a running process
    of yours that started when `started` says, to within three seconds, as `ps` has it, says
    nothing: a helper killed where it stood leaves its note, and its number goes to another
    process; nor does one that isn't as above); each permission `true` or `false`, null while not `known`.
  - `bundle`: that program on the Mac (a full path to `bin/Kuvo Helper.app` in the box's home),
    what you drag into a list in System Settings; null where it doesn't apply.
  - `list`: each permission in words, for a client to draw without naming any itself:
    `[{id, name, line, allowed, settings, byHand, byHandLine, unknownLine, asks}]`. `id` is `screenRecording`, `accessibility` or `fullDiskAccess`;
    `name` what System Settings calls it; `line` what agents need it for, in a sentence (a client
    draws it under the name); `allowed` as above; `settings` the address that opens
    its list in System Settings (`x-apple.systempreferences:…`), which only an app on that Mac
    can open; `byHand`: macOS asks nothing for it, you add the program to the list yourself; `asks`: whether a client brings it up now, true while it's
    known not to be allowed and you haven't put it off. `byHandLine` gives the instruction for
    granting it, and `unknownLine` is shown while the box can't say. Empty where it doesn't apply.
    The Files row opens Privacy & Security › Full Disk Access. Helper uses a filesystem probe and
    reports unknown when the result is inconclusive. It tries a
    one-byte read of `/Library/Application Support/com.apple.TCC/TCC.db`, falling back to the
    per-user database if the system one is absent.
  - `POST kuvo/box/permissions {later: "<id>"}` puts one off (a client's "Not Now"), kept in the
    box (`box/permissions-later.json`) so every client agrees and none asks at each open; once
    it's allowed it's no longer put off, so one taken away later is brought up again. It answers
    as `GET` does. `400 {message}` for no such permission; `409 {message}` where it doesn't
    apply; `500 {message}` where it couldn't be kept. Any client of the box may send it, a phone
    too: it only quiets a reminder, and grants nothing. `405` for any other method: nothing here grants anything, which only you do, in System
    Settings › Privacy & Security.
  - A machine's box (Linux, or a Mac set up as one) and a Mac's box still in its app's folder
    answer `{applies: false, name: null, known: false, …null, bundle: null, list: []}`: on Linux there's nothing to allow,
    and on a Mac macOS asks about each program there by its own name.
  - Files and Folders and Local Network aren't here yet: macOS can't be asked about them, so they
    can only be told from what fails.
- **`serve`**: `kuvo-start serve`, on a Mac's own box only (else exit 3; `run/off`, exit 0), runs
  `kuvo-link.js serve` in the foreground with the engine's Bun, as the box's other processes are
  started, its output in `run/serve.log`. The helper gives it, on its stdin's first line,
  `{"password", "hostVaultSecret", "vaultFileKey"?, "renews"}` and keeps the pipe open: it goes when that
  closes. `renews: true` says the helper leaves by itself for a new build of it put in its place
  (exit 75, "Updates"); a helper from before beta.31 says nothing of it. On a Mac's box in a home of its own, `serve` says where it answers itself, in
  `run/serve.json` (`{pid, port, password, kept: false}`, `0600`), and takes it away as it leaves.
  Started while the Keychain couldn't give the vault's file key (locked), it's started again once
  it can; one that's missing for good isn't asked for again.
- **A helper from before beta.31** never leaves for a new build of itself, so after an update it
  runs on, old (its menu bar item, Open Kuvo and its host interface), until the next login. Its
  `serve`, started again on the new code, hands it over once: where the first line on its stdin
  had no `renews`, its parent is this box's helper (`<bin/Kuvo Helper.app>/…/Kuvo Helper keep`),
  the build in place renews itself (`KuvoHelperRenews` true in its `Info.plist`), no update is
  under way (else it looks again every 30 seconds), and Kuvo on this Mac isn't stopped (`run/paused`,
  `run/off`). It notes the try first, in `run/helper-handover.json` (`{v: 1, bundle, copy, pid, by?,
  at, outcome, message?, stillOld?}`: `bundle` the build in place's hash as the helper's own look
  hashes it, `copy` its program file's number, new with each update that puts it there, `by` the
  process handing it over), and starts `kuvo-link.js helper hand-over --pid <helper>` in a session
  of its own, which outlasts it: the helper is sent SIGTERM (as launchd sends it: its `serve` and
  keeper stop, the engine, bridge and their turns run on, and it exits 0, which launchd doesn't
  start again), waited for (a minute at most), and once launchd no longer names it, started as
  `helper start` starts one (kickstart, or opened where Login Items is off for it), Kuvo being
  stopped on this Mac looked at again right before; where launchd refuses otherwise, it's opened
  (`open -g -j -n`), to run until you log out. Nothing at work is cut, so it doesn't wait for a quiet
  moment. `outcome`: `handing`, then `handed` (the new one started; `message` says where it was
  opened instead), `stopped` (Kuvo was stopped on this Mac before or as it went: nothing started),
  `gone` (it had gone already: nothing done), `stayed` (it didn't stop) or `failed` (`message` says
  launchd's or macOS's answer; or a hand-over that ended without a word). One try for each copy of a
  build in place: a helper found old again for the same `bundle` and `copy` is noted once
  (`stillOld: {pid, at}`, and in `run/serve.log`) and left to your next login; the same release put
  in place again (after a rollback) is a copy of its own, and tried once more. A helper that says
  `renews`, a `serve` started otherwise (`OPENCODE_PASSWORD`), and a box that isn't a Mac's own in
  the real `~/.kuvo-code` (or a test's stand-ins) are never handed over.
- **Host interface**: the same calls, proofs and answers as the keeper's ("Host interface",
  `HostProof` shared by both), from its own Keychain items, named by its bundle ID
  (`<helper ID>.phone-link`, `.integrations`, `.vault`), never asking you anything (a locked
  Keychain answers `503 {"message"}`). `app/open` opens any copy of Kuvo Code the box names (the
  one that registered with it) that's signed by the helper's team (an ad hoc build: one carrying
  this very helper), and leaves one already running as it is (`{}`); `trash` takes only what's in
  the box's `trash`. `sites/signed-in` and
  `link/route`, what only the open app answers, say `503 {"message": "Kuvo Code isn't open on this
  Mac."}`: the open app reaches a box in a home of its own itself.
- **Keys it never makes twice.** It makes the link's keys the first time the box asks
  (`link/identity`) and the vault's file key the first time it starts `serve`, and notes them in `box/keychain.json` (`{"has": ["phone-link/key",
  "phone-link/secret", "phone-link/sign", "vault/files"]}`). One the box has had (noted there, or
  copied by the move) and that's gone from the Keychain is never made again: `link/identity`
  answers `503` saying the keys are missing, and `serve` starts without the vault's file key. A new
  key would make this Mac another box to every phone, machine and peer.
- **The Keychain's move** (legacy keychain items, as they've always been; never by changing an
  item's list of programs, which macOS asks about once per item). Only a program an item names may
  read it or take it away; copies of the app's items name only the helper. The journal is
  `updates/rehome/keychain.json` (`{v, state: copying | copied | settled | returning, app, helper,
  items: [{service, account, label?}]}`; `settling` too), written to disk before what it says is
  done.
  - the app's keeper, or `kuvo-keys` (below), copies each of the app's items under the helper's names, made trusting the
    helper the app carries (its signature, which the copy in `bin` shares), listing every one in
    the journal first (`copying`, then `copied`). It never takes an item already under the
    helper's names for a copy (it can't read one to tell): any there (left by an earlier box)
    refuses the copy, and so does a journal an earlier try left (`copying` or `copied`) until
    `uncopy` has taken its copies away: a copy starts afresh, never resumed;
  - `Kuvo Helper keys check --home <box>` (the move's check, a short run of the helper's own)
    prints `{"unreadable": [...]}`, exiting 0 when it reads every copy, 1 when it doesn't;
  - `keys uncopy` (the move went back before it cleared the old place) takes the journaled copies
    away, then the journal; the app's own are never touched (one gone meanwhile was taken away on
    purpose, as the box ran in the app's folder again: its copy goes too), and a Keychain that can't
    say what's there (locked) changes nothing; once `state.json` says the move's `done`, the copies
    are the box's keys and it refuses;
  - `keys clear` (no journal, and no `box/keychain.json`): items under the helper's names left by
    an earlier box, taken away where the app has its own of each; `{"kept": [...]}` says those it
    kept;
  - once the move can't go back, the keeper takes the app's own away (each once its copy is
    there): `settling` first, which `uncopy` refuses, then `settled`;
  - `keys back --app <Kuvo Code.app>` (moving back, before the helper goes): every item the helper
    has, those made since too, made again under the app's names trusting the app, then its own
    taken away, and the journal. It refuses (exit 2) while the app's own are still there.
  Each of these prints JSON and exits 0 once done (`check`: 1 for a copy it can't read), 2 with why
  on stderr. All but `check` take the box's `run/helper.lock`, refusing while the helper keeps the
  box (its host interface may be changing those keys). `back` takes only Kuvo Code itself for `--app`, signed by the helper's team: a helper
  signed ad hoc (a local build) refuses, as anything can be signed so (the tests' own build aside).
- **`kuvo-keys`** (#713, for a box's move that no Swift keeper runs: the box's own, `rehome --run`, runs it; and
  **none is signed with a real identity yet**: `scripts/build-helper.sh` makes one only ad hoc,
  for its tests, unless asked with `KUVO_SIGNED_KEYS=1`, and no release asks, until the limit
  said below is settled: what keeps it to the box's move holds only against what can't write in
  the box's home): the
  app's side of the Keychain's move as a small program of its own, built beside the helper from
  the same package (`scripts/build-helper.sh`) and signed with Kuvo Code's own identifier
  (`run.kuvo.code`) and team, which is what the items Kuvo Code made go by: it reads them without
  macOS asking, as the app would. The desktop app carries it; the box's move runs it. It never
  asks you anything, takes its identity from its signature (nothing it's told; one signed by no
  team, a local build, does nothing), and reaches only your account's `~/.kuvo-code` (`--home` may
  name only that; the tests' own build takes the box and the app it's given, and only a test's
  keychain). It reads what macOS keeps from every other program, so it works **only for the box's
  move, run by it**: the move's lock (`updates/rehome/lock/pid`) must name the very process that
  started `kuvo-keys`, a process that started before that lock was written (one that got the
  number of a move that was killed isn't it), so the move runs it itself, as its own child, while
  it holds its lock. Anything else that runs it, at any other time, gets exit 2 and nothing done.
  (That stops what can't write in the box's home: a session's sandboxed command, another user.
  A program of yours that runs outside the sandbox can make that lock itself.)
  - `kuvo-keys copy --home <box> --helper <Kuvo Helper.app>`: the copy above, trusting that
    helper, which must be Kuvo Helper itself (its ID the app's with `.box`, its signature whole,
    signed by the team that signed `kuvo-keys`; never one signed ad hoc), in the box's `bin` or
    the release its move unpacked (`updates/install`), where it really is (links followed), every
    folder from the home down to it and inside it yours and closed to others' writes. Those are
    places no command under the sandbox writes to (a session's own folders are elsewhere in the
    home), so none of those can put another program in its place between the check and the
    copies. **Only under the sandbox:** the check is of a path, and so is what the Keychain is
    told to trust, so a program of yours outside the sandbox can change what's there in between
    (and put it back before the second check): left for a decision before any `kuvo-keys` is
    signed with a real identity (#713 §8a, 8e). It
    checks the helper again once the copies are made: changed meanwhile, exit 1, `reason` `helper-changed`,
    and the copies aren't to be used (the helper's `uncopy` takes away those it can; any it can't
    stay as leftovers, which stop the next copy). `{"copied": <how many>}`.
  - `kuvo-keys delete-originals --home <box>`: the app's own taken away once the move can't go
    back, as the keeper does (`settling`, then `settled`). `{}`.
  - `kuvo-keys passwords --home <box>`: the sign-ins Kuvo Code 0.7 kept before the vault (internet
    passwords it marked `KUVO`), said down its standard output, which must be a pipe to what
    started it (a pipe or a socket pair; a terminal or a file is exit 2): `{"v": 1, "logins":
    [{host, account, password, modified?}]}`, `modified` in milliseconds. The box's move reads
    them into memory and gives each to its vault ("Moving this Mac's box", Saved sign-ins).
    Never written to a file. Verified vault copies replace their Keychain originals; one it lists but won't give out stops it
    with nothing said.
  One line of JSON; exit 0 once done; 1 with `{"error", "reason"}` (and the error on stderr) where
  it wasn't, `reason` one of `refused` (the Keychain won't without asking: locked, say),
  `leftovers` (items an earlier box left under the helper's names: the helper's `keys clear`
  first), `journal` (the journal says otherwise: an earlier try's copies, `uncopy` first),
  `helper-changed`, `copy-missing`, `unchanged`, `originals-remain`, `failed`; 2 with why on
  stderr for what it doesn't know, a box that isn't yours alone, no move of the box running it, or
  a helper that isn't Kuvo Helper in the box.

#### In the menu bar

`box.atWork`, #761 (in `FEATURES`, not the update gate: a client without it shows nothing of it). On a Mac whose box lives in a home of its own, quitting the app leaves Kuvo at
work: its sessions, bots and wake-ups go on under Kuvo Helper. So Kuvo Helper, the part that always
runs, draws Kuvo in the menu bar for as long as it runs the box (the item goes with it), from the
box's facts alone:

- `GET kuvo/box/at-work` → `{applies, working, sessions, asking, waiting, background, busy, rings, computers}`,
  and `GET kuvo/box/at-work/events`, a line now and one as it changes (its sessions starting,
  stopping and asking, its bots, the work left running), the rings read again every 15 s.
  - `applies`: whether this box is shown in its computer's menu bar (a Mac's own box in a home of
    its own; false on Linux, on a Mac's box in its app's folder, and on a machine's).
  - `working`: how many of its sessions are at work in their turn; `sessions`: the latest twenty
    of them, `{id, title?, bot?}`, `bot` the name of the bot it works for where that bot lives here.
    (Conversations only, this box's own copy, not archived: never a subagent's or one kept out of
    sight.)
  - `asking`: the latest twenty waiting on you, `{id, title?, asks?}`, `asks` what it asks in the
    box's words ("asks to run a command"); `waiting`: `kuvo/waiting`'s counts.
  - `background`: how many sessions not at work in their turn still have work running (a command,
    a subagent: "Work › Background work"); `busy`: whether anything would stop with Kuvo here
    (`working` or `background` above none). A client asks before stopping while it's true.
  - `rings`: each account's rings, in the box's order (the plan limits' `rows`), `{service, title,
    short?: {used, level}, long?: {used, level}}`, as "Plan limits" says them; none while the
    coding agents' bridge doesn't run.
  - `computers` (#781; left out by a box from before): every one of your computers, this one first
    (`here: true`), then each of its peers by name: `{key, name, kind, here?, reach, working?,
    sessions, waiting?, asking, rings}`. `reach` as `kuvo/computers` says it (`connected`,
    `connecting`, `away`). This one's as above (`waiting`, its sessions waiting on you); another's as
    it last told this box with its agents ("Peers", `computer`'s `working`, `atWork`, `waiting`,
    `asking`), nothing while it's away (what it said is old), and `working` and `waiting` left out
    where it never said (an older box). `rings`: the accounts signed in there, as the plan limits'
    rows say which computers each is on (its `boxes`). The events line comes again as a peer's word
    or reach changes too.
- `POST kuvo/box/stop` → `202 {stopping: true}`: **Stop Kuvo on this Mac**, until it next starts.
  Only over the box's own server with its password (the helper, or the app on this Mac): a phone
  or another computer gets `403`, since nothing there could start it again. Only where `applies`
  (else `409`). It runs the keeper's `kuvo-start pause` in a process of its own and answers at once.
  `pause` marks the box (`run/paused`), ends the phone link, the keeper with its group and the start
  it's at, and stops the engine and the coding agents' bridge, as `off` does, but not for good:
  while the mark is there, `kuvo-start engine` starts nothing, and the next keeper to start takes it
  away. The helper, seeing its keeper gone with a mark made since it started, stops `serve` and exits
  0, so launchd doesn't start it again. Kuvo starts again at the next login (launchd's `RunAtLoad`,
  where Login Items has it on), or as the app opens: the installer's `status` takes a paused box's
  helper as not in place, so `new` starts it (`helper start`, which first waits, ten seconds at
  most, while launchd still has the stopped helper running: a kickstart then would be lost as it
  exits). A machine's box refuses `pause` (exit 3).
- **Kuvo Helper's item**: Kuvo's mark (the app icon's artwork in one colour, a template), the count
  of sessions at work on all your computers beside it, and a dot while anything waits on you (any of
  `waiting`'s counts, or a session waiting on another of your computers). Its panel: each of your
  computers (`computers`; this Mac alone from a box from before), this Mac first with whether its
  Kuvo is starting, running or stopping, the others with whether they're reached; for each, what
  needs you, what's at work (with the bot each works for), and the rings of the accounts signed in
  there. A click on a computer or a session opens the desktop app there, by the link
  `kuvo-code://open?computer=<key>&session=<id>` (each where there's one; no `computer` for this
  Mac's own box), which the desktop app takes (its `CFBundleURLTypes`) as a notification clicked.
  **Open Kuvo** (the desktop app, opened or brought forward): the copy that last said where it is
  (`kuvo/box/app`'s `desktop`), where it's still there and signed as Kuvo; else the newest copy
  with Kuvo's bundle ID (by `CFBundleVersion`, as Sparkle orders them). **Stop Kuvo on this Mac…**, which asks
  first while `busy` or while the desktop app is open, which it quits too once the stop is taken
  (its window would have nothing to reach). A stop that hasn't ended the helper 30 seconds on is
  said not to have taken. Quit as AppKit has it (Activity Monitor, logging out) goes as SIGTERM
  does: everything the helper started is told to stop first. The helper reaches the box's server as a client does (`run/serve.json`'s port,
  with the password it started `serve` with: a record naming another is never read from).
- **The desktop app's first Quit**: where the nearest box says `applies`, the first ⌘Q (or closing
  the window) shows a note that Kuvo keeps working, and where it is, with Cancel and Quit. It shows
  once on that device either way, remembered in the app's own folder (`desktop/settings.json`,
  `quitNoteSeen`).

#### The relay, on this Mac's box

The current Mac box's resident process owns paired sessions and peer mail.
It gets its link identity from Kuvo Helper, with no desktop dependency.
See [the resident process](../docs/architecture/one-client-process.md).
The older Mac front below describes compatibility with app-owned installs.

Since bridge 0.9.61 this Mac's box holds its relay connection, as a machine's bridge does (`run`),
in `serve`'s process: your phones pair with it and open their sessions there. Its keys (link key,
relay secret, signing key) stay in the Mac's Keychain: the box asks the app for them
(`link/identity`) once its link is on, keeps them in memory only, and never makes keys of its own;
without them its link stays off and says why. What it keeps of its phones is in `box/run/link.json`,
as on a machine, without the keys, the relay or its name.

**With no app telling it** (#713): Kuvo Code's desktop app says nothing of the link
(`kuvo/link/config` is the retired Mac app's), and a Mac that never ran that app has nothing kept
in `run/mac-link.json`. A Mac's box in a home of its own then starts from its own settings: the
relay everyone's on (`wss://kuvolink.porigam.com.tr`, the retired app's default), this Mac's name
(as System Settings has it, `scutil --get ComputerName`; else its host's), and "Let my devices
connect" on, as a machine's box always has it (so too a Mac moved over from 0.7, which never
kept the switch in its link: your choice, 2026-11-15). Nothing connects until you pair a device or add a
computer. Its keys come from its helper as ever (`link/identity`, made in your Keychain the first
time they're asked for). What an app said before is kept instead, its switch as you left it. The
switch changed on the box itself (Settings › This Mac, `kuvo/settings/computer`'s `devices`: "A
box's settings") is kept there too, marked the box's own (`mac-link.json`'s `own: true`): the
relay and this Mac's name are then worked out again at each start, and only the switch is kept. Adding a computer asks for the keys
whether or not anything else wants the link yet (`kuvo/link/setup`, and the box's own add). A
test's or a demo copy's folder never takes the real relay by itself: only one it's given
(`KUVO_TEST_RELAY`), else none: the box's own relay is for your account's own `~/.kuvo-code` alone. A Linux box has no settings of its own for this: its relay comes
from the Mac that sets it up, or `kuvo-link.js pair <relay>`. Nothing its link meets (the relay gone, a
frame that isn't one, the app away) stops the box's own routes.

What a phone asks, it answers itself, as a machine's bridge does, with the app open or closed:
everything but the Mac's own routes, below (from #191 step 2, `kuvo/info` among them). Before, it
answered only the areas that had moved onto it (a list of them, which the app kept a copy of), and
handed the app the rest: its phones (`kuvo/phones…`), `kuvo/file`, `kuvo/sign-in/return`,
`kuvo/accounts/credentials`, `kuvo/shell/<id>/stop`, the engine's API and the coding agents'
(`api/…`, `kuvo/agents/…`, telling who a message names with `&`; bridge 0.9.64), `kuvo/named`
and `kuvo/groups…` (bridge 0.9.65), and a session's Autopilot (`kuvo/sessions/<id>/autopilot…`)
and move to the coding agents (`kuvo/sessions/<id>/agents`, bridge 0.9.209) were among them. While its
engine starts, or starts again, the engine's routes answer `503 {"message": "This Mac's engine is starting. Try again in a
moment."}` (a machine's say "This machine's"). From 0.9.66, once the app has given up on it (no try
can help; the app's `run/engine-stopped`, why, until it starts or stops it again),
they say "This Mac's engine isn't running." with why, and that Try Again on the Mac starts it (or
from 0.9.201, while it waits for its next try, `run/engine.retry`, that it's trying again); and a
machine's, while its keeper's next start is more than half a minute away (`run/engine.retry`, when,
in seconds since 1970), "This machine's engine keeps stopping. It's started again in about N
minutes." The Mac's own routes (`MAC_APP_ROUTES`, the one list of them: `kuvo/machines…`,
`kuvo/hosts…`, `kuvo/asks…`, `kuvo/mac`, `kuvo/engine/…`), it hands the app
(`link/route`), but `kuvo/engine/restart` while its keeper runs (`run/keeper.json`, its process
alive), which it answers itself (from #341). (`kuvo/claude-code` was one of them before #341: every
box answers it now.) Those it hands the app as it comes, whether its app or its keeper runs the box (the keeper's
host passes on the app's answer as it came, `x-kuvo-answer` with it), `503 {"message"}` at once when
the app isn't answering (of its machines and hosts it says what it can itself then: "Machines").
A box in a home of its own with no app's host registered (`kuvo/box/app`), which is every Mac with
only Kuvo Code's desktop app, has no app to hand them to, and answers all of them itself, as its
own routes: its machines and hosts ("Machines", In a home of its own), `kuvo/asks…` as a
machine's box does (its own browser's), `kuvo/mac`, and `kuvo/engine/restart` (in a home of its
own it always restarts its engine itself, `kuvo-start restart`; `kuvo/engine/start` is a
machine's alone, `404` on any Mac). `MAC_APP_ROUTES` is then only
what the retired Mac app is asked, where there is one.
The app answers those alone, and hands its box everything else it's asked, its own requests
too (`BoxClient`), so a route a box gains needs no list. Mail your
machines send it, it takes itself, as a machine's bridge does ("Peers"): their documents (from
0.9.62), and their agents, letters and group chats' mail (from 0.9.63).
What it asks the app goes through the app's `hello` proof first (the host interface, above), and
the link's keys (`link/identity`) are never asked of a host that hasn't given it. When the app's
host interface starts again (it failed, or Try Again), what the link has open through it ends: a
phone's followed `link/route` streams end (the phone follows again), and a request in the gap is a
`503`. While the keeper runs the box, the record in `run/host.json` is the keeper's alone: the app's
own host interface failing or starting again leaves it, and the app tells the keeper where it
answers now.

For the app only (anyone else gets `403`):

(Once this Mac's box has moved out of the old app's folder, each of these is `410` with words for
the old app: "Computers".)

- `PUT kuvo/link/config {"phones", "machines", "relay", "name", "app"}`: whether the
  phone link is on (`phones`: the one switch people see as "Let my devices connect", which lets
  in every client of yours from outside this Mac, phones and Kuvo Code's desktop app on your other
  computers alike; "the phone link" below is that switch), whether there are machines to meet, the relay (`ws:` or `wss:`), and the Mac's
  name and version as phones are told them. The link is up while the phone link's on with a phone
  paired or a pairing waiting, or there are machines. Its keys are asked for before this answers,
  so a pairing link can be made right after. Answers the link's state. The app says it again each
  time the box starts, and the box keeps what it last said (from #191 step 2; it kept none before) in
  `box/run/mac-link.json` (`0600`): the phone link on or off, the relay, the name and version,
  never its keys nor whether there are machines. A box that starts before the app says it (the
  keeper's, at login with Background Work on, the app closed) takes it from there, with whether
  there are machines from the app's list of them (`box/machines.json`, one that won't read
  counting), so this Mac is back on the relay for your phones and machines before the app opens:
  the phone link turned off stays off, and machines you've removed don't bring it back. Its keys
  come through the keeper's host interface then, which never asks you to unlock your Keychain
  for them (while it's locked, they're refused at once, never with a prompt that would hold up
  the keeper) and reads them again a minute later while it was locked. The app also says it again when the phone link is turned on or
  off while it's open. An older app also sent `features`, what it answered: the box says that
  itself now (`kuvo/info`, its agents' mail), and leaves it.
- `GET kuvo/link/status` → `{"state": "off" | "connecting" | "connected" | "failed", "reason"?}`;
  `GET kuvo/link/status/events` follows it (ndjson).
- `GET kuvo/link/phones` → `{"phones", "removed", "pairing"}`: its phones whole (with where each is),
  every removal, and whether Settings › Phone's pairing link is still waiting;
  `GET kuvo/link/phones/events` follows them.
- `POST kuvo/link/letters/take {"letters": [{id, from, to, text, peer, at, answers?}], "seen": {"<id>":
  <at>}}`: the letters an older Kuvo Code sent itself and had on their way (`agent-letters.json`),
  into the box's outbox, and those it delivered, remembered so one sent again isn't twice
  (`agent-letters-seen.json`).
- `GET kuvo/link/agents` → `{"peers": [{key, id, at, list, features}]}`: the agents each of this
  Mac's machines told it of ("Peers": "Agents"), by its key and its id here.
- `POST kuvo/link/agents/refresh`: this Mac's own agents worked out again, and `box/run/agents.json`
  with them, before a group chat here names someone with `&`.
- `PUT kuvo/link/peers {"peers": [{key, sign, address, name, id}], "moved": [{session, key}]}`
  (bridge 0.9.62): your machines the app set up over SSH that sign their documents, and the
  conversations being moved, for the Mac's peers document. One no longer there is one this Mac
  removed: named in `left`, and mailed the peers document once, while the box still knows where it
  is. `400 {"message"}` for one that isn't a machine's record.
- `GET kuvo/link/setup` → `{"mac", "macSign", "docs"}`: what setting up a machine over SSH gives it
  (this Mac's key, the key its documents are signed with, and its documents, its own as they are
  now and those it keeps of its machines). `POST kuvo/link/docs {"from", "docs"}`: what the
  machine's setup answer gave of documents (`from`, its key), taken as if by mail; `404` for one
  that isn't one of this Mac's machines.
- `GET kuvo/link/documents` → `{"own", "held", "views", "left", "have"}`: this Mac's documents as the
  box keeps them, its own brought up to date first, and its digest, for looking at them (the app
  doesn't read it; the bridge's tests do).

The app's `kuvo/phones/pair` makes a pairing link of its own (Settings › Phone's), apart from one a
phone asks for, so neither ends the other; with the phone link off it's `409 {"message": "“Let my
devices connect” is off on this Mac."}`. The app's `kuvo/phones/remove` removes as the Mac does (any phone,
and the removals a machine's phones document brings).

Its routes are answered there for every client: a phone's through this Mac's link, and the Mac
app's own, which reach every box's routes the same way (`BoxClient`: this Mac's through the app's
`PhoneLink`, which hands all but its own routes on, a machine's through `kuvo-link.js box route`
over SSH). What only the app answers is described below.

### Projects

Each box keeps its own projects, in `box/projects.json` under its folder (`~/.kuvo-code` on a
machine; this Mac's box's own on a Mac), and any client reads and changes them there: the Mac
app's sidebar and Edit Project as a phone does. A project's folder is in the query, as the box
names it (a `/` can't be in a part of the path). A Mac answers from its box; a machine from bridge
0.9.33 (`projects` in `features`). Before, a Mac kept a machine's projects itself, and moves them
there, with the settings of those it removed, the first time the machine answers; what it changes
while a box is away goes there when it's back.

- `GET kuvo/projects`: `{projects: [{directory, name?, folders, run?, removed?, madeBy?,
  addedByBox?}]}`, newest first. It never lists the retired `terminal` field. Reads do not write
  the saved file; the next project edit drops that field. `name` only when it isn't the folder's own; `folders`, the
  project's other folders; `removed`, one Remove Project took off the list, kept with its settings
  for when one of its sessions is brought back (a client shows it then, and not before); `madeBy`,
  the bot that made it ("Work"); `addedByBox`, one the box added itself (a session started in a
  folder it didn't list, `make_project`) whose folders no client has set yet (#341).
  `worktrees` (bridge 0.9.207), `{"<folder>": "<project>"}`: the project each of the box's worktrees
  belongs to, by the folder its sessions run in (and its top folder), for those it keeps, those it
  removed that can come back and those removed before; and each project's git worktrees made
  elsewhere (`git worktree add /tmp/try`; as its repository lists them and they name it back, by
  their real paths, looked for again every 15 seconds or so, off the box's thread; not one that's a
  project of its own; #422). A client files a session whose folder is
  here under that project, never as a project of its own; the events line changes with them. A box
  from before doesn't say: a client goes by `kuvo/worktrees` then.
  Each project's other folders are here too, under it (not one that's a project of its own, nor a
  removed project's), and a worktree of one of them is its too, so a session started there shows
  under the project (#311).
  A session filed under another folder than its own carries it in its metadata from when it's made,
  `kuvo.filed` `{folder, project}` (as the box names them): one a box's `kuvo/sessions` starts in a
  worktree, in a project's other folder or a folder in one, or in the folder its starter is filed
  from; and one a client makes in a worktree it just made with `POST kuvo/worktrees` (it gives it
  itself). A client may hear of the session from its engine before this list names a new worktree,
  and the list never names a subfolder: one whose folder the list doesn't name, still running in the
  folder its `kuvo.filed` names, is filed under that project (#311).
- `PUT kuvo/projects?directory=<folder>` with any of `{name, folders, run, removed}` adds the
  project or changes what's given (an empty string is none). A supplied `terminal` field is
  ignored. It brings a removed one back unless `removed` is true (a client's copy of one it removed, with its settings); one with
  `folders` takes away `addedByBox`: `200 {project}`; 400 for a folder that isn't a whole path. The folder is kept as it's named,
  as its sessions run there (a link isn't followed), and whether it's there now or not (a drive
  that's away).
  Its `folders` reach each of its sessions (`projects.folders`, #341), whichever client changed
  them: on the engine and the coding agents' bridge, in its folder or one of its worktrees, a
  session gets a rule allowing each folder (`external_directory` `<folder>/*`, and where a link
  leads, after its approval's rules; a bot's own folder's rule stays) and the instruction
  `kuvo.project-folders` naming them, or neither once there are none: as it's started or moved
  there, as a client opens it (`POST kuvo/sessions/<id>/folders` → `200 {session}`, 404 for none
  here, 502 where the engine didn't take it: so it has them before you write to it), and as each of
  its runs starts where they changed since (for one nobody opens: a wake-up's, a letter's; that run's
  first step may go without them). Each is
