  written only where they changed, the instruction also where an earlier write lost it (a write
  makes a session the newest). One filed under a project that's the same place by another name
  (`kuvo.filed`, a link) has that project's; one in a project's other folder, none (it works there
  alone). A folder Settings › Permissions names is Settings' to say, as when a session's rules are
  made, by where it really is (a link and where it leads are one folder): the project adds no rule
  for it (no second copy in Auto; a Don't Allow there holds), and an allow a session has for it
  stays only in Auto and Full Access, which allow what Settings asks about, while Settings' last rule
  for it asks; Don't Allows a lead brought from another computer (`kuvo.held`) stay
  last. Only for a project the box lists with folders a client set: a session of one it doesn't
  list (its Mac keeps them, or hasn't handed them over yet), or of one it added itself
  (`addedByBox`), keeps the rules and instruction it has; one moved into one it added gets none. Not a subagent's, nor a hidden run's (a group chat's seat, an engine run, a review's part).
  This operation requires the box route.
- `POST kuvo/sessions/<id>/move` `{directory}` (`sessions.move`, #341) moves a conversation into the
  project at `directory` here, as a chat that turns into work is: the engine moves it (one at work at
  its next step), and it gets that project's other folders as above. `200 {session, directory,
  info?}` (`info`, the session as its engine lists it now); 400 for a folder that isn't here; 404
  for no such conversation; 409 for a coding agent's session (their sessions keep the folder they
  started in), one moving to another computer, and a subagent's or hidden run's; 502 where the engine didn't take it; 503 with no
  engine. This operation requires the box route.
- `DELETE kuvo/projects?directory=<folder>` is Remove Project: every session of it, its worktrees' and
  other folders' too, and those filed under it from elsewhere (`kuvo.filed`) (removed worktrees included, and the folders an optional body `{folders}` names: those a client
  shows under it that the box doesn't know, worktrees removed before it kept them), archived on
  the engine and the coding agents' bridge, older ones included, then it's marked `removed`.
  `200 {archived, sessions}` (`sessions`: the ids it archived, which a client's lists hide at
  once); `409 {message, archived, kept, sessions}` when some couldn't be archived (it stays
  listed); `503 {"message"}` while its engine doesn't answer, the coding agents' bridge running
  or not (nothing is archived).
- `GET kuvo/projects/events`: `application/x-ndjson`, the list now, then again each time it
  changes.

#### Chats

A chat is a conversation of no project: one in the box's chats folder (`kuvo/info`'s `chats`). A
chat's session can carry a mark in its metadata, `kuvo.chat`, naming the folder it's a chat in (as
the session names it: `sessions.chat`, #571), so a client draws it as a chat from the session
itself, wherever it reads it (the engine's or the coding agents' bridge's list, a session read
again as its event comes, `kuvo/search`'s `info`, a session a move brought), not from its folder. A
mark naming another folder than the session's own is no mark: one moved out of the chats while no
box could take its mark off is never kept a chat by it.

The engine (2.2.6) and the coding agents' bridge make a session the newest for any write, its
metadata alone too, so a mark is written only as a session is made, moved or has its metadata
written (each of which made it the newest already), never on a session from before:

- a client gives a chat it makes its mark from the first (`SessionChat.mark`), as a box's
  `kuvo/sessions` does for one it starts;
- the box marks one made without it (by a client from before, or the engine: a chat's subagent), one
  moved (`session.moved`: a chat moved into a project loses it) and one whose metadata a client
  wrote whole without it (`session.metadata.updated`), as their events come;
- a move sets it as it is here as conversations come in ("kuvo/moves"): before they're imported,
  or, with a coding agent, as its bridge places them (`carry/place`'s `chat`) (kept among the chats,
  naming this box's folder; taken off in a bot's folder).

Nothing else writes it: a chat from before the mark that's only written to (a message, a new
title), or one changed while the box wasn't hearing its engine, stays without it. The box decides it
from its own chats folder (the same folder through a link counts too). Their APIs write metadata
whole, with nothing to say "only if it's unchanged": the box reads a session just before it writes
the mark, in its turn, and writes only when it's wrong (see "Session notes" for what can still be
lost). A client keeps the mark as it keeps the rest of
the metadata when it writes it back. A session without the mark (a chat from before, or on a box
from before `sessions.chat`, which marks nothing) goes by its folder, as before (the folder its
box's `kuvo/info` names, kept for when that isn't answered). The desktop reads the marker in `gpui/kuvo_box`.

#### Session notes

A session's metadata (its notes: `kuvo.*` and the rest) is written whole: the engine (2.2.5) and
the coding agents' bridge keep what a `PATCH api/session/<id>` sends as its `metadata` in place of
what was there (`{}` empties it; a key left out goes; a PATCH without `metadata`, a title or its
rules alone, leaves it as it is), with nothing to say "only if it's unchanged". So every writer
reads it, changes what it owns and sends it all back (the bridge keeps its own `kuvoAgent` and
`kuvo.messages` whatever is sent).

The box's own writers (#581: the chat mark, a new conversation's approval and any change to it,
Autopilot, an agent's answers, archiving by a tool or a project's removal, a carry to the coding
agents, the marks of a session it starts and of a bot it makes, a bot's rules repaired) each take
their turn on the session: in their process, and across the box's processes on that computer and
its coding agents' bridge by a lock folder per session in the box's `run/notes` (named for the
session's ID, so the engine's and the bridge's sessions alike). Each reads the session as it is
then, changes only its own keys on it, and writes it straight away. The bridge's writers through
the API (a branch's mark, a handoff's, a group chat seat's) take the same turn. A client's
`PATCH api/session/<id>` that comes through the box (a phone's, another computer's) waits for it
too, so the box doesn't write over it with what it read before (but see below).

A turn's read and its write are each cut short at half a minute, so none lasts more than a minute;
a lock folder older than that (65 seconds) was left by a process cut off: another process takes it
over then, and the box clears those as it starts. Another process waits for a turn's folder that
long at most, then goes ahead without it. While a box from before #581 runs beside a newer one (an
update taking over), the newer one waits for that box's one lock (`run/work/.notes.lock`, held for
its answers and archiving) as it would have, without taking it.

What can still be lost, as long as the engine has no "only if unchanged", is a write that lands
between a writer's read and its write (a few milliseconds), when it's

- a client's that doesn't come through the box: the Mac's app writes a session's metadata whole
  straight to its own engine (archiving or pinning it, say), taking no turn (an iPhone's, and the
  Mac's to another computer, come through that computer's box and wait for the turn, but are whole
  too: below);
- one that doesn't wait as long as a turn can last: a client's PATCH through the box gives up its
  turn after half a minute, its write still on its way, and a process that waited 65 seconds for a
  turn's folder goes ahead without it;
- a session's rules (`permissions`) written alone, outside a turn (a group chat seat's, the
  bridge's for an engine run of its own), against the box's approval writes, which send them whole;
- or a client's whole write made from what it read before the box wrote: the box's change is lost
  (the chat mark is put back as that write's `session.metadata.updated` comes; the box's other
  notes aren't).

A client writes back what it read with only its own change, as late as it can.

### Artifacts

Each box keeps a record of what its agents made: every file a conversation there wrote, edited,
made or showed, with a version for each turn that changed it (`artifacts` in `features`). The
coding agents' bridge keeps it, in `artifacts/` under the box's folder (`~/.kuvo-code/artifacts` on
a machine, `box/artifacts` in this Mac's app folder), and the box passes `kuvo/artifacts…` on to
the bridge as it answers (`503 {"message"}` while it isn't running).

- **What fills it**: the tool calls of every conversation on the engine and the bridge (their
  `metadata.files`, a write's path, the pictures a tool that makes them made, and a picture a read
  brought back, which shows in the conversation, `via: ["read"]`: a screenshot the agent took and
  then looked at, Claude Code's `Read` of a picture; never anything else it only read), Kuvo
  Code's own tools (`show_file`, of any file, and `show_in_panel` mark it shown; `mark_final` pins
  it), and as each turn ends, files it changed that no tool call named (a command's): in a git
  repository as `git status` lists them, elsewhere by a walk of the folder; a bot's folder is also
  watched, so your own edits there count (`by: {kind: "outside"}`). A conversation's bot comes from
  its folder, its `kuvo.bot` metadata or the bots' folders; a group chat seat's bot and chat from
  its `kuvo.seat`; a chat's part, given to a bot's own conversation, is the chat's too (`trigger:
  "group"`); a wake-up's turn is `trigger: "wake"`; a subagent's work counts as its parent's turn.
  The engine's
  conversations run for the bridge's (`kuvo.engineFor`) aren't recorded twice. What the agent's
  browser downloads is that conversation's too (`kind: "download"`, `via: ["download"]`): the box's
  own browser, or this Mac's app for the browser in its panel, tells the bridge (`POST
  /api/kuvo/artifacts/noted {path, session, via: "download"}`, with the bridge's password; not a
  client's route). A download in a page you'd taken over is yours, and isn't recorded.
- **One file, one artifact**: a file is named by its path as the conversation's folder (or the
  bots' folder) spells it, however a tool reached it (through a link to that folder, like a
  worktree opened at `/tmp/…`), so its versions are one artifact's.
- **Versions**: one per turn (more edits in that turn make it `edits` more); changes with no turn
  running, within 5 minutes of each other, are one version. A file the record first sees changed
  has a version 0 (`before: true`), what it was, worked out from the change when it fits the file
  exactly, so the first change can be shown.
- **Copies**: a copy of each version up to 25 MB, by its SHA-256, except:
  - never the bytes of what's likely a secret (`.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_*`, anything under
    `.ssh`, `.gnupg` or a `keys` folder) or what git ignores: `kept: false`, `reason: "secret"` or
    `"ignored"`, its hash keyed so it says nothing of what it holds, and its bytes and changes are
    never sent (`410`). A client may still save or share what git ignores as the file is now,
    from `kuvo/file`, but never what's likely a secret, nor a `reason` it doesn't know
    (KuvoLink's `ArtifactVersion.mayLeave`);
  - code that git keeps: only the change its tool calls made (`reason: "git"`, `patch`), unless
    it's pinned;
  - with the disk's free space under its floor (whichever is less of 10 GB and a tenth of the
    disk), the version a new one replaces keeps no copy (`reason: "low-disk"`).

  The newest version of each file there, and every version of memory, skills and what's pinned,
  stay; older versions of the rest stay while they take no more than the box's budget (1 GB unless
  you set it), the oldest going first (`reason: "cleared"`), each still listed.
- **Pages**: a document that two wake-ups or more rewrote is `living: true`, a page kept up to
  date, as a Shelf shows it with HTML pages.
- **Times** are seconds since 1970.

An artifact:

```json
{"id": "art_<24 hex>", "path": "/…/report.md", "name": "report.md",
 "kind": "memory|skill|image|page|document|download|code|file", "type": "text/markdown",
 "where": {"bots": ["bot_…"], "project": "/…", "sessions": ["ses_…"], "groups": ["grp_…"]},
 "pinned": {"by": "bot|you", "at": 1760000000, "note": "…"} | null, "living": true, "git": true,
 "restorable": true, "gone": 1760000000 | null, "shown": 1760000000, "updated": 1760000000,
 "versions": [Version]}
```

`git`: it's in a git repository; `restorable`: a version of it can be put back (it's in a bot's
folder or the project it was made in), so a client offers Restore only then.

A version: `{n, at, by: {kind: "agent|you|outside", session?, bot?, agent?}, turn?: {session,
message?}, group?: {id}, trigger?: "group|wake", via: ["edit", "write", "shell", "read",
"show_file", "restore", …], status: "added|modified|deleted", edits, lines?: {added, removed}, size,
hash, kept, reason?: "secret|ignored|git|too-big|low-disk|cleared", patch?, before?, handoff?: {from: "bot_…"},
restored?: <n>}`. `turn.message` is the message that started the turn; `handoff`, another bot in
the same chat made the version before; `restored`, it put back version `n`.

- `GET kuvo/artifacts?<scope>[&kind=][&pinned=1][&limit=][&before=]`: `{artifacts: [summary],
  next}`, the scope's pinned ones first, then the latest changed; a summary has `versions` (how
  many) and `latest` (the newest version) in place of the list. The scope is exactly one of
  `session=`, `bot=`, `group=` or `project=` (400 otherwise). Each file is listed once: artifacts
  that are one file by two paths (recorded before it was named one way) list as one, the pinned one
  or else the latest changed. Two files of the same name in different folders are two (a client
  tells them apart by `path`). `next`, an opaque cursor: pass it as `before` for the next page;
  null when there are none.
- `GET kuvo/artifacts/events?<scope>`: `application/x-ndjson`, the list now (the latest 200), then
  again each time it changes.
- `GET kuvo/artifacts/timeline?<scope>[&by=<bot>][&limit=][&before=]`: `{entries: [{artifact, version}],
  next}`, every version made in the scope, newest first, each with its artifact (without its
  versions): in a group chat only what its bots made for it (on their turns, and in their own
  conversations for its parts), for a bot only what it made (and what you changed of its files),
  for a conversation only its turns'; with `by`, only what that bot made (a group chat's one bot).
  `GET kuvo/artifacts/timeline/events?<scope>` follows it, as `events` does the list.
- Over SSH (`kuvo-link.js box route`, a Mac reaching a machine's box), which answers once: a
  followed route (`…/events`) answers with its first line, what it says now, and a client reads it
  again now and then; bytes that aren't text (a picture, a PDF) come as `{"status", "bodyBase64",
  "type"}` in place of `{"status", "body"}`.
- `GET kuvo/artifacts/<id>`: the artifact with all its versions.
- `GET kuvo/artifacts/<id>/versions/<n>`: that version's bytes, with its type; `410 {"message"}`,
  saying why, when it has no copy or was a deletion.
- `GET kuvo/artifacts/<id>/versions/<n>/changes[?from=<m>]`: what changed from the version before
  (or `m`). Prose (memory, Markdown, text, a job) is `{style: "words", lines: [{kind: "same|added|
  removed", text} | {kind: "changed", runs: [{t: " |+|-", text}]} | {kind: "folded", lines}],
  added, removed, from, to}`, the newer version's lines with the words that changed marked, and
  long unchanged stretches folded to a count; code is `{style: "lines", patch, added, removed,
  from, to}` (code git keeps: its turn's patches); pictures and PDFs are `{style: "pair", from,
  to}`, shown side by side from each version's bytes; anything else `{style: "none"}`. `410` for
  what's private.
- `POST kuvo/artifacts/<id>/pin {pinned, note?}`: pinned by you, or not; the artifact. Pinning
  code git keeps keeps a copy of it as it is.
- `POST kuvo/artifacts/<id>/restore {version}`: that version written back to the file, as a
  version by you (`via: ["restore"]`, `restored`); what it replaced is kept first, with a copy, as
  a version by you (`via: ["replaced"]`), so a restore can itself be undone. Only for a file in a
  bot's folder or the project it was made in, and a version with a copy: `409 {"message"}`
  otherwise. Clients ask first, saying what's replaced.
- `GET kuvo/artifacts/storage`: `{copies, older, budget, free, floor, low}` in bytes (`low`: free
  space is under the floor); `POST kuvo/artifacts/storage {budget}` sets the budget for older
  versions (older ones past it go at once), and answers the same; `POST
  kuvo/artifacts/storage/clear {before?}`: older versions' copies cleared (those from before
  `before`, in seconds), `{cleared, …}`.

### Library

Each box keeps a Library: what was handed over to you there, not everything its agents touched
(`library` in `features`). Its services keep it beside the artifact record, in `library/` under the
box's folder (`~/.kuvo-code/library` on a machine), told by the same recorder:

- **What counts**: a file an agent showed in the conversation (`show_file`: a picture, a PDF, a
  page it built; a subagent's counts as its parent conversation's), a picture `generate_image`
  made, and a file you attached to a message (its `file:` address, or what the attached-files note
  names, but not what stayed on the computer it was sent from). Never edits or writes, what
  `show_in_panel` opens, a bot's memory, job or chat recaps, skills, logs, a file on its way, a
  likely secret, or the screenshots an agent takes to check its own work.
- **One item a file** (`lib_<24 hex>`, from its path): handed over again, its time, where and how
  are the latest; one you removed comes back. A page is named by its `<title>` when it has one.
- **Filled once** as a box first has it, from the coding agents' saved conversations (each at its
  message) and, for the engine's, from what the artifact record saw `show_file` show or
  `generate_image` make (at the turn's message).
- **Removing** one hides it (`hidden`): its file stays where it is.
- **Thumbnails**, made on the computer it's on and kept in `library/thumbnails`: on macOS a picture
  made small (`sips`) and a PDF, document or page by Quick Look; on Linux a picture as it is, and
  none for the rest, which a client draws as its kind.

An item: `{id, name, kind: "image|document|page|other", type, how: "shown|generated|attached", path,
bot?, session?, group?, message?, part?, at, hidden?, there, thumbnail, computer: {key, name, here?}}`.
`bot`: whose conversation it was (none: one of your own sessions); `session` (or `group` for a chat),
`message` and `part` say where it was handed over, for a client to show it there; `there`: its file is
on disk, or the artifact record keeps a copy of it; `thumbnail`: one can be made of it. Times are
seconds since 1970.

- `GET kuvo/library[?source=all|you|<bot>][&kind=image|document|page|other][&q=<words>][&hidden=1]`:
  `{items, more, sources: {bots: [{id, name, look?, computer}], you}, computers: [{key, name, here?, state,
  message?}]}`, the newest 1,000 items across your computers, newest first (`more`: there are older
  ones; a search finds them). A bot's `look` is as `kuvo/bots` gives it, to draw it by. `q` matches words in an item's name, its bot's name and its computer's.
  The box asks each of your other computers for its part by mail (an act in the `library` area,
  `GET list {query}`) and labels each item with the computer it's on: `state` is `here` (this one),
  `there`, `away` (not answering now), `older` (its Kuvo Code has no Library yet) or `failed`, with a
  `message` to show. A client shows the computer only when there's more than one.
- `GET kuvo/library/events?…`: `application/x-ndjson`, the Library now, then again as this computer's
  part changes or, asked again every 20 seconds, another's does.
- `GET kuvo/library/<id>[?computer=<key>]`: the item; `…/file`: its bytes, with its type (the record's
  copy once the file is gone; `410` when there's neither); `…/thumbnail`: a PNG, or the picture as it
  is (`404` for none); `POST …/hide {hidden}`: removed from the Library (`hidden: false` puts it back),
  the item. `computer` is the computer it's on (none: this one); another's is asked by mail.

### Settings per box

Each computer keeps its own engine settings and keys; nothing copies them between computers but
you. A machine's are in `~/.kuvo-code/box` (`opencode.json`, and `keys/` for integrations' keys,
which its settings name as `{file:~/.kuvo-code/box/keys/…}`), which its engine reads
(`OPENCODE_CONFIG`) and reloads as they change; no older Kuvo Code writes there. A Mac makes them
the machine's own the first time it connects: what the machine runs with then (the settings an
older Mac's start left, "For released Macs") goes in its box, or, on a machine with none, the
Mac's. From then on a Mac's start sends none of its own, and a machine's settings are changed through its
box's routes, the same way from a Mac and from a phone (`kuvo/config`), one change at a time under
`run/.config.lock`. A Mac reaches any of a machine's routes that answer once (never a stream) over
SSH: `kuvo-link.js box route` takes `{method, path, body?}` on stdin and prints `{status, body}`,
answered as a phone's request is: once (a followed route's first line), and bytes that aren't text
as `{status, bodyBase64, type}`. (`kuvo-link.js box read | change` are the same, for Kuvo Code
0.8.0-beta.1, which uses them; `key` sets one of its keys.) This Mac's own settings are its box's too
("This Mac's box").

What some providers need from the engine until opencode handles it is each box's own too: a
settings file of the box's own beside yours in its engine's settings folder (`opencode/opencode.jsonc`
under the engine's `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`: a machine's `~/.kuvo-code/config`, this Mac's
`KUVO_ENGINE_CONFIG`), never in your settings. opencode reads it with `opencode.json` and reads it
again as it changes, so what the box learns applies to the engine running now, with no restart: a
conversation going on uses it from its next message. (opencode 2.2.6 reads `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`
only as it starts, `POST api/location/reload` stops every terminal and command and drops the
questions waiting on you, `PATCH api/experimental/config` takes only `shell`, and a machine's
`OPENCODE_CONFIG` is your settings.) The file's first line starts `// Kept by Kuvo Code`; one there
without it (yours) is never changed, and the box doesn't apply what it learned then (its log says
so once). A Kuvo Code from before this file never reads or removes it: after a downgrade, delete it
if you sign out of Copilot. An engine started before a box kept it there has the old layer in
`OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` until its next start. Today it's
GitHub Copilot's Claude models named with
`{"compatibility": {"supportsThinkingBlockBinding": false}}` (anomalyco/opencode#55160), only
while the box has a Copilot account: named in an engine's settings with none, Copilot counts as set
up there and its newest model becomes the engine's default, which fails every message left to it.
The model your subagents use (`subagent_model`, `kuvo/config`) is in it too, as `agents.<id>.model`
for the engine's subagents (`general`, `explore`) and your subagents (`mode` `subagent` or `all`,
not turned off) that have no model of their own: read after your settings, it would go over one
that has. None for a coding agent's model, which the engine can't run. With nothing to name,
there's no file.
The box learns them from its own engine: `GET /api/integration/github-copilot` (an account when its
`connections` aren't empty; an answer it can't read leaves what it learned, and it asks again with
the engine's next event: one just started answers 404 for a moment), then `GET /api/model`
(Copilot's models whose id starts `claude-` and that have a `family`; an account whose models
haven't come yet leaves what it learned), as it finds the engine; at once as the engine says an
account was added, removed, signed in to again or switched to (`credential.updated`,
`credential.switched`, `integration.updated`) and as its models change (`model.updated`: an account's come a moment after
its sign-in); every ten minutes at most besides while it's at work; and as a provider's models are
refreshed (`kuvo/accounts/<provider>/refresh`). On a machine, that's while its bridge runs (it has
peers or phones). It keeps what it learned in `run/compatibility.json` too. Whatever starts the
engine asks the box first: `kuvo-link.js engine-config` prints the `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` it's
run with (the sandbox's note added, nothing of the providers', which would hold an old list over the
file until a restart), having brought a machine's integrations up to date (see
`kuvo/integrations`) and, where it's told the engine's settings folder (a machine's start scripts
export its `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`), the file to what the box learned (one an older box learned before it
kept it there). This Mac's app runs it as it starts its engine, after its box, which keeps the file
as it starts; a machine's start scripts do, so an engine started after a restart with no Mac there
reads it too. A box too old to know it starts its engine as before. A Mac sends none.

A machine's engine, its coding agents and its link find programs on the PATH your login shell sets
up there (`~/.local/bin` from your profile, nvm's node from `.bashrc`), not the bare one a start over
SSH or from cron gets: `kuvo-link.js login-path` (bridge 0.9.117) prints it, read from an interactive
login shell, then a login shell only (`$SHELL`; on Linux your account's when that's cron's `/bin/sh`;
none for nushell or csh), followed by the folders of the PATH it was run with; or nothing when neither
answers in time. A machine's start scripts run it once before starting the engine, and it keeps what
it read in `run/login-path`, which the link and the coding agents' bridge go by; the bridge reads it
again only after it installs or updates an agent (a .bashrc that starts an `ssh-agent` when there's
none would leave one running with each read). This Mac's app reads its own shell's for its engine.

### A box's settings

A box describes its own settings (`settings`, #727), so every client (the desktop app, the phone,
a Linux or Windows client later) draws each of them by its kind, in the box's words, and writes
no settings page of its own. Every box answers it alike, a Mac's and a machine's. Each page is made
from the box's existing routes, and each change goes through them as a client of them would
(`kuvo/approval`, `kuvo/sandbox`, `kuvo/sandbox/allowed`, `kuvo/config`, `kuvo/browser/settings`),
so a client still on those (the phone) sees every change kept just as they keep it. Shapes:
`box/src/shared/routes/settings-pages.ts`.

- `GET kuvo/settings`: `{sections}`, in order, each `{id, title, group, icon, line, keywords}`:
  the heading it's under in a sidebar (`group`), its icon by name (the required set every client
  has is `settings`, `shield`, `globe`,
  `user`, `clock`, `sparkle`, `bot`, `terminal`, `link`, `computer`, `branch`, `folder`, `bell`,
  `file`, `message`, `pencil`, `mic`, `sliders`, `drive`, `archive`; one a client hasn't, it draws
  with its own), and the words search finds it by besides its title and line. The box supplies the group: Git and Worktrees are under `Projects`,
  Archived Sessions and Storage under `System`. Today `clock`, `conversations`, `permissions`, `browser`, `computer`, `git`, `worktrees`, `storage`, `archived`, `agents`, `vault`, `mcp`, `commands`, `custom-auto` and `skills`; the rest come page by page.
  `computer`'s title is for who asks: "This Mac" ("This Computer" on Linux) to the app beside its box, the computer's name to any other client.
- `kuvo/settings/conversations` serves the `compaction` choice row, saved by the usual
  revision-checked PATCH. Choice IDs are `200000`, `400000` (default), `600000` and `never`.
  The choice lives on the box running the conversation. Claude Code and Codex keep their native
  margin on smaller windows, and Grok takes a percentage once it reports the model's window.
  `never` disables automatic compaction in a Claude Code process when its main model reports
  at least 900,000 tokens of context. Codex and Grok use their native limits with that choice.
  Antigravity, Cursor and the engine keep their defaults.
- `GET kuvo/settings/<section>`: `{id, title, line?, groups, notes?}`; `404 {message}` for a section
  this box hasn't. A group is `{id, title?, note?, rows}`, a card with its heading and the words
  under it; `notes` are `{words, tone}` (`quiet` or `warning`) after the groups: what couldn't be
  read, said plainly, and what isn't on the page yet. A row is `{id, title, line?, tone?, kind,
  value?, can?, revision, confirm?, busy?}` and its kind's fields:

  | `kind` | Its fields | What a client draws |
  |---|---|---|
  | `switch` | `value`: true or false | A switch |
  | `choice` | `value`: a choice's `id`; `choices: [{id, title, line?}]` | A menu |
  | `text`, `number`, `folder` | `value`, `placeholder?`, `min?`, `max?`, `lines?: {min, max}`, `folder?: {choose, clear, prompt, message}`, `unit?: {name, factor, decimals, rounding: "nearest"}`, `suggestions?: [{value, title}]`, `confirmBelow?: {value, confirm}` | A field (text may request a multi-line editor with its preferred visible line range; presentation only, outside revisions; unit values divide by factor and round to the nearest value with decimals fractional digits (ties away from zero), omitting trailing zeroes beside name; unchanged fields send their original value exactly; numeric suggestions are common values, not limits; a number below confirmBelow.value requires its confirmation, whose button appends the formatted proposed value) (a folder opens the box's picker, `kuvo/folders`, with its own choose/clear button words, picker prompt and message; clearing sends empty text) |
  | `secret` | `set`: whether one is set; never its value | A field written only; Replace and Remove once set |
  | `status` | `value`: words, or a number with `unit?: {name, factor, decimals, rounding: "nearest"}` | The words or formatted file size, on the right |
  | `actions` | `actions` | Buttons (past one, a menu) |
  | `list` | `items`: rows; `add?`: an action; `empty?`: words for none; `search?: {placeholder, empty}` | The rows in its card, or its `empty` words |
  | `meter` | `windows: [{title, used, resets?}]` (`used` 0 to 1, `resets` ms since 1970); or `parts: [{id, title, value, words, parts?}]`, a whole by its parts (`value` its measure, bytes for storage; `words` "1.2 GB"; `parts` what one is made of, `{title, value, words}`), with `actions?` (Refresh) | Usage windows; or the parts as one bar in the client's own colours, a legend of each part's title and words, what each is made of behind a disclosure, and the row's title and actions over it |
  | `open` | `section` (this box's) or `address` | A row with › |
  | `steps` | `start`: an action | A flow the box leads (to come, with Accounts) |
  | `custom` | `name` | What only an installed app draws; any other client shows its `can`'s why |

  How a client lays them out (the desktop app; others alike where it fits): one card per group,
  each row its title and line on the left and its control on the right; a field is saved as you
  press Return or leave it, never with a button of its own (its row's revision still holds: a
  stale change is refused and said); a `text` row with `lines` alone in its group is written full
  width under the group's title and note, its own title not repeated; a group whose one row is a
  `meter` with `parts` is drawn on the page itself, no card; an `open` row is pressed whole.

  List search matches the list title or each item’s title or line, case-insensitively. A matching
  list title keeps every item. With no matches, replace `{query}` in `search.empty` with the typed query.

  `can` is `true` where it can be changed from here, or `{why}`, in words to show beside it (it's
  still drawn, never hidden); a row with nothing to change (a `status`) has none, or `{why}` where
  what it shows is changed elsewhere (a settings file written by hand). An action is
  `{id, title, style?, confirm?, opens?, can?}`: `style` `destructive`; `confirm` `{title, body,
  button}`, asked first in the box's words (a row's own `confirm` is asked before a change to it);
  `opens` an address the client opens itself, sending nothing (an address of the box's own computer,
  its Software Update, is only given to the app beside it, `fromApp`; any other client gets `can:
  {why}` instead); `can` absent where it can be done. `busy` says in words that a change is under
  way there. A box newer than a client may send a kind the client doesn't know: it draws the row's
  title and line, and says a newer Kuvo Code changes it. `revision` is a hash of what the row is
  and what governs whether it can be changed (its value, `can`, its choices' and actions' ids, a
  list's items' revisions; a `secret`'s, whether one is set; whether `can` holds, not its why; action confirmations, so a growing destructive warning makes a reading stale), never its display words: the same value set
  again, a computer renamed or a line reworded leaves it.
- **Things in a list, forms and flows** (`settings.flows`): what a section that's a flow (a list
  of things you add, edit, remove, turn on and off, and sign in to) is described with, so a client
  draws it without knowing what any of them is.
  - A row (mostly a list's item) may say how it stands, beside its title: `badge: {words, tone}`,
    `tone` one of `quiet`, `good`, `busy`, `warning`, `failed` (a dot of that tone and the words);
    and one more line under it, set apart: `notice: {words, tone}` (`quiet` or `warning`, the error
    a server failed with). Neither is part of its `revision`, nor are actions that follow from how
    it stands (Try Again): the engine says them from moment to moment. A `switch` row may have
    `actions` too, drawn before its switch.
  - An action may ask for values first: `form: {title, submit, fields, note?}`, drawn as a sheet
    with the box's title, its fields in order, `note` under them, Cancel and `submit`'s words. A
    field is `{id, title, kind, line?, value?, placeholder?, choices?, mono?, folder?, pairs?,
    shown?, can?, multi?, shows?, secret?, file?, verified?}`; its kinds: `text` (a line), `lines` (several;
    `mono` in a typeface that keeps a command's flags apart), `choice` (a segmented pick of
    `choices`; a client may draw many as a menu), `switch`, `folder` (the box's picker, with its
    `folder` words; clearing it sends empty text), `pairs` (names and values, `pairs: {key, value}`
    its placeholders, its value `[{key, value}]` in order; `secret: true`, its values hidden as
    they're typed), and, with `settings.vault`, `secret` and `file`. A `secret` opens empty (never
    a value: its `placeholder` says "Unchanged" where one is kept, and empty sends nothing new),
    hidden as it's typed (`multi`: several lines, not hidden); `shows: {route, field}` offers Show,
    which reads `GET <route>` of the same box (`{values}`) only when you press it and puts
    `values[field]` in the field, kept only while the sheet is open (the vault's values route, which
    notes it as shown). A `file` is one on the client's own computer, chosen with its `file:
    {choose, none}` words, sent as `{name, data}` (its bytes, base64); it opens with `{name}` where
    one is kept, sent back as it is when none is chosen. A secret's value, a `secret` pairs' values
    and a file's bytes go only with the action itself: a check gets each as `•` once a character (a
    file as `{name, size}`), so the box can say what's missing or short without seeing it, and no
    words the box says hold one. Whatever a section puts there, the box sends no `secret`'s value,
    no `secret` pairs' values, only a `file`'s `name`, and `shows` only for the vault's values
    route (`kuvo/vault/items/<id>/values`); a client reads only that route for Show. A client that
    makes sure it's you (Touch ID, or its computer's password) says so with each settings request
    (`x-kuvo-confirms-you: 1`: the desktop app on a Mac); one that doesn't never reads what a
    secret keeps. `verified` (on an action, or on a `choice`'s choice): it lets something use
    what's yours more (a vault's grant), so a client asks that first, and sends nothing if it
    isn't you. Only a client that says it makes sure is offered such an action or choice; to any
    other it's `can: {why}` ("This needs Touch ID or your Mac’s password. Update Kuvo to do it
    here.") and refused (`403`) if sent. Taking access away asks nothing. (The box can't see the
    check itself, as it can't for `kuvo/vault/grants`: it relies on what a client says of itself,
    so a client that doesn't check is never offered it.) `shown: {field,
    is}` draws it only while that `choice` field is one of `is` (values typed in a field hidden
    meanwhile are kept while the sheet is open, and sent). `can: {why}`: drawn, not changed. The
    values a form opens with are part of its row's revision, and the form has its own (`revision`,
    of those values alone), which its checks and its values are sent with as `was`: a form goes
    stale only when what it shows changed, never because another thing in its list did. A flow's
    state is part of its row's revision, its actions (which differ by who asks) aren't.
  - `POST kuvo/settings/<section>/<row>/<action>/check {was?, values}` → `{fields, ready,
    values?}`: the values checked as they're typed, changing nothing: the box's words under each
    field (`{id, words, tone}`, `tone` `quiet`, `good` or `warning`), whether its button can be
    pressed (`ready`), and values the box fills in (a server's setup pasted into a field), which
    the client puts in its fields. A client asks a moment after typing stops, and as it opens.
    `409 {page}` where the row changed since, `404` for an action with no form.
  - `POST kuvo/settings/<section>/<row>/<action> {was, values}` for an action with a form: the
    page (`200`, the sheet closes), or `400 {message, fields?}` (the sheet stays, each field's
    words under it); without `values`, `400`; `409 {page}` where what it shows changed (the sheet
    stays with what was typed and says so, but isn't sent again: its values are what it opened
    with, and sent from the new revision they'd put back what changed; it's closed and opened
    again).
  - A flow the box leads for a row: `flow: {id, state, title, line, opens?, code?, actions}`,
    `state` `waiting`, `done` or `failed`, with the box's `line` (why, once failed). Started by an
    action (Sign In…), kept by the box (`run/settings-flows.json`, so whichever of its processes
    reads the page states it) and followed by it as the page is read, until it ends; one that ended
    is shown two minutes more. The client that did the action opens `opens` itself, once; any
    other draws its actions, one of which `opens` it. `code: {title, placeholder, action}` where the
    page you finish on ends at an address on the box's computer that the client's browser can't
    reach (offered to every client but the app beside the box): what's pasted is sent as
    `values.code` with `action`, which the client draws beside the field rather than as a button
    of its own. Its other actions (Cancel, Try Again, OK) are done as any other; a list's `add`
    and a flow's actions are a row's actions too.
- `PATCH kuvo/settings/<section> {row, value, was, confirmed?}`: one row changed, `was` its `revision` as read.
  For a row with `confirmBelow`, a numeric value strictly below `confirmBelow.value` requires
  `confirmed: true`, sent only after accepting `confirmBelow.confirm` in the box's words.
  Without it the box returns `400 {message: confirmBelow.confirm.body}` before changing anything.
  At or above the threshold no confirmation is required. Cancel sends nothing.
  The answer is the page again (`200`), or a refusal in the box's words: `400` for a value that
  doesn't fit (a switch's isn't true or false, a choice's isn't one of its choices) or a body without
  `row` or `was`; `403` where `can` says why not (that `why`); `404` for a row not on the page now;
  `409 {message: "It changed since you read it.", page}` where the row changed since (by another
  client, an agent, a route of its own): only that row's revision counts, so a change to one row
  never refuses another's. A refusal of the route underneath passes on with its status and words; a
  `409` without `page` is one of those (a settings file that can't be used), never a stale reading:
  `page` is what marks a stale answer, and its `message` is words to show.
  A box makes one change to a section at a time, each checked against the page as it is then, in
  its long-running process whichever process is asked (`box route` over SSH passes a change on to
  it, as it does Also Allowed; on a machine with none running, reached over SSH alone, the process
  asked makes it).
- `POST kuvo/settings/<section>/<row>/<action> {was}`: what a row (or a list's item) offers, the
  same answers; `400` for one that `opens`, which the client opens itself.
- `GET kuvo/settings/<section>/events`: the page, a line now and one each time it changes (a change
  here, another process's to the files it's made from, and every fifteen seconds for the rest),
  never twice the same.
- Who's asking: the box treats every client alike, but for what opens only on its own computer
  (above), offered only to a request from the app beside its box (`x-kuvo-from: app`, over its own
  server). Nothing in a page depends on which client asks otherwise.

The sections now:

- **Clock** (`clock`): Time zone (`time-zone`, a `choice` of every zone the box's runtime knows by
  its IANA name, titled `Europe › Istanbul`; while it has no zone of yours yet, `own-clock` first,
  its own clock, its value, which writes nothing when picked and isn't offered once one is set).
  A change is a pick of your time zone ("Your time zone"), which your other computers take (not on a
  machine two setups share, whose row says it's for that machine); `400` for a zone the box doesn't
  know. A `carried` zone picked as it is becomes a pick.
- **Permissions** (`permissions`): Approval (`default-mode`, the mode a new conversation starts in,
  a `status`; `full-access`, a `switch` turned off here, asked first, and turned on only in a
  conversation, its `can` saying so; `auto-held-engine`, `auto-held-agents`, why Auto asks first for
  now; `other-computers`, `kuvo/approval`'s `otherComputers`), When the Agent Wants To (`when-<kind>`
  for `edit`, `shell`, `read`, `external_directory`, `webfetch`, `websearch`, `subagent` and `skill`:
  a `choice` of `allow`, `ask` or `deny`, the one that applies with no rule titled `(Default)`: a rule
  for everything at the front of the engine's `permissions` in `kuvo/config`, the rest left as they
  are; picking the default takes that rule away (none is ever written for it, so the engine's own,
  Plan mode not editing, still apply), and picking what applies already writes nothing. A rule of
  yours that says what applies anyway (it holds in Plan mode too) is titled `(Your Rule)`, with
  `default` beside it to take it away),
  Sandbox (`sandbox`: its state, and its button as `kuvo/sandbox` names it, done by the route it
  names: `retry` and `fix` check it again; `restartEngine` restarts the engine, asked first where
  that stops work, on a Mac only while its keeper runs the box, the app restarting it otherwise
  (`can` says so); `help` and `softwareUpdate` open their page), and Also Allowed (`allowed`, a `list` of `allowed-<id>`, each
  with `remove`). Rules for particular commands or files, approvals saved with Always and blocks
  aren't on it yet.
- **This computer** (`computer`, #713): how Kuvo stands on this computer, each row's title saying
  it. No row says "box": the computer is named ("this Mac" to the app beside it, its name to any
  other client). `state` ("Running", or "Not running" as a warning while its engine is down, who keeps it in its line; `restart`, asked first, saying
  whether agents are at work: `kuvo/engine/restart`'s own restart, on a computer you added and on
  a Mac's own box in a home of its own; the retired Mac app's box says to restart it there).
  `version` ("Kuvo Code 1.0.0", or "Kuvo Code 1.0.1 is ready" once `kuvo/update` knows a newer
  one; `update`, titled Check Now or Update Now, is `POST kuvo/update {now: true}`, asked first
  unless nothing is at work; a `status` with no button while updates aren't set up or are held,
  saying why, and while a release the app offered waits for a quiet moment; `busy` while it
  looks for one ("Checking…") or installs it ("Updating…")). `devices` ("Let my devices connect": on a Mac's own box a `switch`, the link's
  `phones` ("The relay, on this Mac's box"), asked first as it's turned off, `409` on a copy with
  no relay, and changed only from the app beside it (`can: {why}` to any other client, which
  would cut itself off); on a computer you added a `status`, always on; on the retired app's box, changed
  there). On a Mac's own box, a second group, What macOS Allows Kuvo Helper
  (`kuvo/box/permissions`' facts, the place to look them up after "Not Now"): `login-items`
  (whether Kuvo Helper is on in Login Items, `launchctl print-disabled`; off, a warning with Open
  Login Items; left out where launchd can't be asked, a copy's home, or its launch agent isn't in place), `allows-<id>` for each
  permission (`Allowed`; not allowed, a warning with Open System Settings, which `opens` the
  address of its list; not known while the helper hasn’t said). For Files the row is
  `allows-fullDiskAccess`. What opens only on that Mac is given to the app beside it alone (`can:
  {why}` elsewhere). A client that has a way to help with a permission added by hand (the desktop
  app's drag tile) matches the address it opens to `kuvo/box/permissions`' `list`. Linux has no
  helper and nothing macOS allows: that group isn't there.
- **Browser** (`browser`): `search-engine` (a `choice`), `tidies` and `offers` (`switch`es), and
  Never Offered (`never`, a `list` of `never-<site>`, each with `offer-again`, which takes that one
  site out and leaves the rest as they are then): `kuvo/browser/settings`,
  the box's browser. How the side panel's own browser keeps its data is each client's.

- **Git** (`git`): a group with no heading (`branch-prefix`, “Branch prefix”), then Commit
  Instructions (`commit-instructions`) and Pull Request Instructions (`pull-request-instructions`),
  each a `text` row with `lines` alone in its group (written full width under the group's title and
  note), all wrapping `kuvo/config`'s `branch_prefix`,
  `commit_instructions` and `pull_request_instructions`. An unset prefix shows `kuvo/`;
  empty text means no prefix. Page writes clean the prefix as git uses it and trim instructions;
  the old config route stays unchanged. Instructions are added when suggesting a commit message or
  writing a pull request. Changes use the existing config route with that field's `was`,
  leaving unrelated fields alone. Unavailable settings say why in `can`. Page events follow
  config changes, including the old Git settings migration route.

- **Worktrees** (`worktrees`): a group with no heading: `worktrees-folder` (“Worktree folder”, its
  placeholder the default folder, `~`-shortened; empty text goes back to it), a project's place
  only where it goes elsewhere or needs you (a folder that can't be made, one inside its
  repository; at most five, then how many more), and `projects-folder` (“New projects folder”);
  then Sessions’ Worktrees (`worktrees`, a list with Remove…, confirmed with the box's words).
  Folder rows accept text; empty clears the choice.
  Project folders wrap `kuvo/work/settings`, worktree folders `kuvo/config`, and removal
  `kuvo/worktrees/remove`. Sources that cannot be read give no rows and a warning.
  Polling each second covers the settings, project and worktree records, engine lists and
  the folders' live git and disk state.
  `PATCH kuvo/work/settings` accepts optional `was: {projectsFolder?, keepsAwake?}` for
  the fields being written, compared under the file's lock; absent `was` keeps its old behavior.
  A mismatch answers `409 {message: "It changed since you read it."}`.
  `POST kuvo/worktrees/remove` accepts optional `was: {record, uncommitted?, ahead?}`, the worktree record and git facts read;
  removals of one root share a turn across box processes and compare the record and git facts before removal. Absent `was`
  keeps its old behavior. A mismatch answers the same 409, mapped to a stale page.

- **Storage** (`storage`): first the computer (its group titled as `computer`'s page is, “What Kuvo
  keeps on this Mac.”): `used`, a `meter` titled “1.2 GB used by Kuvo” with `parts` (`sessions`,
  the engine's data, chats and attachments without worktrees; `worktrees`, the engine's default folder and
  each worktree the box keeps a record of elsewhere, each measured by itself, never a whole folder it's in; `made`, `~/.kuvo-code/artifacts`; `browser`; `other`, the
  rest of Kuvo's folder, its `parts` each of its folders by name), `busy` “Measuring…” while it's
  measured, and `refresh` (measures again; answered at once, the page following). Measured with
  `du` (folders followed where a link points; one taking past ten minutes stopped and said) off the event loop as the page is first read and again once it's an hour old (a failed one too, unless Refresh), kept in
  `run/storage-sizes.json` so every process of the box shows the last one; until the first is in,
  the row has no `parts` and says it's measuring. Storage by Folder: `home-folder` (Kuvo's folder,
  `~`-shortened, its size as a number with `unit`) and `worktree-folder-<n>` (“2 worktrees in”) for each
  folder outside it with recorded worktrees, their size alone; to the app beside a Mac's box, each with Show in Finder (`opens` its
  `file://` address), else a `status`. Then What Agents Made: copies (status in bytes),
  older-budget (number in bytes, with decimal suggestions of 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 5 and 10 GB and confirmation when
  lowering below what older copies take), and older-copies (Clear…, with confirmation); then
  `manage-worktrees` and `manage-archived`, `open` rows to those sections.
  `POST kuvo/artifacts/storage {budget, was?, wasOlder?, confirmed?}` compares optional `was` with the budget
  and `wasOlder` with older copies’ bytes atomically before
  setting it. Every budget write is guarded in the store: below the current older copies’ bytes,
  only boolean `confirmed: true` permits deletion; otherwise `400 {message}` returns the box’s
  confirmation body without changing settings or copies. This applies to both settings and direct
  storage routes. `POST kuvo/artifacts/storage/clear {was?}` compares with older copies' bytes before
  clearing. Mismatches answer `409 {message: "It changed since you read it."}`. Both checks and
  writes run synchronously in the bridge's event loop. Without `was`, revision checking is omitted; the confirmation requirement still applies.
  Page writes floor byte counts as the store does. Polling each second reads the bridge again,
  covering its settings, copies and live disk usage. An unavailable bridge gives no What Agents
  Made rows and a warning; the rest of the page stays. Log and download deletion have no box
  routes and are not included here.

- **Skills** (`skills`, group `Agents & Tools`): Skills the Agent Can Use is a list of authored,
  GitHub-installed and engine-discovered skills, each with a use switch. New Skill and Edit use
  text and multiline fields for its name, when to use it and Markdown instructions; name checks
  and submissions share their words, and editing preserves unknown front matter. Delete confirms
  and moves the whole folder to Recently Deleted; Restore uses the existing trash route. Get
  Skills installs a repository/folder through the reusable skills library route. Repository
  browsing and file previews are reserved for Marketplace (#750). Other Places edits the folders
  and catalog addresses the engine reads. File changes use `kuvo/skills` with optional `was` text;
  settings changes use `kuvo/config` with `was`. Events follow the settings and skill folders.
  Clients draw ordinary lists and forms; no new kind is needed.

- **Commands** (`commands`, group `Agents & Tools`): Your Commands (`your-commands`),
  a `commands` list of `command-<name>` action items, with `add` (New Command…),
  `edit` (Edit…) and `remove` (Delete Command…, confirmed). The forms describe Name,
  Description, Agent (a choice from the engine), Model (a choice from the engine, preserving
  the saved model), Run as a subagent and Prompt. Name checking removes a leading slash,
  replaces spaces with hyphens, and checks existing and engine command names; checking and
  submitting share the same field words. Extra fields stay when editing. Each write uses
  `kuvo/config` with the command's entry as `was`. From Claude Code offers each command's
  existing import through the same route; Also Available lists engine and plugin commands.
  Unreadable settings give no rows and a warning. Events follow settings, Claude Code's
  command folder and the engine's list each second. Clients draw ordinary lists and forms.

- **Custom Auto** (`custom-auto`, group `Models`): named lists of models to try in order,
  described as lists and ordinary forms. New List and Edit ask for a name; Add Model and Change
  the model or its effort offer the models from `kuvo/models/offered` (excluding Auto itself),
  with a single effort field (the add form checks typed efforts against the selected model;
  the edit form initially states that entry’s efforts; checks follow the selected model). Move Up/Down are offered only where a move is
  possible and apply to lists and entries, Remove deletes an entry,
  and Delete List confirms first (the last list cannot be deleted). Changes use the coding
  agents' existing `api/kuvo/auto` routes with their per-list `revision` (order uses `was`);
  their 409 becomes a stale page. Limits are shown beside each held model; Try All Again
  clears them through the existing limits route. An unavailable source has a warning and no
  invented lists. The section follows the agents' state each second. No additional field kind
  or sign-in flow is needed. Permissions' allow/deny rules remain in Permissions.

- **MCP Servers** (`mcp`, group `Agents & Tools`, the first flow section): Servers (`servers`, a
  `list` of `server-<name>`, your servers in the engine's settings' `mcp.servers`: not Kuvo's own
  `kuvo-browser`, nor an integration's, which Integrations keeps). Each a `switch` (on: its
  `disabled` taken away; off: `disabled: true`), its line its command or URL, its `badge` from the
  engine's `api/mcp` (Connected, Connecting…, Needs sign-in, Couldn't connect, Off, Not started;
  none while the engine isn't running, the page's note saying so), its error as a `notice`; its
  actions `sign-in` (Sign In…, while it needs a sign-in the engine names an integration for),
  `try-again` (connected again everywhere its engine runs one), `edit` (Edit…, a form) and
  `remove` (Remove…, asked first). The list's `add` is Add Server…'s form: `name` (a paste of a
  server's setup from a README, Claude Desktop's, Cursor's, VS Code's, opencode's, Zed's or a
  `claude mcp add` line, fills the rest in), `runs` (`local` or `remote`), `command`, `cwd`,
  `environment` (local), `url`, `oauth`, `headers` (remote) and `codemode`; checked for a name
  taken, Kuvo's or an integration's, the command's program on this computer (`kuvo/programs`), and
  a web address (one without a scheme gets https, or http for this computer's own). Each writes
  through `kuvo/config` with the server's settings as read (`was`): what the form doesn't show (a
  timeout of its own, a sign-in set up by hand) stays. A server's sign-in is the engine's
  (`api/integration/<id>/connect/oauth`), led as a `flow`; once done, the server is connected
  again. Its page is kept only as an http(s) address, and a pasted address its page turns down
  is refused in words (`400`). Then the popular servers (`kuvo/mcp/catalog`, not an integration's) in groups by what
  they need (`popular-signIn`, `popular-open`, `popular-local`), each `popular-<id>` with `add`
  (`POST kuvo/mcp/catalog/<id>`'s add) or "Added"; and Timeouts (`timeout-startup`,
  `timeout-catalog`, `timeout-execution`, `number`s at `mcp.timeout`). Its events follow the
  settings file, its flows and the catalog, and read the engine each second. The engine doesn't
  list a server's tools, so the page doesn't either.

- **Agents** (`agents`, group `Agents & Tools`, a flow section without flows): Agents (`agents`, a
  `list` of `agent-<id>`: the engine's built-in Build, Plan, General and Explore, then yours, each
  an object in the engine's settings' `agents`; the hidden `compaction`, `title` and `summary`
  aren't listed and their settings stay). Each a `switch` (off: `disabled: true`), its line how
  it's used (`mode`: A mode, A subagent, A mode and a subagent) and its description's first line
  (Kuvo's words for a built-in one), a built-in one with settings of yours `badge` Changed, and a
  `notice` where its `mode` isn't one the engine takes (it leaves the agent out). Its actions
  `edit` (Edit…, a form), and `reset` (Reset to Built-In…, a built-in one with settings, asked
  first) or `delete` (Delete Agent…, yours, asked first). The list's `add` is New Agent…'s form.
  The form's fields: `name` (New Agent only: letters, digits, spaces, hyphens and underscores,
  one space between words; a name taken by an agent in the settings or the engine's, whatever the
  case, is refused), `mode` (`primary`, `subagent`, `all`; a new one `subagent`), `description`,
  `model` (`""` for none, then the engine's models whose provider is ready, as
  `provider/model`), `on` (Edit only), `system` (its instructions; a built-in one's replace its
  own), a `may-<action>` choice for each kind of action Permissions has (`edit`, `shell`, `read`,
  `external_directory`, `webfetch`, `websearch`, `subagent`, `skill`: the choice marked
  "(Default)" is Settings › Permissions' choice, else how the agent is built, else the engine's;
  picking it writes no rule of the agent's own), and `allowed`, `asks` and `never`: its rules for
  particular commands, files or sites, one a line, "<what it's for>: <pattern>" (what it's for by
  its title, "Run commands", or the engine's name, "shell", either case). A submit writes the
  agent's entry through `kuvo/config` with the entry as read (`was`): the choices first, then the
  rules allowed, asked, never (so Never Allowed wins), and what the form doesn't show (`steps`,
  `temperature`, a value of a kind the form doesn't show, like a `model` object) stays. Permissions
  in another order (a choice after a rule, or a rule allowing after one asking or denying), or that
  aren't a list, are shown as `can: {why}` on the `may-*` and rules fields and kept exactly as they
  are. A name of more than 64 characters, or one every object has (`__proto__`, `toString`), is
  refused. One of yours turned on whose entry has nothing else is kept as `disabled: false`. A built-in one left as it's built in has no
  entry. An agent turned off, made a subagent only, or deleted that `default_agent` names stops
  being it, in the same write. Then From Claude Code (`claude-code`, only while there are any):
  `kuvo/claude-code`'s agents, each `claude-<id>` with `import` (written at `agents.<id>` as a
  subagent with its description and instructions) or "Imported". Its events follow the settings
  file and ~/.claude/agents, and read the engine every ten seconds. With the engine not answering,
  the agents are listed from the settings and the page's note says the models and defaults aren't
  known.

- **Vault** (`vault`, group `Agents & Tools`, `settings.vault`): this computer's vault, read and
  changed through its own routes ("Vault") as the client asking reads them, so only your clients
  see it (anything else gets the page with a note, nothing listed) and the vault's rules, refusals
  and activity are its own. Locked (a machine's, after a restart): a note alone, saying it's
  unlocked with the key it was made with, which a page can't carry and the desktop app doesn't
  keep. Notes for files
  changed outside Kuvo and for agents that can't use it yet. Waiting for You (`asks`, while agents
  wait): each `ask-<id>` an `actions` row, its title "<who> wants to use “<item>”" or "<who> needs
  <need>", its line why and where; `no` (Don't Allow), `once` (Allow Once) and, where Always would
  give it for good, `always` (Always Allow…, asked first, `verified`); an `item` ask has `no` and
  `give` (Give…: `item`, a choice of the items, and `how`, This Once or From Now On, `verified`),
  answered through
  `kuvo/vault/asks/<id>`; one answered elsewhere meanwhile is no longer on the page (`404`), and
  the page followed drops it. Items (`items`, a `list` of
  `item-<id>` by name, its line what it is and its sites, user or file, its `badge` On its own or
  Asks where anyone may use it; searched past six): `edit` (Edit…: `name`, `site` and
  `username` and `password` and `signInOnly` for a sign-in, `hosts` and `value`, `field-<name>`
  for each other kept field, `remove` (one of them to take away) and `more` (`pairs`, secret) for
  an API key, `file` for a file, `text`
  (`multi`) and `readable` for a note; each kept value with `shows`), `who` (Who Can Use It…:
  `bot-<id>` and `project-<folder>` for each one listed, `everyone`, each On Its Own, Asks Each
  Time or No, and `add-bot`, Let a Bot Use It, which asks each time; each choice that lets it be
  used more `verified`, and to a client that doesn't make sure it's you, only what each is now and
  less, checked against the grants as they are when it's saved, all before any is written) and
  `delete` (Delete…, asked first). Edit writes only what changed (a value typed as it's kept, asked with `/same`, isn't).
  The list's `add` is Add Item's form, the same fields with `kind` first and each shown for its
  kind, checked for a name taken, a site, and each value's presence and length; before a machine
  has a vault it can't be pressed here (`can`: the key a new vault makes, which unlocks it after
  its computer restarts, would be lost, as a page can't carry it). Then `pause` (a `switch`, Pause Agents' Use) and `paused-<who>`
  for each bot or conversation paused (`go-on`, Let Go On); and Activity (`activity`, its newest
  50 as `status` rows, each a sentence, the client's own said plainly, a refusal a warning; a
  form's check reads none).
  Its events follow the vault's files, the bots, and, in the process that holds it, what's asked.
  It's for the clients the vault answers (your devices over the relay, the app beside the box): a
  `box route` reads it as anything else on the computer does, with a note and nothing listed.

- **Archived Sessions** (`archived`): archived sessions grouped by project, from
  `kuvo/sessions/list`; each row uses `kuvo/sessions/<id>/actions` verbatim, including
  Unarchive, Delete and the box's confirmation words. Delete All’s confirmation comes from
  `POST kuvo/sessions/deletes`; confirmed deletion calls each existing session DELETE route.
  No session rules are added here. A list may offer `search: {placeholder, empty}` for client-side
  filtering by list title and item title and line (`{query}` in empty is replaced with the query). A missing source gives no rows and a warning.
  Session archive/pin routes accept optional `was: {updated, archived}`; DELETE additionally
  requires the current Delete `confirm: {title, message, label}` in `was`. These are compared
  inside the existing session turn before mutation. Mismatch answers `409 {message:
  "It changed since you read it."}`; absent `was` preserves old calls. Page events poll every
  second, covering session lists, live session actions, moves, worktree confirmations and time zone.

### Your time zone

A time zone you pick, for all your own computers in a setup, which what happens at a time of day
goes by: bots' and conversations' wake-ups, a `/loop`'s time of day, goals' days and ends written
without a zone, a chat's meetings, and the times limits reset.
Until you pick one, each box goes by its own clock, as before. Each box keeps it
(`box/time-zone.json` in its folder: `{kuvo: 1, zone, n, zoneinfo?, carried?, kitSeen?}`), any
client picks it there (`kuvo/settings/clock`, "A box's settings"), and boxes carry a pick to each
other. Every box does it alike, a Mac's and a machine's, on macOS and Linux.

- **A pick**: counted past what the box had and at least the time it's made (milliseconds since
  1970), so a pick made on a box that hasn't heard your others yet (reinstalled, just set up) still
  wins over an older one they have; with the zone's rules where the box has them (`zoneinfo`, a TZif
  file, base64, under 16 KB). The same pick told again with rules, where the receiver has none, keeps
  them (a first mail too big to carry them goes without). Two picks made before either box hears the other are ordered by
  their clocks, so a clock off by some minutes can reorder picks made within those minutes; picking
  again after hearing the other always wins.
- **Carried**: in the agents' mail ("Peers"), beside `agents`, as `zone: {zone, n, zoneinfo?}`, a
  pick only (never a box's own clock, nor what an older Mac gave a machine), to each peer that's one
  of your own computers and has said what it is (as `computer` goes), and on to the rest as each
  takes it. A box takes one counted higher than its own, or at the same count with a name that sorts
  after its own (so every box keeps the same one); not one counted 0, a zone its runtime doesn't
  know, nor a count past 2^52. It keeps the rules sent with it where it has none of its own (a Linux
  machine without tzdata; rules that aren't a TZif file under 16 KB aren't kept). To and from every peer, each one
  of your own computers (#783). A box with no pick takes the first it's told: a computer
  set up later takes yours at its first round with your others.
- **A computer's clock is never your zone**: a Mac's clock moving (you travel) changes nothing on
  your other computers, and nothing of a pick: a Mac's bots go by its clock only while there's no pick
  (it isn't announced). (Whether travel should move your other computers is for later.)
- **Carried from before**, the first time a machine's box reads it with none kept: what its Mac last
  gave it, marked `carried` (count 0: kept and gone by here, never told, and giving way to any pick):
  its kit's `timeZone` and `zoneinfo` (`bots/kit.json`), else the zone above its conversations'
  wake-ups (`wakes/timezone`, `wakes/zoneinfo`), else its launch's `KUVO_TZ` (`run/launch.env`). With
  none of them, none: its own clock (the box never writes its own clock above its conversations'
  wake-ups, where it would be read as yours). A Mac's box carries nothing: it goes by its clock, as
  before. A Mac of 0.7 or before still connecting writes its kit again with its own clock: a
  `timeZone` there other than the one last seen (`kitSeen`) replaces a `carried` zone, for that
  machine alone, as it did; a pick stays, the kit's zone only noted. Picking the zone a `carried` one
  shows makes it a pick. Two machines `carried` with different zones keep each their own until you
  pick one.
- **Where it goes**: each bot's folder and the folder above conversations' own (`wakes`) have the
  `timezone` file `kuvo-wake` reads, and `zoneinfo` (its rules) where the setting has them, each
  written whole, by a rename (the rules before the name; for a moment between, a computer without
  zone files may read the old name with the new rules): as the zone changes, as a bot is made, settled or arrives, and
  each minute while the box runs; not for a bot that's moving, which the box it arrives at settles.
  With no pick: on a machine, its own clock (as before), or its `carried` zone; on a Mac, no file
  (they go by its clock as it changes). What a bot is told says the zone where there's a file, and
  "this Mac's clock" on a Mac without one. The box's own times read the setting, else `KUVO_TZ`, else
  the computer's clock; its coding agents' bridge the setting (from `KUVO_HOME`), else the `timeZone`
  the box gives it with its group chats' settings (`box-settings`), else `KUVO_TZ`, for its chats'
  meetings, limits' resets and its night. A computer without the zone's rules (none of its own, none
  sent) wakes on UTC: the setting's row says so, as a warning.

### Personalities

The personalities you make are one library on every computer: each keeps its copy (a Mac in
its data folder, a machine in `~/.kuvo-code/bots/personalities.json`), and
copies meet box to box (each box's view is a document, "Documents") and as a Mac connects to a
machine or changes one (`kuvo-link.js box personalities`, over SSH). Per personality a removal wins
over any change, and stays noted (`removed`, counted past its last change, or the time it was
removed if that's later; the 500 highest kept), so no copy brings it back; otherwise
the change counted highest: `updated` is when one was made (milliseconds since 1970), and each
change counts on from the one before it, whatever any clock says; at the same count, the words
that sort last. A count past 2^52 isn't taken. Held to `vectors/personalities.json` (KuvoLink's
`PersonalityLibraries`, the bridge's `mergePersonalities`). Kuvo Code's own presets (`preset.…`)
aren't in it. A change that would take the library past what a document holds is refused, `400
{"message"}`, on a Mac as on a machine.

- `GET kuvo/personalities`: `{"personalities": [{id, name, description, symbol, updated}]}`, the
  ones you made, on the computer asked.
- `POST kuvo/personalities` with `{name, description}` makes one (`custom.<uuid>`) and answers
  with it; 400 without both.
- `PATCH kuvo/personalities/<id>` with `{name?, description?}` changes one and answers with it;
  `DELETE` removes it. 404 for one that isn't there, or a preset.
- `GET kuvo/personalities/events` (bridge 0.9.54, feature `personalities.events`): ndjson
  `{"personalities": [...]}`, the same list as `GET`, a line now and one each time the library
  changes: through these routes, a copy met (another box's document, a `take`), or another
  process writing the file (`box personalities` over SSH). Only the ones you made: presets come
  with the kit. 405 for any method but `GET`.

A box keeps the library in its bots' folder: `personalities.json` in `KUVO_BOTS` when it's set
(this Mac's box, the app's bots folder), else `~/.kuvo-code/bots`, as `{"kuvo": 1, "personalities",
"removed"}`. Two routes are the app's own, for the app beside this Mac's box, which signs the
library for your other computers until the box holds the relay connection. They answer only a
request with the header `x-kuvo-from: app` (the app's own over `serve`; the phone link never
sends it for a phone, and the relay and `box route` never carry it), and anything else, a phone's included, gets
`403 {"message": "Only Kuvo Code on this computer can do that."}`:

- `GET kuvo/personalities/document`: the library whole, `{"kuvo": 1, "personalities": [...],
  "removed": [{id, removed}]}`, what the box keeps and signs. 405 for any other method.
- `POST kuvo/personalities/take` with `{"document": {personalities, removed?}}` meets another
  computer's copy with this box's, by the rules above (each entry cleaned as the routes clean it,
  one that isn't a personality left out), and answers `200 {"changed": ["custom.…"]}`: the ids
  whose personality or removal changed here (none when it had nothing new). Their bots here are
  told what they are now, and the box's own document goes to the others, as after a change
  through the routes. `400 {"message"}` when `document` isn't an object with a `personalities`
  list (and `removed`, if there, a list). It's met whole, as a peer's copy is, even when the two
  together are past what a document holds (that library isn't given to the others until it's
  smaller again). 405 for any other method.

A change on one computer reaches the others it reaches by mail at once, and the rest as they
connect. A bot made on a machine can have one there at once: its
`kuvo/bots/templates` lists them, told as the Mac words them (the kit's `personalityWords`).

### Vault

Each box keeps a vault of its own (`vault` in `features`, bridge 0.9.100): sign-ins, keys, files
and notes that its agents use without seeing a value. An agent names an item; the box fills it into
a page (through the browser's own process), a command's environment or a temporary file. No answer
an agent can get holds a value. Each computer keeps only its own; nothing is synced or fetched from
another box.

**Where it's kept.** In `box/vault/` under the box's folder: `items.json` (each item without its
values), `grants.json`, `paused.json` and `activity.jsonl` (kept a year). The first three are
`{"v": 2, "gen", "data", "sig"}`, signed (HMAC-SHA256 of `<file name>\0<gen>\0<data as JSON>`) with
a key no agent can read: a machine's from its store key (so they can't be checked while it's
locked), this Mac's given by its app from the Keychain to the box alone, on its stdin as it starts
(below). `gen` goes up with each write. One that isn't signed with it, was changed, or is older than
the newest the box knows counts for nothing. This Mac's app keeps each file's newest `gen` in the
Keychain, in one item with the file key (host interface `vault/generations {file?, generation?}`
→ `{generations}`), which the box reads before it answers anything of the vault and tells as it
writes: a file there whose generation the app doesn't have counts as changed, and while one it told
couldn't be kept, agents' use waits; a client remembers a machine's
(the state's `generations`) and, seeing one go back, pauses every agent's use there. `paused.json`, made with the first item,
then pauses everyone, and so does its being gone. The state says `tampered`. Values:

- this Mac's are in the Keychain, through its app ("Host interface": `vault/get {"id"}` →
  `{"values"}` or `404`, `vault/set {"id", "values"}`, `vault/delete {"id"}`), never in the box's
  folder. The app gives the box a secret of the vault's (with its own password and the file key)
  on `serve`'s stdin as it starts, `{"password", "hostVaultSecret", "vaultFileKey"}`, never in its
  environment, which any of the user's processes can read (`ps -E`): the password in
  `run/host.json` is in a file an agent's command can read, and rewrite. Before a vault call the
  box asks `hello` with `"vault": true`, and goes on only if the answer's `vaultProof` is that
  secret's HMAC-SHA256 of `kuvo-host-vault\0<nonce>\0<where it reached it>`; each call carries
  `x-kuvo-vault-at` (ms) and `x-kuvo-vault-auth`, the secret's HMAC of
  `kuvo-host-vault-call\0<call>\0<sha256 of its body, hex>\0<at>`, taken within a minute and once
  (`403` otherwise);
- a machine's are in `box/vault/values/<id>`, AES-256-GCM with the store key, which is only ever
  in the memory of the process that holds the vault. `key.json` keeps the store key wrapped by the
  unlock key, and an HMAC that checks one. Only clients keep the unlock key. After the box starts
  again the vault is locked (`423 {"message"}`) until a client sends it.

**The process that holds it.** The box's long-running process (`run` on a machine, `serve` on a
Mac) holds the vault. A `box route` passes `kuvo/vault…` to it over `run/vault.sock` (`0600`, owned
by the user, which the route checks first), one request a connection: `{"hello": <nonce>, "key"}`
(`key`, the box's socket key: the text of `run/socket.key`, `0600`, made by whichever of the box's
processes needs it first; a connection without it gets nothing and is closed), answered
`{"nonce", "proof"?}` (`proof`, while the holder has the unlock key: HMAC-SHA256 with it of
`kuvo-vault-holder\0<the route's nonce>`, base64url); then a line of `{"method", "path", "headers",
"body"}` (base64) there, `{"status", "type", "body"}` back. A request with the unlock key sends, to
a holder that proves it has it, `x-kuvo-vault-auth` instead: HMAC-SHA256 with the key of
`kuvo-vault-client\0<the holder's nonce>\0<METHOD>\0<path>\0<sha256 of the base64 body, base64url>`,
for that request alone. To one whose proof is wrong, nothing (`403`); to one that gives none (a
locked one), the key itself only for `kuvo/vault/unlock`, which a client sends when you ask
(**Unlock** on a machine's Vault page), and `423` for anything else. It says `503 {"message"}` when nothing holds it. A
machine's link keeps running while it has a vault.

**Who may do what.** Clients are your phones (through the relay, by their keys), this Mac's own app
(`x-kuvo-from: app`, on the box's own password, which it was given on its stdin), and a request from
the computer itself (the Mac over SSH, `box route`) that carries the Mac's proof for that request
alone in `x-kuvo-vault-proof`: base64url JSON `{mac, at, nonce, proof}`, its signing key's signature
of `kuvo-vault-request\0<the machine's id>\0<at>\0<nonce>\0<METHOD>\0<path>\0<sha256 of the body,
hex>`, within five minutes, each nonce once (`box route` takes the body as sent, `bodyText`, for
it). The unlock key goes only to unlock (`x-kuvo-vault-key`, or `kuvo/vault/unlock`), when you ask:
what runs as you on a machine (its `bin/kuvo-link.js`, its engine) could take it on its way then. Anything else
(an agent's command) gets `403 {"message"}` from every route but the agents' own two and `unlock`.

- `POST kuvo/vault/key` → `{"key"}`, the unlock key (32 bytes, base64url), for a client to keep:
  answered to a phone, this Mac's app, or the Mac over SSH proving it set the machine up:
  `{"mac", "at", "nonce", "proof"}`, its link key, the time (ms), a nonce (16 to 64 base64url
  characters) and its signing key's (link.json's `macSigns`) Ed25519 signature of
  `kuvo-vault-key\0<the machine's id on its Macs>\0<at>\0<nonce>` (link.json's `id`), within five
  minutes, each nonce once. It makes the vault
  if there isn't one yet. `409` on this Mac (its Keychain needs no key), `423` while locked.
- `POST kuvo/vault/unlock {"key"}` → the state; `403` for a key that isn't this vault's. Before
  there's a vault, the state (`made: false`) whatever the key, so a client can tell whether to fetch
  one without making it.
- `GET kuvo/vault` → `{state, items, grants}`. `state` is `{made, locked, paused, pausedBots:
  {<bot on this computer, or a conversation that isn't a bot's>: why}, store: "keychain" | "encrypted", keptDays,
  agents, agentsWaiting?, tampered?, generations: {items, grants, paused}}` (`agents`: whether agents may use it
  on this box, below; `agentsWaiting`: its sandbox is on, and they may once the coding agents
  started before it came on have finished, which clients say as “Locked for now: some agents started before the sandbox was on. The vault opens when they finish.”); an item is `{id, kind: "login" |
